raw_json_ld.title: Academic Cardiologist - Expertise in Cardiac Imaging & Artificial Intelligence
raw_json_ld.description: Academic Cardiologist with Expertise in Cardiac Imaging & Artificial Intelligence Position Description The Department of Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences at McMaster University and St. Joseph’s Healthcare invite applications for an Academic Cardiologist with subspecialty expertise in multimodality cardiac imaging (cardiovascular CT and echocardiography) and an established record of accomplishment in artificial intelligence applied to cardiovascular imaging. Research, Innovation & AI Scholarship The successful candidate is expected to focus approximately 40% of their time on research developing, validating, and implementing AI algorithms and software for cardiovascular imaging. The candidate will have experience or formal training in AI and software development sufficient to lead an independent research program in this area. A key focus will be to develop and validate software tools (deep learning, statistical shape modelling, computational hemodynamics) for coronary CTA interpretation and TAVR CT procedural risk stratification. The candidate is expected to publish in peer-reviewed journals, present at major scientific meetings, pursue external grant funding, and engage McMaster’s AI / data-science ecosystem. Educational Responsibilities The candidate will supervise cardiology fellows and residents and provide clinical and research mentorship in cardiac CT and clinical AI/computational research methods. The candidate is expected to collaborate with the McMaster Biodesign group in education of students and supervision of student projects. The candidate will contribute to divisional academic half-day, structural-imaging rounds, and curriculum delivery for the Cardiovascular CT related fellowship programs. Clinical Responsibilities The candidate’s clinical time will be spent on cardiac CT, general cardiology outpatient and inpatient cardiology service, and echocardiography. The candidate will be responsible for Independently reporting cardiovascular CT studies, transthoracic echocardiograms and transesophageal echocardiograms. The candidate will participate in the on-call rotation to provide general cardiology coverage across outpatient clinics, CCU, and inpatient consult service. Required Qualifications MD or equivalent. Applicants should be certified (or eligible for certification) by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and must be licensed (or eligible for licensure) in the Province of Ontario. Subspecialty fellowship training in Cardiovascular CT with focus on coronary imaging and TAVR planning studies. Demonstrated independent track record in clinical AI and software development for cardiovascular imaging or intervention, evidenced by deployed applications, patents, or peer-reviewed publications. This is a full-time faculty position for a period of three years (renewable). Academic rank will be commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will be a full-time member of the Division of Cardiology and will be expected to contribute to the academic mission of the Faculty and Division. Please apply online to Job Opening 78555 via the McMaster Academic Careers website ( http://www.workingatmcmaster.ca/careers/ ) directing your application to: Sara Sellers Academic and Administrative Manager Expressions of interest should include: An up-to-date curriculum vitae and cover letter. A written description of training and research experience (two-page maximum). Applicants are encouraged to describe any impact that career interruptions have had on research, academic, and/or clinical scholarly productivity, if applicable. A brief statement describing any contributions made or planned in relation to advancing equity, diversity and inclusion, or inclusive excellence in teaching, research, or service within higher education, community-based, or other professional settings (two-page maximum). The names and addresses of three professional referees, including one current or recent supervisor. Letters of reference are not required and will not be reviewed at the application stage; letters of recommendation from referees will be requested at later stages of the search process. All qualified applicants are encouraged apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be considered first for this position. To comply with the Government of Canada’s reporting requirements, the University is obliged to gather information about applicants’ status as either Permanent Residents of Canada or Canadian citizens. Applicants need not identify their country of origin or current citizenship; however, all applications must include one of the following statements: “Yes, I am a citizen or permanent resident of Canada” or “No, I am not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada” Pay Transparency Statement Compensation for Clinical Faculty is derived from multiple sources and varies based on clinical activity, speciality, and practice arrangements. Compensation may include a combination of university-based salary, stipends, hospital or partner organization funding, and earnings through clinical practice plans. How To Apply To apply for this job, please submit your application online. Employment Equity Statement McMaster University is located on the traditional territories of the Haudenosaunee and Mississauga Nations and within the lands protected by the “Dish With One Spoon” wampum agreement. The diversity of our workforce is at the core of our innovation and creativity and strengthens our research and teaching excellence. In keeping with its Statement on Building an Inclusive Community with a Shared Purpose, McMaster University strives to embody the values of respect, collaboration and diversity, and has a strong commitment to employment equity. The University seeks qualified candidates who share our commitment to equity and inclusion, who will contribute to the diversification of ideas and perspectives, and especially welcomes applications from indigenous (First Nations, Métis or Inuit) peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+. jobs.title: Radiologist - Diagnostic Imaging
jobs.full_description_text: RADIOLOGIST Flexible Full-Time, Part-Time & Selected-Day Opportunities Monday-Friday rotations | No weekends or holidays | Flexible start date Build a practice that works with your life. Wentworth-Halton X-Ray & Ultrasound (WHXR) is seeking RCPSC-certified Radiologists, fully licensed to practise in Ontario, to join our established outpatient diagnostic imaging practice serving Hamilton and surrounding communities. Whether you are looking for a full-time role, a part-time commitment or coverage on selected days, WHXR offers a flexible, well-supported environment designed to let radiologists focus on efficient, accurate and high-quality reads. Why Join WHXR · No weekend or holiday coverage - Monday-Friday rotations only · Flexible commitment - full-time, part-time and selected-day coverage available · Flexible start date · Established practice with 12 facilities and more than 50 years serving the community · State-of-the-art digital imaging with voice recognition or transcription support · Pre-filled ultrasound reports and highly automated BMD reporting · Optional standalone breast-imaging rotation About the Practice Established in 1972, WHXR is a trusted network of 12 independent health facilities owned and operated by radiologists from Hamilton General Hospital. Our team of more than 100 skilled health professionals performs close to 1,000 diagnostic imaging examinations each day across X-ray, ultrasound, bone mineral density and mammography. The Opportunity · General rotation includes routine X-ray, BMD and ultrasound, excluding specialty MSK ultrasound · Optional standalone breast-imaging rotation includes mammography and breast ultrasound · Cases are read from 12:00 p.m. the previous day to 12:00 p.m. the current day · Stat cases are covered until 4:00 p.m. on a specific rotation (all other rotations have only routine work). · Typical daily volume is approximately 200 X-ray, ultrasound and BMD studies Qualifications · RCPSC certification in Diagnostic Radiology · Full licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) · A strong commitment to quality, accuracy and patient-focused care · Experience in high-volume outpatient imaging is an asset Interested in Learning More? We welcome a confidential conversation about how this opportunity could fit your preferred schedule and practice interests. Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter to: Dr. Danielle Walker, CEO Wentworth-Halton X-Ray & Ultrasound danielle.walker@medportal.ca

jobs.title: Family Physician (FHO)
jobs.full_description_text: About Us Danton Medical Centre is a modern, physician-owned healthcare facility located in the growing community of Oakville, Ontario. Our clinic serves a diverse patient population, including young families, working professionals, and older adults. Located in a newly developed residential area with limited access to nearby family physicians, the clinic continues to experience strong demand for primary care services.Position Overview We are seeking a dedicated and compassionate Family Physician to join our established team. This is a unique opportunity to replace a departing physician and take over an existing practice providing the incoming physician with an established patient panel from the beginning. In addition, the clinic has a substantial and growing waitlist of patients actively seeking a family doctor, offering the opportunity to expand the practice quickly based on the physician’s preferred capacity. The ideal candidate will be committed to providing comprehensive, patient-centred care to patients of all ages and will enjoy working within a supportive, collaborative clinic environment.Key Responsibilities Provide comprehensive primary care services, including preventive care and the diagnosis and management of acute and chronic medical conditions. Assume care of an established patient roster Accept additional patients from the clinic’s existing waitlist based on the physician’s preferred practice size and availability. Establish and maintain strong physician-patient relationships based on trust, respect, and empathy. Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals to support coordinated and integrated patient care. Use the clinic’s electronic medical record system for efficient clinical documentation and communication. Participate in quality-improvement initiatives and continuing medical education activities. Participate in rotating after-hours or same-day clinic coverage, where applicable, to support patient access and provide additional income opportunities. Benefits An established patient practice No cost to transfer patient roster. Competitive shared-overhead arrangement. Modern, fully equipped, paperless clinical workspace. Administrative support for appointment scheduling and other non-clinical responsibilities. On-site blood laboratory. Join an established FHO group operating for more than 15 years. Supportive and collaborative physician-owned clinic environment. Excellent opportunity to establish a busy and successful family medicine practice without starting from zero. Qualifications Licensed to practise medicine in Ontario and in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Excellent clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary healthcare environment. Commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. How to Apply Physicians interested in joining Danton Medical Centre are invited to submit a brief résumé or expression of interest to doctors@danton.ca, indicating their interest in the Family Physician position. We welcome inquiries from physicians seeking an established practice, a supportive clinical environment, and the opportunity to serve a growing Oakville community.

jobs.title: Family Medicine Physician - Burlington Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Executive Health Physician Location: Medpoint Health Care Centre – Burlington, Ontario Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time Reports to: Medical Director About Medpoint Health Care Centre: Medpoint is a leading provider of preventive and executive health services in Southwestern Ontario. We offer comprehensive medical assessments, diagnostics, and wellness programs tailored for busy professionals and executives who prioritize health, performance, and longevity. Position Overview: The Executive Health Physician is a key member of the Medpoint medical team, responsible for delivering high-quality, client-focused health assessments for corporate and individual executive clients. The physician will lead comprehensive medical evaluations and provide actionable, preventive health advice to help clients achieve optimal well-being. Key Responsibilities: Conduct comprehensive executive medical assessments , including detailed medical history, physical examinations, and interpretation of diagnostic tests. Review and evaluate lab work, imaging, cardiovascular testing, and other diagnostics with a focus on preventive and lifestyle medicine . Provide clear, personalized medical recommendations and health optimization plans for each client. Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of specialists (nutritionists, kinesiologists, mental health providers) to deliver holistic care. Engage in regular follow-up consultations , ensuring continuity of care and progress monitoring. Contribute to continuous improvement in clinical programs and services within the Executive Health Department. Stay current with the latest in preventive medicine, executive health trends, and best practices. Qualifications: Medical degree (MD or equivalent) and licensed to practice in Ontario. Certification from the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CCFP) or equivalent. Experience in executive, preventive, or occupational medicine is strongly preferred. Exceptional interpersonal, communication, and bedside manner skills. Strong clinical judgment and ability to work autonomously within a team-based environment. Passion for wellness, prevention, and improving the lives of professionals. Why Join Medpoint? Be part of a growing, innovative healthcare organization that is transforming preventive medicine in Canada. Access to state-of-the-art diagnostic equipment and comprehensive medical support staff. Flexible scheduling and work-life balance in a non-acute setting. Competitive compensation, CME support, and opportunities for career growth.

jobs.title: Family Physician for Walk-In Clinic, Family Practice, Locum coverage
jobs.full_description_text: North Burlington Medical Centre (NBMC) - physician owned and serving Burlington and surrounding communities since 1992 - now has several opportunities for family physicians looking to work in an established family health group practice. These opportunities include - all options: 1. Walk-In Clinic shifts - mostly in person with occasional telephone visits (i.e. follow-up test results) 2. Family Practice - part-time 3. Locum coverage for our 13 family docs 4. Hospital work - including hospitalist coverage 5. Nursing Home opportunities when available 6. Hospice care 7. House calls 8. Teaching medical students and residents from McMaster University This an opportunity for a new (or recent) grad to join an existing, well-established Family Health Group (FHG) with collegial colleagues who share time off vacation coverage. With the Walk-In (WI) Clinic component of our practice, previous new docs have had no trouble building a busy family practice within a few months by meeting unattached patients in the walk-in clinic. Our WI Clinic typically sees 150-200 patients per day (busy days 250+ patients in 12 hours). We pride ourselves on our "patient's first" approach. Most of our WI docs are also family docs in the community (at our location or at other practices around town). Many docs have been with us for 15-20 years or more. Our WI Clinic is open 365 days a year so the community knows we are available - it helps that we have a rota of 25-30 docs to fill shifts, so we all get time off. We have full nursing, billing, and receptionist support and use Telus Practice Solutions (PS Suite) EMR. We have access to blood work (LifeLabs), basic imaging (Halton X-Ray and Ultrasound) in the building as well as equipment for simple procedures (e.g. suturing, LN2, ear syringing, FB removal, etc). Our RNs, RPNs and MOAs are trained to do strep, COVID, and urine testing as needed. Docs at NBMC bill extremely well due to enhanced fee for service for FHG rostered patients including 30% after hours premiums above existing OHIP fees. As there are still no individual caps on physician billing in Ontario, docs in our group can earn as much as they choose - depending on how many shifts they wish to do. Our WI clinic shifts are typically 4 hours long and docs typically take home $150-$250/hr - after overhead. Take home pay range for our WI Clinic docs is $200-$500/hr - again this is after overhead paid to group. I would be pleased to meet and give anyone interested to learn more a tour and discuss overhead splits in person. It would be my pleasure to help a new grad transition from residency to practice. Harpal Singh, MDCM, CCFP, FCFP Lead Physician, North Burlington Medical Centre Family Health Group 1960 Appleby Line, Suite 18 Burlington, ON L7L 0B7 (905) 319-2000 harpalemail@gmail.com Clinical Assistant Professor, Department of Family Medicine McMaster University School of Medicine Attending Physician, Joseph Brant Hospital, Burlington Attending Physician, Age Care Brant LTC, Burlington Attending Physician and Medical Director, Queens Garden LTC, Hamilton Attending Physician and Medical Director, Wellington Park Care Centre LTC, Burlington Attending Physician, Cawthra Gardens LTC Co-Chair, Steering Committee, Burlington Ontario Health Team (OHT) 2019-2024 Executive Committee, Burlington Primary Care Network

jobs.title: Headache and Interventional Pain Physician
jobs.full_description_text: Practice Overview The Headache, Migraine & Concussion Centre (HMCC) is an established, community-based specialty clinic serving patients throughout Durham Region and the Greater Toronto Area. Our practice focuses on compassionate, evidence-based and non-narcotic care for people living with chronic migraine, headache disorders, concussion-related headaches and selected chronic pain conditions. Many of our patients come to HMCC after months or years of persistent symptoms and difficulty accessing specialized care. The Opportunity We are seeking a physician with established experience in headache medicine, chronic pain management and related interventional procedures. We welcome applications from: Neurologists and headache medicine specialists Anesthesiologists with chronic pain experience Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation physicians Family physicians with formal training and an established focused practice in headache or chronic pain medicine Qualified US-based physicians interested in relocating to Ontario This flexible opportunity can begin with one clinical day per week , with the option to increase to two or three days as desired. Clinical Focus Ideal candidates will have in-depth knowledge in the management, diagnosis, and treatment of complex headache and facial pain disorders, including performing interventional procedures, participating in interdisciplinary care and research. Chronic migraine and complex headache disorders Therapeutic toxin injections for migraine and dystonia Longitudinal specialty care and treatment optimization Position Highlights Outpatient-focused position No call requirement Dedicated headache clinic with access to infusion therapies and neuromodulation treatments Collaborative team of advanced practice providers and pain specialists Qualifications Applicants must: Hold an MD, DO or equivalent medical degree Be registered with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO), or be eligible to apply for Ontario registration Hold appropriate specialty certification, focused-practice credentials or equivalent documented training and experience Demonstrate current competence in the assessment and management of headache or chronic pain conditions Demonstrate existing training and competency for any interventional procedures they intend to perform Be committed to compassionate, patient-centred and evidence-based care Work collaboratively with physicians, nurses, administrative staff and referring providers Headache medicine fellowship training or equivalent clinical experience is preferred. Experience administering Botox for chronic migraine and performing peripheral nerve blocks is a strong asset. US-Trained Physicians HMCC welcomes confidential discussions with US-based physicians interested in practising in Ontario. Physicians certified by an American Board of Medical Specialties member board may be eligible for a streamlined CPSO registration pathway. Eligibility and approved scope are determined individually by CPSO. Candidates must also satisfy applicable Canadian work authorization requirements. Practice Location HMCC is located in Ajax, Ontario, approximately 35 kilometres east of downtown Toronto. Ajax provides access to the Greater Toronto Area while offering a growing community, waterfront trails and a more manageable cost of living than central Toronto.

jobs.full_description_text: EMERGENCY MEDICINE OPPORTUNITIES at Lakeridge Health Ajax-Pickering, Bowmanville, Port Perry or Oshawa We are currently inviting applications for permanent full and part-time Emergency Medicine Physicians to join a congenial team providing care in Durham Region with hospital privileges at Lakeridge Health sites including Ajax, Bowmanville, Oshawa and Port Perry. While one of these hospitals will be your "primary" locations, you may be required to work at our other hospital sites. Physicians enjoy flexible scheduling and extensive specialty and subspecialty consultation services. These emergency departments range in volume from a small community ED, to a moderate sized ED, to a large, very high volume urban ED. There is a dedicated ED education team providing ongoing quality Continuing Medical Education. Remuneration is based on a fee-for-service billing system (Oshawa) and AFA (Ajax-Pickering, Bowmanville and Port Perry). The anticipated compensation range is $350,000 - $500,000. You will have teaching opportunities through the Lakeridge Health partnership with Queen’s University, for those interested and qualified. Lakeridge Health offers many administrative options for those interested in pursuing physician leadership positions. The candidate must hold FRCPC certification with the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or CCFP(EM) certification in Emergency Medicine or significant experience appropriate to the ED and be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Language of work: English. The position start date is negotiable. About Lakeridge Health With five hospitals, four emergency departments, three critical care units, a long-term care home, a full range of medical and surgical specialties, more than 20 community health-care locations and a state-of-the-art surgical centre within the Jerry Coughlan Health & Wellness Centre, Lakeridge Health offers some of the broadest and most comprehensive acute care, ambulatory care, and long-term care services in Ontario. Lakeridge Health is also home to several regional specialty centres and services, including the Central East Regional Cancer Program, R.S. McLaughlin Durham Regional Cancer Centre, The Shoulder Centre, and eye care and chronic kidney disease services. Additionally, we are proud to serve our community with a full suite of inpatient, ambulatory, and community-based mental health and addictions services, and provide safe, high-quality, compassionate care in our state-of-the-art long-term care home, Lakeridge Gardens. Lakeridge Health is redefining the future of health care through transformative research, dynamic academic partnerships, and groundbreaking clinical trials. With over 140 active studies, we’re at the forefront of advancing medical knowledge, expanding treatment options, and improving the lives of our patients. Our one-of-a-kind Queen's-Lakeridge Health MD Family Medicine Program is at the forefront of training the next generation of primary care doctors. Each year, over 3,000 students and trainees are supported by the Lakeridge Health Education and Research Network (LHEARN). Through our innovative collaboration with Ontario Tech University, we’re also harnessing the power of Artificial Intelligence to revolutionize patient care. Together with our academic, community, and industry partners, Lakeridge Health is tackling the toughest health challenges and elevating the quality of care for the communities we serve. Guided by our vision of One System. Together, we are focused on empowering people to live their best health and fostering an accessible, inclusive, and equitable environment for all. jobs.full_description_text: Family Physician – Walk-In & Family Practice Location: Whitby, Ontario Position: Part-Time / Flexible Compensation: Fee-for-Service (FFS) We are seeking a Family Physician to join our established medical clinic in Whitby. This is a flexible opportunity for a physician looking to combine walk-in clinic coverage with family practice . The physician can provide walk-in coverage on a few select days each week, as well as provide coverage when other physicians are away. On the remaining days, there is an opportunity to build and manage your own family practice . Position Highlights Flexible scheduling based on your availability Regular walk-in clinic shifts on select days Opportunity to cover walk-in shifts when other physicians are away Ability to build your own family practice and patient roster Established clinic with existing patient volume and infrastructure Supportive clinic staff and administrative support Opportunity to increase your family practice workload over time Compensation The position is offered on a Fee-for-Service (FFS) basis . The physician bills OHIP directly for services provided and receives the associated billings. An agreed portion of the billings is then paid to the clinic for the use of the facility, infrastructure, and administrative support. To help support a new physician during the transition and start-up period, the clinic will waive its portion of the billings for the first month. This allows the physician to get established and build their practice without an initial clinic fee. Responsibilities Provide comprehensive primary care to walk-in and family practice patients Assess and manage acute and chronic medical conditions Provide appropriate follow-up and continuity of care Maintain accurate and timely medical documentation Work collaboratively with clinic physicians and staff Provide coverage for other physicians when required Requirements Licensed to practise medicine in Ontario CPSO registration in good standing Eligible to bill OHIP Family Medicine certification or equivalent Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills Commitment to high-quality, patient-centred care A Flexible Opportunity Whether you are looking to supplement an existing practice, establish a new family practice, or combine family practice with regular walk-in coverage , this position offers the flexibility to structure your schedule around your professional goals. Interested physicians are invited to contact us to discuss the opportunity, availability, and practice arrangement.

jobs.full_description_text: MedCare Clinics @ Walmart Oshawa – Primary Care (GP) / Walk-in Physician MedCare Clinics is seeking full-time or part-time Physicians to join our team at our Oshawa location. Physicians may provide walk-in clinic coverage (FFS) or join our existing Family Health Group (FHG). Why Join MedCare Clinics? Flexible Scheduling: Shifts are available during weekdays, evenings, and weekends with no on-call or mandatory hour requirements, offering excellent work-life balance. Collaborative Team: Work alongside a supportive network of Family Physicians, NPs, nurses, MOAs, pharmacists, and clinical assistants/scribes. Continuous Patient Care: Multiple physicians per location ensure seamless patient coverage during vacations or leave. Modern Facilities: On-site blood draw lab, triaged patient flow, sanitized equipment, and trained staff for immunizations and phlebotomy. Specialist Access: Established referral pathways to Allergy & Immunology, Cardiology, Dermatology, Pediatrics, and Diagnostic Imaging. High Patient Volume: Serve a diverse patient population in a busy, modern clinic with free parking and easy accessibility. Technology & Support: Accuro EMR and full billing support. Compensation & Benefits: Competitive, low income split with full transparency (no hidden overhead). Guaranteed minimum monthly salary for full-time or FHG physicians (income stabilization). Comprehensive Health & Dental benefits package for full-time physicians and their families. Opportunity to work across multiple sites. jobs.title: Family Physician Wanted — Below-Market Overhead, Overhead-Free Ramp-Up
jobs.full_description_text: ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY An established, independently owned community pharmacy in Oshawa, Ontario is seeking a Family Physician or General Practitioner to practice within our pharmacy space. This is a unique opportunity to build or expand your practice in one of Durham Region's most underserved communities, with immediate access to a large population of unattached patients actively looking for a family doctor. We have the space. We have the patients. We need the right physician. --- WHAT WE OFFER - Dedicated, fully equipped examination room within an established, busy community pharmacy - Below-market overhead rate — our pharmacy co-location model means we don't need to charge clinic-standard rates - On-site pharmacy for seamless patient care and prescription fulfillment - Administrative and reception support - EMR access - Flexible scheduling — full-time or part-time arrangements considered - Possible overhead-free period during ramp-up for the right candidate - Walk-in, rostered, or hybrid practice model — your preference - Ample free parking and accessible location --- WHY OSHAWA? Durham Region has one of the highest concentrations of unattached patients in Ontario. A physician joining our practice can expect to build a full patient roster quickly, with strong walk-in demand from day one. This is a community that genuinely needs you — and a setup designed to let you hit the ground running. --- IDEAL CANDIDATE - Licensed with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) - Eligible to bill OHIP on a fee-for-service basis - Interest in community-based primary care - Family medicine or general practice background - New graduates, established physicians looking for a fresh start, and internationally trained physicians with active CPSO registration are all welcome to apply --- COMPENSATION Fee-for-service model. You bill OHIP directly and retain the majority of your billings. Overhead is structured competitively below standard clinic rates, reflecting the mutual benefit of our pharmacy partnership model. Possible overhead-free period during initial ramp-up for the right candidate.

jobs.title: FHO Locum Physician -Oshawa - Illness Coverage
jobs.full_description_text: 6-Month Family Medicine Locum – Oshawa Ontario – Starting September 2026 We are looking for a family physician to provide locum coverage for an approximately 6-month medical leave, starting in September 2026. Duration and weekly schedule are negotiable. This is a well-established FHO+ practice in Oshawa with a diverse, loyal patient population ranging from young babies to seniors. You will be joining a supportive group of 20 family physicians in a collaborative practice environment. The Practice · Glazier Medical Centre — a large, established multidisciplinary medical centre with convenient parking and a pharmacy, lab, diagnostic imaging on site · Approximately 1,300 rostered patients · 6 clinic half-days per week, plus inbox/results management, with flexibility in how the schedule is arranged · Dedicated, experienced MOA support to assist with your practice and day-to-day workflow · Nursing support on site · TELUS PS Suite EMR · Opportunity to join our FHO after the locum period if interested Compensation · $300 per half-day paid directly by the physician · Plus applicable FHO+ hourly payments from the Ministry · Plus shadow-billing income · 75% of applicable FFS payments and non-insured fees · The $300 half-day stipend plus FHO+ hourly payments should bring compensation to over $500 per half-day before FFS payments and non-insured fees For additional information, please contact Fotini Mainville @ fmainville@glaziermedical.com or 905-579-1212 x 264 Glazier Medical Centre Thank you for our interest in medical practice opportunities at Glazier Medical Centre ( GMC). The physicians at our mixed family/multi-disciplinary group have been providing care to Oshawa and the Durham Region for over fifty years. Currently we have almost thirty partners and associates. In addition to our physician complement, our patients also benefit from our onsite diagnostic imaging department, physiotherapy, chiropody, optometry, pharmacy and dental offices. For more information, please visit our website www.glaziermedical.com. Oshawa is just 30 minutes east of Toronto and the Clinic is just off the 401 for an easy commute from anywhere within the GTA

jobs.title: Surgical Assistants
jobs.full_description_text: SURGICAL ASSISTANTS – AJAX/PICKERING & OSHAWA HOSPITALS Join our growing team of full and part-time Surgical Assistants supporting high-volume surgical programs across Lakeridge Health. Due to increasing surgical demand and a regional shortage of Surgical Assistants, we are actively recruiting qualified candidates. Surgical Assistants support procedures across Orthopedic Surgery, General Surgery, Urology, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Non-Cardiac Thoracic Surgery, and Plastic Surgery. Opportunities are available for both regular daytime work and after-hours coverage at all sites but primarily Ajax-Pickering and Oshawa Hospitals. We have a large and expanding surgical program with excellent ancillary support services. The Surgical Assistant provides intra-operative support including exposure, hemostasis, retraction, suturing, and wound closure to assist the surgeon in safely performing operative procedures. The Surgical Assistant performs duties under the direction and supervision of the Surgeon and in accordance with hospital policies and applicable laws and regulations. Eligibility Applicants must be qualified to perform the duties of a Surgical Assistant within the scope of their professional training and licensure and must be eligible for appointment and credentialing at Lakeridge Health. Eligible applicants include physicians holding independent licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario and eligible for appointment to the Lakeridge Health Credentialed Staff and privileging through the Medical Advisory Committee in accordance with the Public Hospitals Act (Ontario ) and hospital by-laws. All applicants must be eligible to practice within Ontario and meet the credentialing and professional standards required by Lakeridge Health. Qualifications and Experience Demonstrated knowledge of surgical assisting principles including tissue exposure, retraction, hemostasis, suturing, wound closure, and other intraoperative technical support functions. Experience working in a hospital operating room environment is preferred. Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary surgical teams. Commitment to patient safety, quality improvement, and adherence to hospital policies, professional standards, and applicable legislation. Successful candidates must meet all Lakeridge Health credentialing requirements, including occupational health screening and professional practice standards. How to apply Interested candidates are invited to send their curriculum vitae to the Medical Affairs Office, Lakeridge Health by email at mdcv@lh.ca Application Closing Date Applications will be considered on a rolling basis. Accommodation will be provided in all parts of the recruitment and assessment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Applicants are asked to make their needs known in advance. At Lakeridge Health we value inclusion and diversity. We are committed to fostering a culture that is respectful, inclusive, and accessible and to employing a workforce that is representative of the diverse communities we serve. As an equal opportunity employer we welcome applications from all qualified applicants. Lakeridge Health is committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment for all team members and patients. New Lakeridge Health team members will be required to complete a Pre-employment Health Assessment as a condition of employment.

This is a part-time, in-person position, requiring 1–2 daytime shifts per week. The successful candidate will provide comprehensive primary care services to patients of all ages, with opportunities to build a longitudinal patient panel while working in a collaborative clinical environment. Excellent medical documentation and clinical decision-making abilities. Commitment to providing patient-centred, evidence-based care. What We Offer Flexible part-time daytime schedule (1–2 days per week). Opportunity to build and maintain a longitudinal primary care practice. Collaborative, supportive multidisciplinary team. Administrative support and electronic medical records. On-site parking. Flexible scheduling. jobs.title: Emergency Medicine - Mentorship Opportunities
jobs.full_description_text: EMERGENCY MEDICINE MENTORSHIP OPPORTUNITIES The Department of Emergency Medicine is seeking aspiring emergency medicine physicians for locum positions at all Lakeridge Health sites as part of our LHEDE program. This 4-month enrichment experience includes didactic lectures, supervised ER shifts and simulation sessions designed to improve the ED skills of family medicine graduates and allow them to practice to their full scope in an emergency setting. Our 4 EDs are highly efficient and well supported by a multidisciplinary team including collaborative, experienced emergency nurses, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, geriatric emergency medicine nurses and crisis workers. Lakeridge Health offers a variety of services at its various, high-acuity hospitals, supported by a multitude of medical and surgical specialties, including psychiatry (2 schedule 1 facilities), interventional radiology, thoracic surgery, and stroke support (stroke center) as well as most medical subspecialties and a regional cancer center. The successful applicant will have an opportunity to join a collegial and supportive ED team in one of the fastest growing community hospital settings. Physicians must be licensed to practice in Ontario and hold CCFP certification. Other international credentials will be considered. About Lakeridge Health With five hospitals, four emergency departments, three critical care units, a long-term care home, a full range of medical and surgical specialties, more than 20 community health-care locations and a state-of-the-art surgical centre within the Jerry Coughlan Health & Wellness Centre, Lakeridge Health offers some of the broadest and most comprehensive acute care, ambulatory care, and long-term care services in Ontario. Lakeridge Health is also home to several regional specialty centres and services, including the Central East Regional Cancer Program, R.S. McLaughlin Durham Regional Cancer Centre, The Shoulder Centre, and eye care and chronic kidney disease services. Additionally, we are proud to serve our community with a full suite of inpatient, ambulatory, and community-based mental health and addictions services, and provide safe, high-quality, compassionate care in our state-of-the-art long-term care home, Lakeridge Gardens. Lakeridge Health is redefining the future of health care through transformative research, dynamic academic partnerships, and groundbreaking clinical trials. With over 140 active studies, we’re at the forefront of advancing medical knowledge, expanding treatment options, and improving the lives of our patients. Our one-of-a-kind Queen's-Lakeridge Health MD Family Medicine Program is at the forefront of training the next generation of primary care doctors. Each year, over 3,000 students and trainees are supported by the Lakeridge Health Education and Research Network (LHEARN). Through our innovative collaboration with Ontario Tech University, we’re also harnessing the power of Artificial Intelligence to revolutionize patient care. Together with our academic, community, and industry partners, Lakeridge Health is tackling the toughest health challenges and elevating the quality of care for the communities we serve. Guided by our vision of One System. Best Health . and supported by a dedicated team of nearly 9,000 staff, physicians, and volunteers, Lakeridge Health is a proud member of the Durham Ontario Health Team (Durham OHT) and works in collaboration with the Durham OHT, as well as primary care, and community and government partners to foster a truly integrated, regional system of care. Together, we are focused on empowering people to live their best health and fostering an accessible, inclusive, and equitable environment for all. Interested and qualified candidates are encouraged to send a CV and contact information for three referees (including your current Chief or Program Director) to: mdcv@lh.ca; Attention: Dr. Jaclyn Herman, Department Chief & Medical Director. Phone: (905) 576-8711 x33720. Accommodation will be provided in all parts of the recruitment and assessment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Applicants need to make their needs known in advance. At Lakeridge Health we value inclusion and diversity. We are committed to fostering a culture that is respectful, inclusive and accessible and to employing a workforce that is representative of the diverse community we provide services to. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome applications from all qualified applicants. Lakeridge Health is committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment and to preventing the transmission of COVID 19 infections among Lakeridge Health team members and our patients. New Lakeridge Health team members will be required to provide proof of full vaccination for COVID-19 during their Post-offer/Pre-employment Health Assessment, subject to any exemptions recognized under the Ontario Human Rights code.

jobs.title: Staff Pathologist – Gastrointestinal Pathology
jobs.full_description_text: Staff Pathologist – Gastrointestinal Pathology Lakeridge Health | Multiple Sites | Durham Region, Ontario Build your career. Advance patient care. Shape the future of pathology. Lakeridge Health is seeking a Staff Pathologist with expertise in Gastrointestinal Pathology to join our growing, high-performing Department of Laboratory Medicine. This is an outstanding opportunity to develop a rewarding subspecialty practice within a large, multi-site hospital system while contributing to medical education, quality improvement, innovation, and the continued growth of a community-based academic health system committed to delivering exceptional and equitable patient care. Additional expertise in Diagnostic Oncology, including Hematopathology , is considered an asset. The successful candidate will possess excellent diagnostic skills, strong communication abilities, and a collaborative approach to patient care. Our Department of Laboratory Medicine includes 16 pathologists supported by experienced pathology assistants, medical laboratory technologists, and allied health professionals who work collaboratively to provide timely, high-quality diagnostic services. We provide comprehensive diagnostic pathology services spanning a broad spectrum of benign and complex oncologic cases, including consultation services, in close collaboration with regional hospitals and the Cancer Program. Our department practices within a subspecialty-based model , fostering collaboration, professional growth, and diagnostic excellence. We offer a flexible hybrid work model that combines on-site collaboration with remote sign-out. This approach supports professional collaboration while promoting work-life balance and allowing pathologists to work efficiently both on-site and remotely. Lakeridge Health has received approval to implement a comprehensive Digital Pathology Program and is actively deploying this transformative initiative. The implementation of a fully digital workflow will support remote reporting, enhanced collaboration, and future innovations in diagnostic pathology. The Opportunity The successful candidate will participate in: Practice within a subspecialty model Participation in the departmental on-call and weekend coverage schedule Collaboration within a multi-site, interprofessional healthcare environment Quality improvement, program development, and system transformation initiatives Teaching and supervision of medical students, residents, and other learners Opportunities for leadership, mentorship, research, and academic engagement Why Join Lakeridge Health? Academic Medicine Lakeridge Health is evolving as a community-based academic health system with a growing commitment to education, scholarship, innovation, and system improvement. Physicians play an integral role in shaping this environment through teaching, mentorship, leadership, and program development. Successful candidates may be eligible for academic appointments through our university partners, commensurate with their qualifications and experience. Queen's University Partnership and Distributed Medical Education Lakeridge Health is home to the Queen's University–Lakeridge Health Family Medicine Program satellite campus and supports learners through the QBOL Family Medicine Residency Program, together with an expanding network of undergraduate and postgraduate learners. Opportunities include: Undergraduate and postgraduate medical education Clinical teaching and supervision Mentorship and preceptorship Academic program development Educational scholarship Academic promotion Distributed medical education LHEARN – Education, Simulation and Innovation Physicians have access to the Learning, Health Education and Research Network (LHEARN) and the LHEARN Centre, providing outstanding resources for education, simulation, and innovation. These include: Dedicated education and learning facilities Four simulation laboratories Simulation-based teaching opportunities Interprofessional education Health Sciences Library services and point-of-care resources Innovation in experiential learning Commitment to Health Equity Lakeridge Health is committed to advancing health equity and improving the health of the diverse communities we serve throughout Durham Region. Physicians are encouraged to: Deliver equitable, patient-centred care Improve access and healthcare outcomes Participate in initiatives that promote culturally safe and inclusive care Contribute to population health and system improvement Mentorship and Physician Support We recognize that joining a new organization or transitioning into independent practice requires meaningful support. Our department offers: Structured onboarding Departmental mentorship Collegial peer support Flexible practice transition for early-career physicians Leadership Development Physicians are encouraged to pursue leadership opportunities throughout their careers. Opportunities include: Leadership development programs Departmental and organizational leadership Quality improvement initiatives Educational leadership Mentorship of learners and junior colleagues Participation in provincial and national professional organizations Research and Scholarship Physicians interested in scholarship may participate in: Clinical research Education scholarship Quality improvement research Program evaluation Collaborative academic initiatives A Supportive Physician Practice Environment Lakeridge Health is actively strengthening the infrastructure that supports physician practice through: Clear governance and leadership Enhanced onboarding Professional practice support Fair and transparent policies A culture of respect, accountability, and psychological safety A Growing Health System Lakeridge Health serves one of Ontario's fastest-growing regions and continues to invest in clinical programs, education, technology, and system innovation. Physicians have opportunities to influence program development, model-of-care design, and organizational transformation. Live and Work in Durham Region Durham Region offers an exceptional quality of life with vibrant communities, excellent schools, waterfront trails, conservation areas, and convenient access to Toronto and major academic centres. Qualifications Required Applicants must: Hold, or be eligible for, independent licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) Be certified, or eligible for certification, in Anatomical Pathology or General Pathology Demonstrate fellowship training or significant expertise in Gastrointestinal Pathology Be eligible for hospital privileges at Lakeridge Health Demonstrate excellent diagnostic, communication, and interpersonal skills Demonstrate a commitment to patient-centred, high-quality, and equitable care Work effectively within a collaborative multidisciplinary team Preferred Qualifications Preference will be given to candidates with: Additional subspecialty expertise in Diagnostic Oncology, including Hematopathology Experience or interest in Digital Pathology and pathology informatics Experience in medical education and learner supervision Interest in quality improvement and program development Leadership experience or demonstrated leadership potential Support for Internationally Trained Physicians Lakeridge Health welcomes applications from internationally trained physicians who meet, or are eligible to meet, Ontario licensure and certification requirements for independent practice. Applicants must possess authorization to work in Canada, including Canadian citizenship, permanent residency, or a valid Canadian work permit. Prior Canadian work experience is not required where it is not a bona fide requirement of the position. Compensation and Appointment Appointment: Staff Pathologist Compensation: Competitive and aligned with the remuneration framework for hospital-based pathologists in Ontario Start Date: As soon as possible Additional Supports: Mentorship, flexible scheduling, and structured onboarding Our Commitment to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, Accessibility and Anti-Racism (IDEAA) Lakeridge Health is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and accessible environment for patients, learners, physicians, and team members. We welcome applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and lived experiences and will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment process in accordance with applicable legislation. To Apply Please submit: Cover letter Curriculum vitae Contact information for three professional references, including your current Department Chief, Division Head, or Program Director Please forward your application to: Dr. A. Plotkin mdcv@lh.ca

This 4-month enrichment experience includes didactic lectures, supervised ER shifts and simulation sessions designed to improve the ED skills of family medicine graduates and allow them to practice to their full scope in an emergency setting. Our 4 EDs are highly efficient and well supported by a multidisciplinary team including collaborative, experienced emergency nurses, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, geriatric emergency medicine nurses and crisis workers. Lakeridge Health offers a variety of services at its various, high-acuity hospitals, supported by a multitude of medical and surgical specialties, including psychiatry (2 schedule 1 facilities), interventional radiology, thoracic surgery, and stroke support (stroke center) as well as most medical subspecialties and a regional cancer center. jobs.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Job share at PRHC - Peterborough, Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Job Share at PRHC The Opportunity The department of Obstetrics/Gynecology at Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is seeking a maternal-fetal medicine (MFM) specialist to join our team! Work Better Our current call group consists of seven (7) generalists and one maternal-fetal medicine specialist. Our recruit would share a full-time position with our current MFM. The partnership would together be responsible for sharing call, reading ultrasound, providing high-risk consultations and prenatal care, and providing other high-risk pregnancy services such as amniocentesis and cerclage placement. When not on service, other work opportunities would include assisting in the gynecology Operating Room (OR) or participating in abortion care, if desired. Currently our MFM specialist is fee-for-service, but we are actively exploring alternative options for remuneration. Our Labour & Delivery unit welcomes around 1,700 babies each year, has its own dedicated OR, and is attached to PRHC’s Level 2B NICU. Our hospital has an adult ICU and full-time genetics service. PRHC is the referral centre for the group of five hospitals in the region. We also have an excellent working relationship with the MFM group at Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto. This is an exciting time to join the OB/GYN team at PRHC! We have big plans for the coming years. We are exploring new opportunities to enhance our Women’s and Children’s program, developing formal relationships with the nearby community hospitals for which we serve as the referral centre, and continuing to partner and work closely with individuals and organizations in the greater Peterborough community. For those who are interested in quality improvement, in creative partnerships, and in leadership, this job will be of particular interest! Remuneration is via fee-for-service billing to the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) and Burden-Based On-Call (BBOC) funding. Minimum expected annual earnings for a full-time practicing Maternal Fetal Medicine Specialist working at our hospital and in our region is more than $350, 0000. Benefits are not applicable for this position. Language of work is English. Live Better We are also a group of physicians committed to work-life balance, and anticipate that candidates seeking a job share are apt to feel similarly! We value family time, mental health, and the freedom to pursue hobbies and leisure activities. We are hoping to recruit someone who is not only a skilled and compassionate physician, but who shares these values. We encourage and welcome fellows and locum physicians to come test the waters and see if we may be a good fit. Peterborough is located 90 minutes north-east of Toronto, making it a convenient yet peaceful alternative to city living. For those who love the outdoors, the area offers easy access to cottage country, just 20 minutes away. With Trent University and Fleming College in the area, along with a growing business sector, the opportunities here are abundant. Position Qualifications · Currently registered with or eligible for registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario · Fellow Royal College of Physicians and Surgeon of Canada in Maternal-Fetal Medicine or equivalent · Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively with physicians, nursing, staff, patients, directors, managers, and the community as required · Eligible for staff privileges at PRHC · Evidence of ongoing continued medical education Have questions? Please feel free to contact Dr. Aleah Hazan, Maternal-Fetal Medicine Specialist at ahazan@prhc.on.ca or Dr. Kate Gerster, Chief of Obstetrics/Gynecology at kgerster@prhc.on.ca Interested parties can send their CVs to Laura Golloher, Medical Affairs at medicalrecruitment@prhc.on.ca PRHC is an accessible workplace, and an equal opportunity employer. For more information about our programs and services, please visit our website at: www.prhc.on.ca

raw_json_ld.description: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Job Share at PRHC The Opportunity The department of Obstetrics/Gynecology at Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is seeking a maternal-fetal medicine (MFM) specialist to join our team! Work Better Our current call group consists of seven (7) generalists and one maternal-fetal medicine specialist. Our recruit would share a full-time position with our current MFM. The partnership would together be responsible for sharing call, reading ultrasound, providing high-risk consultations and prenatal care, and providing other high-risk pregnancy services such as amniocentesis and cerclage placement. When not on service, other work opportunities would include assisting in the gynecology Operating Room (OR) or participating in abortion care, if desired. Currently our MFM specialist is fee-for-service, but we are actively exploring alternative options for remuneration. Our Labour & Delivery unit welcomes around 1,700 babies each year, has its own dedicated OR, and is attached to PRHC’s Level 2B NICU. Our hospital has an adult ICU and full-time genetics service. PRHC is the referral centre for the group of five hospitals in the region. We also have an excellent working relationship with the MFM group at Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto. This is an exciting time to join the OB/GYN team at PRHC! We have big plans for the coming years. We are exploring new opportunities to enhance our Women’s and Children’s program, developing formal relationships with the nearby community hospitals for which we serve as the referral centre, and continuing to partner and work closely with individuals and organizations in the greater Peterborough community. jobs.title: Nuclear Cardiologist - Peterborough, Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Nuclear Cardiologist (FULL-TIME POSITION) Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. Add more life to your career. With our investments in people and leading edge, specialized services, it’s an amazing time to be a part of PRHC. As a part of Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC), you’ll work with diverse and talented leaders and colleagues who are committed to providing extraordinary care, and you’ll be doing it all in a place where you’ll make a meaningful impact on people’s lives while you transform your own. Experience the PRHC difference. Visit prhc.on.ca/careers/ The Opportunity PRHC is seeking a Nuclear Cardiologist to join its vibrant growing cardiology program. As one of the Cardiac Centres of Excellence for the Central East LHIN, PRHC serves as a regional cardiac referral centre for our parner hospitals through the region, supported by regional nephrology and hemodialysis programs, vascular surgery and Level 3 ICU. Qualified Candidates will: · Join our team of Cardiologists who provide MRP Cardiac Care in our CCU, ward telemetry unit · Provide Consultative services to our busy Emergency Department and throughout the hospital · Attend in PRHC Regional Chest Pain, Rapid Access and Heart Function clinics (NP supported). Reading and Reporting of Nuclear Cardiology studies to support these clinics is required · Have opportunity to join an established group Cardiology practice with full range of testing: stress testing, stressechocardiography, echocardiography, Holter Monitors Position Qualifications: • Currently licensed with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario or eligible to obtain license • Fellow Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively with physicians, nursing, staff, patients, directors, managers, and the community as required • Eligible for staff privileges at Peterborough Regional Health Centre • Evidence of ongoing continued medical education • Demonstrated interest in patient safety and quality improvement · Level II or III Nuclear Cardiology Certification is required Work Better PRHC is a regional hospital delivering acute healthcare to a rapidly growing population of more than 300,000 in Peterborough and the surrounding communities, including the First Nations of Curve Lake, Alderville and Hiawatha. The Health Centre is located in Peterborough Ontario, a 90-minute drive north-east of Toronto – and has a proud local history extending back over a century. We are the region’s largest employer with more than 3,100 staff, 450 physicians with privileges and a core group of 250 volunteers. As a member of the PRHC team, you will be part of an exceptional working environment – a forum to share knowledge, to learn, to develop talents, relationships and careers, and a culture that recognizes and rewards the achievements of its people. Live Better In Peterborough, you’ll be as close to the great outdoors as you are to work, schools and other amenities. Cottage country is as close as 20 minutes away. An hour south of Kawartha Highlands Provincial Park and a couple of hours from Algonquin Provincial Park. Here, we boast all the conveniences and comforts that an exceptional quality of life demands. Here, you can have it all. Just 90 minutes from downtown Toronto by car, Peterborough is a unique community unto itself, an established entity with a rich heritage, a thriving culture, and a bright future. Home to Trent University and Fleming College as well as a burgeoning business sector, the opportunities here abound. Peterborough offers a unique blend of outdoor pursuits and urban amenities right at your doorstep. Our arts and culture community is renowned for its exceptional events, exhibitions and performances, and the city offers a wide array of multicultural cuisine, local cafés, and unique shops. Interested individuals should forward their curriculum vitae or inquiries to: Julie Tataryn, Medical Affairs, PRHC medicalrecruitment@prhc.on.ca PRHC is an accessible workplace, and an equal opportunity employer. For more information about our programs and services, please visit our website at: www.prhc.on.ca

jobs.full_description_text: Geriatric Psychiatrist - Full-time permanent opportunities available Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The Opportunity Peterborough Regional Health Centre is looking for a Geriatric Psychiatrist to support our Psychiatric Assessment Services for the Elderly program (PASE) and integrated Geriatric Medicine Psychiatric Consultation Liaison (CL) Service. The outpatient PASE program is located on-site at PRHC, with outreach locations in Northumberland, Haliburton and the City of Kawartha Lakes. PASE offers assessment for those over 65 years experiencing mental health problems and under 65 with early onset dementia. Short-term treatment and case management services are offered through the program. The PASE Team includes Psychogeriatric Resource Consultants, Consultant Geriatric Psychiatrists, Nurses, Social Workers, Occupational Therapist, Manager and support staff. Opportunities are also available for Psychiatrists as co-therapists in our Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) Despression-Anxiety Groups. Our dynamic Geriatric Medicine Psychiatry CL service is supported by three nurses in collaboration with Geriatricians, a Behavioural Supports Ontario (BSO) worker and substance use support Nurse Practitioner. A 12-bed Geriatric Assessment Behavioural Unit (GABU) provides care for older adults with dementia and behavioural disturbances. Remuneration is via fee-for-service billing to the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), Sessionals, and HOCC. Minimum expected annual earnings for a full-time practicing Geriatrics Psychiatrist working at our hospital and in our region is $300,000-$450,000. Benefits are not applicable for this position. Language of work is English. Additional Programs A 24-bed adult inpatient unit, supported by full-time social work, occupational therapy, psychology and therapeutic programming. A six-bed Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Unit (CAPU) provides a regional service for children and adolescents with serious mental health concerns requiring assessment and stabilization. PRHC also has a three-bed Crisis Response Unit (CRU) located in the Emergency Department, with nursing staff providing 24-hour crisis assessments and monitoring. jobs.full_description_text: Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist - Part-Time or Full-Time Opportunity Available Physicians trained in Canada and the United States are encouraged to apply. We also welcome other qualified international applicants who are licensure-eligible. Work permit assistance is available if needed Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The Mental Health and Addictions Department is seeking a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist to join a collaborative team of Psychiatrists providing care across our inpatient unit, Family and Youth Clinic, and Child and Adolescent Urgent Care Clinic. This role offers a dynamic mix of urgent and scheduled outpatient assessment and treatment, with opportunities to work within both the Urgent Care Clinic and the Family and Youth Clinic. The position also includes psychiatric consultation to the Pediatric (medical) Unit and shared coverage of the Inpatient Child and Adolescent Unit. This is a full-time or part-time opportunity, with the ability to tailor the role to areas of special clinical interest. Our program values collaboration and maintains strong partnerships with local First Nations communities and the Peterborough Family Health Team. Experience or interest in providing assessment and treatment for adolescents with dual diagnosis would be an asset, supporting our Dual Diagnosis Community Consultation Program in partnership with CMHA and TriCounty Behavioural Services. Practice Highlights Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) has a extensive Child and Adolescent Mental Health Department which includes the following inpatient and outpatient services. Inpatient Child and Youth Psychiatry Unit (CAPU) - 6 Beds This is a specialized 6 bed inpatient unit that provides a safe place for the multidisciplinary team (Psychiatrists, Nurses, CYWs, Social Worker) to work together to provide comprehensive mental health assessment and acute stabilization for youth up to the age of 18 years. Family or guardians and other community service providers are involved throughout the inpatient stay. Services •Individual and group therapy •Safety planning • Psychoeducation in healthy coping mechanisms and life skills •Medication management • Connecting to community resources Family and Youth Clinic – FYC The Family and Youth Clinic is an outpatient program offering assessment and therapy for moderate to severe mental health presentations. The FYC offers family and individual treatment, group therapy, psychiatric consultation, urgent care, and eating disorder treatment and is supported by a multidisciplinary team of Psychiatrists, Social Workers, Psychologists, RNs, CYWs, and Dieticians. Urgent Care Clinic for Children and Adolescents The clinic provides urgent short–term mental health followup to youth and families following a visit to the Crisis Unit. Parents and youth can typically expect a phone call from the Urgent Care Team within three business days of the Crisis Unit visit. Referrals from a Pediatrician or a GP/NP are also accepted for youth who are experiencing urgent safety issues and/or sudden changes in functioning or mental status. The Mental Health and Addictions Department is seeking a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist to join a collaborative team of Psychiatrists providing care across our inpatient unit, Family and Youth Clinic, and Child and Adolescent Urgent Care Clinic. This role offers a dynamic mix of urgent and scheduled outpatient assessment and treatment, with opportunities to work within both the Urgent Care Clinic and the Family and Youth Clinic. The position also includes psychiatric consultation to the Pediatric (medical) Unit and shared coverage of the Inpatient Child and Adolescent Unit. This is a full-time or part-time opportunity, with the ability to tailor the role to areas of special clinical interest. Our program values collaboration and maintains strong partnerships with local First Nations communities and the Peterborough Family Health Team. Experience or interest in providing assessment and treatment for adolescents with dual diagnosis would be an asset, supporting our Dual Diagnosis Community Consultation Program in partnership with CMHA and TriCounty Behavioural Services. Practice Highlights Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) has a extensive Child and Adolescent Mental Health Department which includes the following inpatient and outpatient services. Inpatient Child and Youth Psychiatry Unit (CAPU) - 6 Beds This is a specialized 6 bed inpatient unit that provides a safe place for the multidisciplinary team (Psychiatrists, Nurses, CYWs, Social Worker) to work together to provide comprehensive mental health assessment and acute stabilization for youth up to the age of 18 years. Family or guardians and other community service providers are involved throughout the inpatient stay. Services •Individual and group therapy •Safety planning • Psychoeducation in healthy coping mechanisms and life skills •Medication management • Connecting to community resources Family and Youth Clinic – FYC The Family and Youth Clinic is an outpatient program offering assessment and therapy for moderate to severe mental health presentations. The FYC offers family and individual treatment, group therapy, psychiatric consultation, urgent care, and eating disorder treatment and is supported by a multidisciplinary team of Psychiatrists, Social Workers, Psychologists, RNs, CYWs, and Dieticians. Urgent Care Clinic for Children and Adolescents The clinic provides urgent short–term mental health followup to youth and families following a visit to the Crisis Unit. jobs.full_description_text: General Community Orthopedic Surgeon Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. Join a Regional Centre of Excellence for Orthopedics Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is a leading surgical hub in Central East Ontario, offering a broad scope of complex and high-acuity services. As a Regional Centre of Excellence for Orthopedics and Vascular Surgery, PRHC is proud to deliver exceptional care across nine (9) surgical specialties with access to advanced technologies and a collaborative surgical culture. The Opportunity PRHC is seeking a full-time Orthopedic Surgeon to join our team of seven (7) orthopedic surgeons. The successful candidate will provide general orthopedic care, contributing to a collegial and high-performing surgical program. We are particularly interested in candidates who bring advanced trauma experience and/or fellowship training that complements our current group such upper extremity subspecialty training. This position provides an opportunity to broaden the scope of our practice while participating in a collaborative team environment. Responsibilities include: · General orthopedic trauma coverage through a shared call model. · Participation in general orthopedic clinics, including fracture and casting clinics, as well as rapid access services. · Engagement in quality improvement and innovation initiatives. Orthopaedics at PRHC: A High-Performing, Subspecialty-Driven Program · Subspecialty-driven practice with dedicated pathways for sports medicine, shoulder, and foot and ankle surgery. · Turnkey surgical practice with established referral patterns and diagnostics. · Same-day discharge for joint replacement procedures. · High-functioning 12-room OR equipped for complex surgical volumes. · Dedicated Orthopedic Rapid Access Clinic and Cast Clinic. · Teaching and mentorship opportunities available. · Growth in the daytime trauma room model and support for future robotic surgery integration. Advanced Technology and Innovation at PRHC · Use of the Conmed system for arthroscopic procedures and minimally invasive surgery, supporting precision and patient recovery. · Intraoperative blood conservation with cell saver technology for complex or revision cases. · Streamlined care through same-day surgery pathways, supported by skilled AAs and PAs for efficient team-based delivery. · Enhanced safety and precision with advanced anesthetic monitoring tools, including BIS, McGrath, and Glidescopes. · Dedicated block room with nerve catheter capability to enhance perioperative pain management and patient comfort. · Forward-looking investment in hybrid OR capabilities and future robotic surgical integration. jobs.full_description_text: Geriatric Medicine Specialist (2 positions available) Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The Opportunity Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is seeking Geriatric Medicine Specialists to join our growing geriatric program on a permanent basis. The role includes inpatient consultation, outpatient clinics, and home visits, all well supported by a team of experienced allied health professionals. Successful candidates will join a collegial team of seven Geriatric Medicine specialists, within a division that is actively involved in teaching Queen’s University Family Practice students. Locum opportunities may be available initially for those interested, as we currently have short-term coverage needs. As part of a truly continuum-of-care model, you will support older adults through our Geriatric Assessment and Intervention Network (GAIN) outpatient clinics serving Peterborough and surrounding rural communities, in addition to providing inpatient consultative services at PRHC. Your practice will focus on timely intervention, coordinated care planning, and safe transitions that uphold a “home first” philosophy and promote functional independence. PRHC is home to one (1) of the twelve GAIN clinics in the region. Our clinic plays a vital regional role in delivering specialized assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, education, and interdisciplinary support for older adults experiencing complex and multifactorial health challenges. As a Seniors’ Care Centre of Excellence , Geriatric Medicine Specialists will have an opportunity to liaise with and support the Geriatric Assessment and Treatment Unit (GATU) and the Geriatric Assessment and Behavioural Unit (GABU). PRHC has a new Reactivation Care Centre with a “home first” philosophy. This unit is a participant in the Institute for Healthcare Improvement’s (IHI) Age Friendly Health System. Age‑Friendly care , by design. PRHC is one of the first hospitals in Canada to be recognized through the IHI Age‑Friendly Health System - Committed to Care Excellence initiative, and our new Reactivation Care Centre is a showcase for embedding the 4Ms (What Matters, Medication, Mentation, Mobility) across teams and transitions. Help shape what’s next . We are currently redesigning our Geriatric Assessment and Treatment Unit (GATU) to fully align care practices with the 4Ms model. As a Geriatrician on our team, you will have a voice in co-design, implementation, and outcome evaluation. Additionally, we are planning to expand the 4Ms model organizationally, ensuring that its principles are integrated across our entire system. This will enhance our commitment to age-friendly care and support our goal of becoming a leading example of excellence in geriatric healthcare. Remuneration is via fee-for-service billing to the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP). Minimum expected annual earnings for a full-time practicing Geriatric Medicine Physician working at our hospital and in our region is more than $250,000. Benefits are not applicable for this position. Language of work is English. A clear and viable pathway to licensure must be established at the time of application. · Fellowship with the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC) with Certification in Geriatric Medicine or equivalent training (e.g. American Board Certification) and eligible for RCPSC assessment. · Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively with physicians, nursing, staff, patients, directors, managers, and the community as required. · Eligible for staff privileges at PRHC. · Demonstrate the ability to integrate current evidence and best practice into the delivery of quality care. · Evidence of ongoing continued medical education to satisfy the requirements of the appropriate college. The Opportunity Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is seeking Geriatric Medicine Specialists to join our growing geriatric program on a permanent basis. The role includes inpatient consultation, outpatient clinics, and home visits, all well supported by a team of experienced allied health professionals. Successful candidates will join a collegial team of seven Geriatric Medicine specialists, within a division that is actively involved in teaching Queen’s University Family Practice students. Locum opportunities may be available initially for those interested, as we currently have short-term coverage needs. As part of a truly continuum-of-care model, you will support older adults through our Geriatric Assessment and Intervention Network (GAIN) outpatient clinics serving Peterborough and surrounding rural communities, in addition to providing inpatient consultative services at PRHC. Your practice will focus on timely intervention, coordinated care planning, and safe transitions that uphold a “home first” philosophy and promote functional independence. PRHC is home to one (1) of the twelve GAIN clinics in the region. Our clinic plays a vital regional role in delivering specialized assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, education, and interdisciplinary support for older adults experiencing complex and multifactorial health challenges. As a Seniors’ Care Centre of Excellence , Geriatric Medicine Specialists will have an opportunity to liaise with and support the Geriatric Assessment and Treatment Unit (GATU) and the Geriatric Assessment and Behavioural Unit (GABU).
