jobs.full_description_text: General Adult Psychiatry - Full-time permanent opportunities available Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The Opportunity Peterborough Regional Health Centre is looking for a Psychiatrist to support our adult outpatient program (AOP). AOP is a multidisciplinary program, emphasizing a teambased approach to psychiatric care of individuals with moderate – severe persistent mental illness. We offer a Rapid Assessment Program (RAP), an Urgent Care Clinic (UCC), Complex Trauma/Emotional Regulation and Mood-Anxiety Streams, with a range of evidence based individual and group psychotherapies, along with Neurofeedback supported by our psychology service. Our program has a 24-bed adult inpatient unit, supported by full-time social work, occupational therapy, psychology and therapeutic programming. A six-bed Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Unit (CAPU) provides a regional service for children and adolescents with serious mental health concerns requiring assessment and stabilization. A 12-bed geriatric Assessment Behavioural Unit (GABU) provides care for older adults with dementia and behavioural disturbances. PRHC also has a three-bed Crisis Response Unit (CRU) located in the Emergency Department, with nursing staff providing 24-hour crisis assessments and monitoring. Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) and Four Counties Addictions Services Team (Fourcast) staff are located on the unit and provide short-term case management for patients living in the community. A multidisciplinary consultation-liaison service provides inpatient consultations and ongoing liaison across medical and surgical units. We offer a diverse range of outpatient mental health programs across all stages of life, which includes evidencebased individual and group psychotherapies, outreach services and psychiatric management. Subspecialty clinics include Early Psychosis Intervention (EPI); Psychosis Assessment and Treatment Clinic; Eating Disorder Program; Psychiatric Assessment Services for the Elderly (PASE) and the Family and Youth Clinic. A satellite Developmental Disabilities Consulting Program (DDCP) affiliated with Queens University is available through our outpatient program. Psychological testing is also available for inpatients and outpatient services. Our Neurostimulation Program includes Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT) with plans to introduce repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) in 2022. Our department is a designated teaching site for trainees at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels, affiliated through Queens and McMaster University and University of Toronto, with opportunities for faculty appointments. Remuneration is via fee-for-service billing to the Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP), Sessionals, and HOCC. Minimum expected annual earnings for a full-time practicing Psychiatrist working at our hospital and in our region is $300, 000-$450,000. Benefits are not applicable for this position. Language of work is English. jobs.full_description_text: Generalist ObGyn Locum Opportunity Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) is seeking a generalist locum with coverage dates December 14, 2026 to September 7, 2027. This is to cover a maternity leave for one of our physicians and dates can be flexible. The group of physicians you will be working with are committed to work-life balance in addition to being skilled obgyns and supportive colleagues. We welcome new graduates and those wanting a positive change to consider locum work within our department. If there is a good mutual fit, there are opportunities for permanent employment as well. Our current call group consists of seven generalists and one maternal-fetal medicine specialist. Locum coverage would be for a full-time generalist practice at Evolve Obgyn, www.evolveobgyn.com . The locum would be responsible for: · Call, four (4) to five (5), 24 hour shifts per month · One (1) to two (2)clinic days per week · Operating room time, two (2) days per month Options to assist colleagues in the operating room or to participate in abortion care are available. Peterborough is conveniently located 90 minutes from Toronto and offers a nice alternative to city living for those who enjoy the outdoors and cottage country! For more information about the City of Peterborough visit www.ptbotourism.ca . We ask that the candidate be currently registered or eligible for registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. For more information, please email Dr. Nicole Hill at nihill@prhc.on.ca

jobs.title: Emergency Medicine Moonlighting Resident Opportunity - Peterborough, Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Emergency Medicine Moonlighting Resident Opportunity Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. The Department PRHC has a busy Emergency Department which receives approximately 77,000 visits per year of all age groups and variable acuity. Our group is very collegial with excellent clinical support for each other, including no single coverage times in the department. We have monthly interprofessional simulations and departmental educational rounds. We also organize and host an annual Kawartha Emergency Medicine conference. We are affiliated with Queen’s University and are an educational site for the CCFP (EM) residents and the Queens CCFP residency program based in Peterborough. PRHC has been designated as a Level III Trauma Centre site and has a high-volume cardiac catheterization laboratory that performs diagnostic and interventional procedures, including a 24/7 EMS bypass Code STEMI system. We have 24-hour emergency service to CT scans and pediatrics on call. As a Moonlighting Resident you will have excellent support from specialty colleagues. The Opportunity As a Moonlighting Resident: • You will provide Emergency Medicine Care for patients in the PRHC emergency department, within the scope of your training, and within the scope of services indicated by the registration issued by the College • You will be assigned your own shifts and be expected to provide emergency care similar to that provided by physicians in our department. A PRHC staff Emergency physician present in the Emergency Department will be MRP for each of your patients • You will not be scheduled for any midnight shifts, nor shall you pick up any call shifts. Your sole responsibility will be the care of patients in the emergency department. Qualifications • PGY4 or PGY5 residents currently enrolled in a FRCPC EM program in an Ontario medical school and in good standing • Restricted license with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario • Appropriate CMPA coverage • Must have successfully completed training in Advanced Trauma Life Support and Advanced Cardiac Life Support The Community Peterborough is located 90 minutes north-east of Toronto, making it a convenient yet peaceful alternative to city living. For those who love the outdoors, the area offers easy access to cottage country, just 20 minutes away. With Trent University and Fleming College in the area, along with a growing business sector, the opportunities here are abundant. Renumeration • Competitive AFA hourly rate • Accommodations provided for summer coverage (June through September) “I was moonlighting in the PRHC ED during my final year of residency, and I had a tremendous experience. The nursing, ED docs, consultants and hospital staff were all extremely welcoming and always willing to help me out. There is a great amount of acuity and clinical variety at the PRHC ED that helped expand my knowledge, skill and experience in a meaningful way. Plus, being able to use Epic as an EMR and having great access to imaging made adjusting and adapting to the department quite seamless. I felt like a valuable and important member of the department, and even got to be involved in some education initiatives for the department. I would wholeheartedly recommend the PRHC ED as a place to work!” - Former Moonlighting Resident For further information, please contact: Laura Golloher, Business Partner, Medical Affairs lgolloher@prhc.on.ca PRHC is an accessible workplace, and an equal opportunity employer. For more information about our programs and services, please visit our website at: www.prhc.on.ca

The Opportunity Our Plastic Surgery team is seeking to expand our group and is offering a locum opportunity with the potential to transition into a full-time role for the right candidate. This collegial team of plastic surgeons values collaboration, professional development, and continued program growth. The successful candidate will provide comprehensive plastic surgery services, with a particular focus on reconstructive breast surgery. This includes both immediate and delayed reconstruction. While there is currently no microsurgical program, there is opportunity for program development and expansion. Call responsibilities are shared equally (1:3 or 4) and include coverage for hand trauma. Craniofacial trauma expertise is not required. The position includes dedicated weekly main operating room time as well as access to a minor procedure clinic (up to one day per week). The ideal candidate will have an interest in leading the development of a more formalized breast reconstruction program, working collaboratively with a supportive and active group of general surgeons. Additional institutional resources may be available to support this growth. This is a community-based role within a large regional hospital, with no formal teaching or research obligations. PRHC offers a welcoming, collegial environment with experienced and supportive OR staff and a strong community hospital culture. jobs.title: Family Medicine - Peterborough, Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Family Medicine at PRHC Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. Nature of Services Provided The members of the Department of Family Medicine provide a wide range of services within both the hospital and the community. They have the opportunity to practice in various care models, including independent physician practice, co-managed care with specialists, and collaboration with hospitalists. Crossing several programs within Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) , family practitioners are involved in the following areas: · Rehabilitation · Complex Continuing Care · Obstetrics · Functional Enhancement Unit (Sub Acute) · Emergency Medicine · Palliative Care · MRP for their own admitted Medical Patients · Hospitalist Service · Surgical Assistants Rehabilitation Family physicians are part of the multidisciplinary inpatient rehabilitation team who support patients requiring inpatient treatment for up to 60 days and serves adult patients who are recovering from stroke, neurological disorders (Guillain Barre Syndrome, Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson’s Disease, Peripheral Neuropathy), amputation, orthopedic surgery or trauma or general disability (e.g. post-operative strengthening). This includes regular stream and slow stream rehabilitation through Geriatric Assessment Treatment Unit (GATU). Complex Continuing Care The Complex Continuing Care (CCC) program at PRHC meets the highly specialized needs of adults with complex physical and/or cognitive conditions whose needs cannot be met at home or in the community. Family physicians are part of the multidisciplinary healthcare team that patients may see. The goal of the CCC program is to meet the patient’s physical, emotional and social needs and improve quality of life, with a focus on discharge to the community, with or without supports. Obstetrics There are family practitioners who have developed a group practice that is solely focused on obstetrics. They provide pre and post-natal care and maintain a dedicated call schedule for their patients. Functional Enhancement Unit (Sub Acute) Designed to maintain, support and enhance the function and independence of patients who are waiting long term care placement. • Staffed by physician and nurse practitioner model of care with RN, RPN’s and PSW’s • Interdisciplinary Team consists of; PT, OT, Rehab Assistants, Recreation, RD, SW, CCAC Case managers • 32-36 Patients Emergency Medicine Join this collegial emergency medicine department staffed primarily by CCFP/CCFP-EM trained physicians. This high acuity and high-volume department is well supported by its multidisciplinary team and specialists and has 24 hour CT access. The group offers excellent educational opportunities like teaching rounds, monthly in-situ simulations, and a yearly conference. Palliative Care There are family practitioners who focus primarily on in and outpatient palliative care. They provide MRP care for patients on a dedicated 22-bed unit at the hospital as well as maintaining a dedicated call schedule and providing pain and symptom management clinics to improve the end of life care and transitions. MRP for Own Patients The model allows family physicians admitting privileges for patients they carry in their community-based practice. These patients may be admitted and followed on an inpatient basis by the family physician acting as MRP throughout hospital stay. Hospitalists The model supports family physicians joining the Medicine Program as hospitalists. In this role, Hospitalists practice throughout the hospital and are responsible for the care of the majority of PRHC’s inpatient population. Physicians have the flexibility to pursue either a full-time hospitalist position or a hybrid model, combining part-time hospitalist work with a community-based family medicine practice, typically in collaboration with local Family Health Teams. Surgical Assistants There are a group of family practitioners who routinely fill the role of first assistant in the operating rooms assisting surgeons during their cases. Their commitments range from occasional work to full time. Some of them also provide availability for after-hours cases but they do not have a dedicated call group. jobs.full_description_text: Pediatrician - Full-time Position Available Add more life to your career....because you're more than your job. Add more life to your career. With our investments in people and leading edge, specialized services, it’s an amazing time to be a part of PRHC. Our pediatric program prides itself on its participation in quality initiatives, hospital strategic planning and excellence in care. We offer mentorship, guidance and an ongoing commitment to supporting new recruits and their family to join our community. As a Pediatrician at PRHC, you’ll work in a large community hospital with a diverse and talented team committed to providing extraordinary care, and you’ll be doing it all in a place where you’ll make a meaningful impact. Experience the PRHC difference. Visit prhc.on.ca/careers/ The Opportunity The regional pediatric program at PRHC includes a dynamic group of pediatricians, nurses and nurse practitioners providing a wide breadth of services to the hospital, including: • Inpatient care with a 24 bed Maternal Child Unit, 10 of which are dedicated to pediatrics. • Participation in a shared-care hospitalist rounding model is an expectation. • Level 2b NICU (10 bed). An interest or additional training in neonatology would be an asset. There are approximately 1,700 deliveries a year at PRHC, with another 700 at surrounding referral centres. • Pediatric Outpatient (POP) Clinic. A variety of pediatric clinics operate out of the hospital, with over 20,000 visits annually. Pediatric clinics include: Complex Care Clinic, Personal Health Improvement Team (PHIT), Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome/High Risk Antenatal (NAS), Asthma/ Complex Respiratory Medicine, Diabetes Clinic, Emergency Room Follow-up, Urgent Care, Pediatric Oncology Group of Ontario (POGO) and Infusion clinics. The pediatric group provides continuous, shared call coverage, consultation services to the PRHC specialists, emergency room, and regional institutional partners as well as attendance at high-risk deliveries. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Please advise us of any requirements in advance.

jobs.title: Physicians Wanted - Family Medicine and Specialists
jobs.full_description_text: Family Physician – Belleville, Ontario Mizan Health is seeking a dedicated and community-oriented Family Physician to join our modern medical clinic located at 59 Dundas Street East, Belleville, Ontario . This opportunity is suitable for a physician interested in providing comprehensive family medicine, episodic care, or a combination of both. The successful candidate will have the flexibility to develop their own patient panel and shape their practice according to their clinical interests, preferred schedule, and long-term professional goals. Belleville and the surrounding Quinte region continue to experience a significant need for accessible primary care. The incoming physician will have an opportunity to establish a busy practice while helping improve access to timely, patient-centred medical services within the community. Position Overview The Family Physician will provide comprehensive and evidence-based primary care to patients across the lifespan. The physician will work collaboratively with clinic administrative and clinical support staff to assess, diagnose, treat, and manage acute and chronic medical conditions. The practice may include scheduled family medicine appointments, same-day and walk-in visits, preventative care, chronic disease management, minor office procedures, and virtual care where clinically appropriate. Physicians may choose to practise on a full-time, part-time, locum, or flexible basis. The clinic is open to physicians seeking a long-term community practice as well as those wishing to provide coverage on selected weekdays, evenings, or weekends. Clinical Duties and Responsibilities The successful physician will be responsible for: Providing comprehensive primary care to pediatric, adult, and geriatric patients. Assessing and managing acute illnesses, injuries, and common medical concerns. Diagnosing, treating, and monitoring chronic medical conditions, including diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, asthma, COPD, thyroid disorders, and mental health conditions. Conducting routine health examinations, periodic health visits, and age-appropriate preventative screening. Providing immunizations, health counselling, lifestyle counselling, and disease-prevention education. Offering women’s health services, which may include contraception counselling, cervical cancer screening, prenatal and postnatal care, and management of common gynecological concerns according to the physician’s scope of practice. Providing pediatric care, including newborn and well-child assessments, developmental monitoring, immunizations, and management of common childhood illnesses. Providing care for older adults, including medication reviews, falls-risk assessment, cognitive screening, and management of multiple chronic conditions. Assessing and treating common mental health concerns, including anxiety, depression, insomnia, stress-related conditions, and attention-related concerns within the physician’s competence and scope. Reviewing laboratory investigations, diagnostic imaging, consultation reports, hospital records, and other relevant clinical information. Ordering appropriate laboratory testing, imaging, and diagnostic investigations. Initiating referrals to specialists, allied health professionals, community services, hospitals, and other appropriate healthcare resources. Providing follow-up care after hospital admissions, emergency department visits, specialist consultations, and diagnostic investigations. Prescribing and renewing medications in accordance with current clinical guidelines and professional standards. Completing medically necessary forms, reports, certificates, insurance documentation, and third-party medical documentation when appropriate. Providing virtual or telephone-based care when clinically appropriate and permitted under applicable professional and billing requirements. Performing minor office procedures according to the physician’s training, interests, and scope of practice. Optional Procedural and Focused-Practice Opportunities Depending on the physician’s experience and clinical interests, the practice may also include: Joint and soft-tissue injections. Cryotherapy and treatment of common skin lesions. Incision and drainage of uncomplicated abscesses. Suturing and basic wound care. Ear irrigation. Pap testing and other office-based women’s health procedures. Contraceptive procedures where appropriately trained. Minor dermatologic procedures. Sports medicine and musculoskeletal assessments. Workplace, driver, insurance, and other third-party medical examinations. Physicians are not required to provide all listed procedures. Scope of practice may be customized based on the physician’s qualifications and interests. Professional and Administrative Responsibilities The physician will be expected to: Maintain complete, accurate, and timely electronic medical records. Document patient encounters in accordance with College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario requirements. Review and respond to laboratory results, diagnostic imaging, consultation reports, prescription requests, and other clinical correspondence in a timely manner. Maintain appropriate continuity and follow-up systems for patients under their care. Practise in accordance with CPSO policies, applicable legislation, privacy requirements, and accepted standards of medical care. Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with the Personal Health Information Protection Act and other applicable privacy legislation. Participate in reasonable clinic quality-improvement, patient-safety, and workflow initiatives. Communicate respectfully and effectively with patients, families, clinic staff, pharmacists, specialists, hospitals, and community healthcare partners. Collaborate with administrative and clinical team members to support safe, efficient, and coordinated patient care. Maintain all professional licences, certifications, and continuing professional development requirements necessary to practise medicine in Ontario. Clinic Environment and Support The clinic offers: A newly established and professionally designed medical clinic. Multiple examination rooms and a dedicated procedure room. Electronic medical record access. Administrative and medical office support. Appointment scheduling, patient registration, and billing support. Support with clinic onboarding and practice setup. Assistance with community promotion and patient recruitment. Flexible scheduling based on physician availability. Opportunities to develop a full family medicine practice or provide episodic and walk-in care. Opportunities to collaborate with other family physicians, specialists, nurses, and allied healthcare providers as the clinic expands. An established clinic website, online presence, and community marketing platform. Convenient access for patients within Belleville and the surrounding Quinte region. Practice Arrangement Flexible practice arrangements are available, including: Full-time family medicine. Part-time family medicine. Walk-in or episodic primary care. Combination family practice and walk-in care. Locum or temporary coverage. Weekday, evening, or weekend availability. In-person and clinically appropriate virtual care. Remuneration is based on physician billings. The clinic offers a competitive overhead arrangement, with administrative, facility, and operational support included. Final terms will be discussed with the selected physician based on the proposed schedule and practice model. Community Recruitment Incentive A physician recruitment incentive through the City of Belleville or an applicable community physician recruitment program may be available to qualifying physicians. Any incentive is subject to the eligibility criteria, approval process, return-of-service obligations, availability of funding, and contractual terms established by the applicable program. Interested physicians will be connected with the appropriate recruitment representative to determine eligibility. Qualifications Applicants must: Hold, or be eligible to obtain, an independent or otherwise appropriate certificate of registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Hold, or be eligible to obtain, medical professional liability protection through the Canadian Medical Protective Association or another acceptable provider. Be eligible to bill the Ontario Health Insurance Plan. Have appropriate certification in Family Medicine or equivalent qualifications acceptable for licensure in Ontario. Maintain current professional standing and comply with all CPSO requirements. Demonstrate effective communication, professionalism, clinical judgment, and commitment to patient-centred care. Be legally entitled to work and practise medicine in Ontario. Physicians completing residency, physicians relocating to Ontario, and internationally trained physicians who are eligible for Ontario registration are encouraged to apply. Preferred Attributes The ideal candidate will: Be committed to providing accessible and compassionate community-based care. Be comfortable caring for patients across different age groups and cultural backgrounds. Demonstrate strong communication and collaborative skills. Be interested in establishing a long-term practice in Belleville or the surrounding region. Be willing to participate in building and growing a new community medical practice. Have an interest in comprehensive family medicine, preventative care, chronic disease management, women’s health, pediatrics, geriatrics, minor procedures, or another complementary area of practice. Location Mizan Health – Belleville 59 Dundas Street East Belleville, Ontario K8N 1B7 Belleville offers the amenities of a growing regional centre while maintaining a welcoming and affordable community environment. The city serves patients from Belleville, Quinte West, Prince Edward County, Hastings County, and surrounding communities. Application Information Interested physicians are invited to submit a curriculum vitae and a brief description of their preferred practice schedule and clinical interests. Email: operations@mizanclinics.com All inquiries will be treated confidentially. Mizan Health welcomes applications from qualified physicians of all backgrounds and is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful, and professionally supportive clinical environment.

jobs.title: Primary Care Physician needed for CFB Kingston - weekdays only
jobs.full_description_text: Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to supporting the health and wellbeing of our military members. Calian is currently seeking a primary care physician to work at the CFB Kingston medical clinic. Physicians working as civilians within the Canadian Armed Forces medical clinics enjoy the opportunity to work as part of an interdisciplinary team treating an active and motivated population. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: •performing comprehensive health assessments and synthesizing data from multiple sources to make a diagnosis of a disease or disorder; •initiating and managing the care of patients with a disease or disorder within the Physician's scope of practice and/or monitoring the ongoing therapy of patients with chronic stable illnesses by providing effective pharmacological, complementary or counseling interventions; •making appropriate medical employment limitation recommendations; •implementing strategies to promote health and prevent illness with individuals; and •practicing as a member of an interdisciplinary team and consulting with members of other health professions as appropriate in order to ensure the health care needs of the patient are met. Advantages to working in this unique environment: No overhead costs or clinic fees, guaranteed hourly rate Generous allotment of time for each patient Onsite access to multidisciplinary team including pharmacy, physiotherapy and mental health services Work in an environment where no one is left untreated and patient wait times are minimal Mandatory Qualifications: Currently licensed for independent practice and in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario; or eligible for independent practice and prepared to pursue licensure within the province of Ontario Certification in Family Medicine with the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CCFP) Basic Life Support (BLS) certification Asset Qualifications: Canadian Armed Forces Aviation Medicine or Dive Medicine certification Position Details: Part time or full time contract available

jobs.title: Academic Dermatologist - Mohs Surgeon
jobs.full_description_text: The Division of Dermatology within the Department of Medicine at Queen’s University invites applications for the position of an Academic Dermatologist specializing in Mohs micrographic surgery . The Division of Dermatology provides specialist clinical care to a large catchment area at Kingston Health Sciences Centre. Clinical responsibilities will include Mohs microsurgery clinics, dermatology outpatient clinics, and dermatology in-patient consultation service. Applicants must demonstrate expertise and experience in Mohs micrographic surgery. jobs.full_description_text: Position Overview The Department of Psychiatry at Queen’s University at Kingston invites applications for a Clinical Academic Psychiatrist appointment with experience in providing care to patients with psychiatric disorders in multiple settings including inpatient, outpatient and community. This position welcomes applicants with broad clinical experience including general psychiatry, psychiatric comorbidities, forensic psychiatry, mental health and the law and a demonstrated interest or established record in academic and clinical leadership, with opportunities for progressive advancement in clinical administration, program development, teaching and research. The successful incumbent will be expected to provide clinical services across inpatient, ambulatory, and community settings. Deliver expert assessment and treatment for adults including older adults experiencing psychiatric disorders, mental health and the law, and medical-psychiatric comorbidities. Work collaboratively within interdisciplinary teams and with regional partners, including hospitals, primary care, long-term care homes, and community agencies. The incumbent will contribute to undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing professional education. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent) and be eligible for licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario . They will also hold or be eligible for certification in Psychiatry from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (or equivalent). jobs.full_description_text: Academic General Hospitalist – Department of Surgery The Department of Surgery (www.surgery.queensu.ca) at Queen’s University is seeking four Academic General Hospitalists for four geographically full-time positions. Growth of the Department of Surgery and high patient volumes have necessitated the establishment of these additional hospitalist positions, which require Internists or Family Physicians, with relevant clinical experience, to manage the acute care patients. The Hospitalist service provides excellent care for patients on two Surgical Units composed of Cardiovascular and Thoracic Surgery and second unit composed of Neurosurgery, Plastic Surgery, Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery. The average census on each unit is between 30 – 35 patients. Academic General Hospitalists will work on a rotational schedule, providing support to all the above surgical units. The successful candidates will work with a combination of Physician Assistants, Nurse Practitioners and Fellows associated with some of these services. In addition to a major focus of providing exemplary clinical service, interested individuals would be expected to teach at both the undergraduate and postgraduate levels, and contribute to the administrative functions of the University and Hospitals. It is expected interested individuals will exhibit strong leadership skills, excellent communication skills, and the ability to work in a collaborative environment, as well as provide evidence of a strong academic portfolio with demonstrable teaching experience. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent), and have or be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario and certification from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or the College of Family Physicians of Canada. The successful candidate will be a full-time member of the Department of Surgery and participate in the Surgery Hospitalist on-call schedule at Kingston Health Sciences Centre. jobs.full_description_text: Position Overview Join a department that is redefining Academic Psychiatry in Ontario. The Department of Psychiatry at Queen’s University in Kingston invites applications for two innovative and collaborative Clinical Academic Psychiatrists to join the Division of Forensic and Correctional Psychiatry. The Division provides specialized services to justice-involved adults with mental disorders, enhancing care through evidence-based practices, education, research, and community involvement. The successful candidate(s) will play a key role in advancing clinical care and academic/scholarly service in the field of Forensic Psychiatry. This posting is to fill new positions within the University. Among the two available positions, one involves providing psychiatric services to the Ontario Region of Correctional Service Canada (CSC). This role includes delivering psychiatric services and consultations to interdisciplinary teams as well as on-call services for the Ontario Region of CSC. The other position is situated within the Forensic Program at Providence Care Hospital, which manages a 30-bedded mixed-gender unit and a forensic outreach service that accepts patients from across Ontario and interprovincial transfers. There is also the potential to explore a hybrid role that integrates both settings, subject to a case-by-case evaluation of the candidate’s qualifications and personal preference. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent) and be eligible for licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. They will also hold or be eligible for certification in Psychiatry from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (or equivalent). Candidates must also demonstrate a commitment to excellence in clinical care, education, and scholarly activity and uphold Queen’s commitments to equity, diversity, inclusion, and Indigeneity (EDII) in both clinical and academic practice. Successful candidates will join a department with strong divisional leadership, expanding specialty programs, a supportive academic culture, customized clinical-academic blends, and a clear strategic direction focused on access to care, harmonization, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Protected academic time, mentorship, and opportunities for leadership are available. The Department of Psychiatry supports robust interdisciplinary collaboration, innovative models of care, and a vibrant academic culture. The successful candidate will join a collegial department committed to strengthening Psychiatry services and advancing academic leadership across the region. Queen’s Department of Psychiatry is academic, community responsive, collegial, and innovative. We design our clinical and academic systems to support sustainable, fulfilling careers. jobs.title: ACADEMIC ANESTHESIOLOGIST- CLINICIAN SCIENTIST
jobs.full_description_text: ACADEMIC ANESTHESIOLOGIST- CLINICIAN SCIENTIST The Department of Anesthesiology & Perioperative Medicine at Queen’s University in Kingston, Ontario, Canada, is accepting applications for an Academic Anesthesiologist-Clinician Scientist position. Candidates must possess a Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada fellowship or equivalent, with additional clinical or research fellowship training. Additional research training and/or degree (Masters, PhD) is a strong asset. Candidates should have a demonstrated record of, or potential for, high-quality research, commensurate with their career stage. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and maintain a strong externally funded research program. The candidate would also be active in developing collaborations. Candidates must also be eligible for licensure with College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. The position would consist of a mix of clinical anesthesiology, teaching, and a heavy emphasis on research. Given the current strengths and areas of research focus in our Department, preference will be given to researchers working in: - Perioperative Pain research - Chronic Pain research - Perioperative Cardiovascular research - Perioperative Outcomes research Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent). The successful candidate will have a n excellent track record of high-quality research output and will exhibit strong potential for innovative and scholarly research. The candidate will display evidence of being able to lead independent research. Protected time and appropriate resources are available to those who establish a significant research program. Applicants must demonstrate strong potential for outstanding teaching contributions as well as evidence of an ability to work in an interdisciplinary, collaborative environment. Referees who can attest to the applicant’s expertise are required. Members of the Department of Anesthesiology & Perioperative Medicine enjoy a competitive compensation package, including a generous benefits plan. Academic rank will be commensurate with experience. Faculty and their dependents are eligible for an extensive benefits package including prescription drug coverage, vision care, dental care, long term disability insurance, life insurance and access to the Employee and Family Assistance Program. Employees also participate in a pension plan. Tuition assistance is available for qualifying employees, their spouses and dependent children. Queen’s values families and is pleased to provide a ‘top up’ to government parental leave benefits for eligible employees on maternity/parental leave. In addition, Queen’s provides partial reimbursement for eligible daycare expenses for employees with dependent children in daycare. For more information on employee benefits, see Queen’s Human Resources . Queen’s University is recognized nationally for the quality of its undergraduate and graduate programs, which attracts outstanding students. Queen’s University is an integral part of the vibrant Kingston community in the heart of the Thousand Islands region of southeastern Ontario. It has a community spirit and amenities unmatched by any other Canadian university. The University and the region offer an outstanding academic and community environment (www.queensu.ca). Queen’s is strategically located between Montreal, Toronto, and Ottawa, in historic Kingston, Ontario, on the shores of Lake Ontario. It offers excellent lifestyle opportunities and a strong academic environment. Remuneration is competitive within a unique alternate funding plan. The work schedule is flexible, with a large pool of members sharing in the call schedule. Prior to May 1, 2022, the University required all students, faculty, staff, and visitors (including contractors) to declare their COVID-19 vaccination status and provide proof that they were fully vaccinated or had an approved accommodation to engage in in-person University activities. These requirements were suspended May 1, 2022. However, they remain in effect for students, staff, and faculty in workplaces, including hospitals, where patient care is provided and/or where the work duties or educational requirements of the position involve or support patient care. The University invites applications from all qualified individuals. Queen's is strongly committed to employment equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace and encourages applications from Black, racialized/visible minority and Indigenous people, women, persons with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQA+ persons. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada will be given priority, including any qualified individuals who have a legal work status in Canada. Please indicate in your application if you have a valid legal work status in Canada. Applications from all qualified candidates will be considered in the applicant pool. Those interested in this position should submit a complete application package, including a cover letter summarizing expertise, qualifications, and accomplishments relevant to the position. The cover letter should also indicate whether or not you will require a work permit and/or require support with an extension of your work permit in the future. As well, a curriculum vitae and the names and full contact information of three referees should be submitted. Complete applications are to be directed to the Department of Anesthesiology and Perioperative Medicine (address listed below). Review of applications will commence immediately and will continue until the position is filled. The University will provide support in its recruitment processes to applicants with disabilities, including accommodation that takes into account an applicant’s accessibility needs. If you require accommodation during the interview process, please contact Anesthesiology & Perioperative Medicine. jobs.full_description_text: Vascular Surgery– Academic Surgeon The Department of Surgery (www.surgery.queensu.ca) at Queen’s University is seeking an Academic Vascular Surgeon position specializing in vascular/endovascular surgery. The candidate will have completed vascular fellowship training at the commencement of their appointment or have been practicing vascular/endovascular surgery with an interest in an academic career. Additional fellowship training as a Masters or PhD would also be advantageous. The preferred candidate must have an excellent record of success working in a collaborative multi-disciplinary clinical environment. They must demonstrate strong potential for outstanding educational contributions and significant academic and scholarly research in line with the mission of the Division of Cardiovascular Surgery. Evidence of current involvement and commitment to research through the submission of a research dossier outlining an academic plan and career goals is requested. Applicants will also be involved in undergraduate and post-graduate medical education. Submission of an educational dossier is encouraged. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree, have completed an accredited residency program in vascular surgery and received certification in Vascular Surgery. Any postgraduate/fellowship qualifications should be completed prior to appointment. Candidates must be eligible for licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario and hold certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. The successful candidate will be a full-time member of the Division of Cardiovascular Surgery and participate in the vascular surgery on-call schedule at Kingston Health Sciences Centre. The successful candidate will also be expected to contribute to the teaching, supervision, and mentorship of undergraduate, graduate, postgraduate students. Endovascular surgical and intervention will be done collaboratively with Interventional Radiology. Members of the Department of Surgery enjoy an Alternate Funding Program (AFP) compensation package. jobs.title: Hospitalist Physician and Division Chair Providence Care Hospital (1.0FTE)
jobs.full_description_text: Hospitalist Physician and Division Chair Providence Care Hospital’s Division of Hospital Medicine (1.0 FTE) Department of Family Medicine Queen’s Health Sciences Position Overview The Department of Family Medicine at Queen’s University at Kingston invites applications for a Clinical Academic Hospitalist Physician and Division Chair appointment. The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing clinical care and academic/scholarly service in the field of Family Medicine. This position is to fill an existing vacancy within the University. The Department of Family Medicine (DFM) at Queen’s University delivers an exceptional learning journey, where academic excellence and diverse training opportunities meet a close-knit, supportive community dedicated to innovative and high-quality patient care, and learner well-being and success. We are Family Medicine: for learners, for patients, and for communities. The Division Chair serves as the lead for the Division of Hospital Medicine within the Department of Family Medicine, responsible for guiding the work of physicians practicing at Providence Care Hospital (PCH) and Providence Transitional Care Centre. The Division Chair also serves as Clinical Director for Hospital Medicine at Providence Care. This role is responsible for assigning and balancing each member’s clinical and academic workload and ensuring the division’s work remains aligned with departmental and hospital priorities and expectations. The Clinical Director is a member of Providence Care’s Medical Advisory Committee and other committees as required. In addition, the position works with the Department Head to ensure SEAMO requirements are met within the practice plan. The Department supports the academic development of clinical faculty in alignment with the expectations of their clinical academic appointments Primary Duties and Responsibilities: I - The role of the Division Chair: 1. Provides strategic and operational leadership for the division. 2. Provides regular communication to the Department Head, Chief of Staff and senior PCH leaders. 3. Oversees the division’s clinical, educational, and research deliverables. 4. Reviews annual reports and supports performance review processes. 5. Supports scheduling, service continuity, leave planning, workload management, and member accountability. 6. Leads divisional meetings and supports clear communication within the division. 7. Contributes to recruitment, succession planning, and long-term divisional sustainability. 8. Serves as a key link between the division, the Department Head, and Providence Care Hospital 9. Ensures the division works collaboratively, meets its obligations, and supports members in delivering high-quality clinical and academic work. II - The role of the hospitalist: 1. The hospitalist will work closely with other hospitalists in the Division to provide medical coverage as per the Division's needs, and the clinical needs of Providence Care. 2. Be a member of the Hospitalist On-call group at Providence Care. 3. The teaching role of the hospitalist is to provide a unique learning opportunity for residents and medical students interested in Hospital Medicine. 4. The incumbent will be responsible for providing medical coverage for up to 22 patients at the Providence Transitional Care Center (PTCC). III - The role of the Clinical Director: 1. In collaboration with the Senior Director and/or Regional Director, the Clinical Director contributes to the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of: a) An annual Operational Plan that is reflective of Providence Care’s Strategic Directions b) The Program’s annual Operating Budget c) The Program’s research and education program d) The Program’s human resource plan 2. To report regularly to the Providence Care Vice-President, Medical & Academic Affairs, and the VP, System Innovation, and the Administrative Director of the relevant area, maintaining open and direct communication 3. To seek input from and guide the medical staff of the assigned clinical Program 4. To maintain contact and promote stronger relationships with all stakeholders in the Program 5. To communicate all relevant developments in the Program to medical staff 6. To monitor the medical program team and be active in the recruitment of and hiring of physicians within the approved human resources plan, and in the performance review of medical program team members 7. Lead and support quality improvement, education, and research within the Program 8. If not the same, to actively communicate and collaborate with the Queen’s department head or division chair on matters about the academic mandate Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent) and be eligible for licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Certification, or eligibility for certification, by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada in Family Medicine is preferred. Preference will be given to applicants who can provide evidence of a current involvement and commitment to education through the submission of an educational dossier and the identification of referees who can attest to the applicant’s educational expertise. A Master’s level degree is considered an asset. Why Queen’s Queen’s University is recognized nationally for the quality of its undergraduate and graduate programs, which attracts outstanding students. Queen’s University is an integral part of the vibrant Kingston community in the heart of the Thousand Islands region of southeastern Ontario. It has a community spirit and amenities unmatched by any other Canadian university. The University and the region offer an outstanding academic and community environment ( www.queensu.ca ). Members of the Department of Family Medicine enjoy competitive compensation and benefits packages. Compensation is determined in accordance with the Department’s Practice Plan policies for clinical academic faculty. For additional information regarding compensation structures for this position, please contact Faculty Support Coordinator: dfm-fac-sup@queensu.ca . Academic rank will be commensurate with experience. Faculty and their dependents are eligible for an extensive benefits package including prescription drug coverage, vision care, dental care, long term disability insurance, life insurance and access to the Employee and Family Assistance Program. Employees also participate in a pension plan. Tuition assistance is available for qualifying employees, their spouses and dependent children. Queen’s values families and is pleased to provide a ‘top up’ to government parental leave benefits for eligible employees on maternity/parental leave. In addition, Queen’s provides partial reimbursement for eligible daycare expenses for employees with dependent children in daycare. For more information on employee benefits, see Queen’s Human Resources .

jobs.full_description_text: Position Overview The Department of Surgery (www.surgery.queensu.ca) at Queen’s University is seeking a temporary Surgical Oncologist for a Locum position in the Division of General Surgery. The candidate will have completed two years of Surgical Oncology fellowship training at the commencement of their appointment. An advanced post-graduate degree (i.e. Master’s, Doctoral) would be advantageous. An academic focus on quality improvement/patient safety, health services research, and/or residency education will be an asset. The successful candidate will be expected to have clinical expertise in managing surgical oncology patients, with a focus on breast and melanoma disease sites. The preferred candidate must have an excellent record of success working in a multi-disciplinary clinical environment. They must demonstrate strong potential for outstanding educational contributions and significant academic and scholarly work in line with the mission of the Division of General Surgery. Evidence of current involvement and commitment to scholarly work through the submission of an academic dossier outlining a plan and career goals is requested. Applicants will also be involved in undergraduate and post-graduate medical education. Submission of an educational dossier is also encouraged. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent) and have completed postgraduate / fellowship qualifications in Surgical Oncology prior to appointment. Candidates must have or be eligible for licensure by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. Preference will be given to those who either hold or are eligible for certification by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. Applicants must also possess expertise, training, and experience in General Surgery. As a temporary member of the Division of General Surgery, and Department of Surgery, the successful candidate will also be expected to contribute to the teaching, supervision and mentorship of undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate students. Why Queen’s Queen’s University is recognized nationally for the quality of its undergraduate and graduate programs, which attracts outstanding students. Queen’s University is an integral part of the vibrant Kingston community in the heart of the Thousand Islands region of southeastern Ontario. It has a community spirit and amenities unmatched by any other Canadian university. The University and the region offer an outstanding academic and community environment ( www.queensu.ca ). How to Apply The University invites applications from all qualified individuals and is strongly committed to employment equity, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace. Queen’s encourages applications from Black, racialized/visible minority and Indigenous people, women, persons with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQ+ persons. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, in accordance with Canadian immigration requirements, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority. Applicants are asked to indicate whether they have valid legal work status in Canada. The University will provide support throughout the recruitment processes to applicants with disabilities, including accommodation that takes into account an applicant’s accessibility needs. If you require accommodation during the interview process, please contact the Department of Surgery. Those interested in this position should submit a complete application package, including the following documents: · A cover letter, summarizing expertise, qualifications, and accomplishments relevant to the position. The cover letter should also indicate whether or not you will require a work permit and/or require support with an extension of your work permit in the future, · A current Curriculum Vitae; and, · The names and full contact information of three referees, · A research dossier outlining an academic plan and career goals; and, · An educational dossier is encouraged. The review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Complete applications are to be directed to: Dr. Oluwadamilola “Lola” Fayanju, Head, Department of Surgery, Queen's University, Watkins 3, Kingston General Hospital, Kingston, Ontario, K7L 2V7, Fax: (613) 544-9174, Email: KGH.DepartmentOfSurgery@kingstonhsc.ca As part of the application process at Queen’s University, our recruitment process uses Artificial Intelligence (AI), as defined under the Ontario Employment Standards Act, to ask job-related questions and/or assess suitability for hire. jobs.full_description_text: Academic Respirologist – Clinician Scholar Division of Respirology and Sleep Medicine, Department of Medicine Queen’s Health Sciences Position Overview The Division of Respirology and Sleep Medicine within the Department of Medicine at Queen’s University invites applications for a Clinical Academic Respirologist . This is a Clinician Scholar role and the successful incumbent’s time will be heavily focused on clinical activity. This position is to fill an existing vacancy within the University. The Division of Respirology and Sleep Medicine’s mission is to provide excellence in the care of respiratory patients in our community as well as to continuously improve the treatment and prevention of respiratory illnesses by conducting and supporting high quality clinical research, and by educating students and caregivers in the state-of-the-art clinical practice of respiratory medicine. The Division provides an array of services to the community and broader geographic region though a large ambulatory practice, expanding procedural services in bronchoscopy and pleural disease, and provides 24/7 consultation for hospitalized patients with respiratory problems. The Department of Medicine supports the academic development of clinical faculty through mentorship, allocated academic time, access to research infrastructure, and teaching and research development opportunities, consistent with the expectations of clinical academic appointments. Candidates are expected to demonstrate exemplary clinical skills and service. Clinical responsibilities will include general and subspecialty respirology clinics, bronchoscopy, and respirology in-patient consultation service. Clinical expertise in Pulmonary Hypertension, Airways Diseases, Interstitial Lung Disease, Lung Cancer, or Sleep Medicine is preferred. Experience in interventional pulmonology procedures including any of EBUS-TBNA, transbronchial lung cryobiopsy, and/or medical thoracoscopy/pleuroscopy will be considered an asset. Candidates must exhibit a strong potential for innovative scholarly contributions. The Division of Respirology offers collaborative opportunities within our group to support interests in any of: Quality Improvement, Medical Education, Applied Physiology, Clinical Research, Health Informatics, and Knowledge Translation. Candidates must demonstrate an aptitude for medical education. They will contribute to the teaching of medical students and residents at the School of Medicine at Queen’s University, including those within the core and subspecialty Respirology training programs. As opinion leaders, Faculty members also make service contributions to the Division, the Department, the University, and the broader community. Qualified applicants will hold an MD degree (or equivalent). Candidates must be eligible for licensure in Respirology by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. jobs.title: Family Physician
jobs.full_description_text: KCHC is structured to support sustainable primary care practice. Physicians work within an interdisciplinary team and are provided with dedicated time for documentation, care coordination, and complex care planning. The model allows comprehensive care without rushed visits. The physician works in collaboration with nurse pracitioners, social workers, dietitians, diabetic educators, nurses, practical assistance and other allied health professionals to support the health and wellbeing of patients and the community. Members of the inter-disciplinary team assist with forms, non-medical needs, and allied health support around social complexities. Physicians join KCHC to continue practicing full-scope family medicine. Within this position, you will hold cross-appointments with Queen’s University as Adjunct Clinical Faculty and participate in teaching. This environment allows physicians to practice the full scope of comprehensive family medicine while maintaining professional sustainability. In this role you will provide comprehensive primary health care services to individuals and families as part of an interdisciplinary team. Care includes health promotion, disease prevention, full life cycle, chronic disease management, and coordination of care with community partners. Benefits: Vacation, Personal Days, Sick Days and Education time Health Care of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP) Extended Health Benefits come into effect after three months of employment in this position: Health and Dental Coverage, Life/Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program Predictable hours and work-life balance Sustainable call and after-hours obligations Clinical Responsibilities Client Care Provide comprehensive primary care across the lifespan, including diagnosing and managing acute and chronic conditions, as well as delivering preventive care and health education. Provides client centred care acknowledging the social deteminated of health in a non-judgemental, harm-reduction-oriented manner. Communicates in a manner that can be understood by the client and their families and other members of the care team. Shares on call duties with team of providers as applicable by ministry and group guidelines. Acts as health advocate and makes effective use of health care resources (e.g. consultants, hospital facilities, e-referral and e-consult etc.) to benefit clients. As a member of multi-disciplinary team, participates in case consultations, shared care with allied health professionals and specialists, and other forms of team-based collaborative care. Administration Contributes to developing, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating medical protocols and directives. Employs a quality improvement approach to population health efforts and client care interventions. Participates in team meetings, fostering a positive team environment to support effective communication and shared care. Maintains accurate records of client visits and encounters, including phone encounters. Supervises medical students and residents. Assists in health services planning and programming by participating on committees, supporting programs, and sharing information about identified health needs within the community as obtained through client encounters. Organizational Responsibilities Comply with all relevant legislation and KCHC policies, including privacy laws Commits to acquiring an understanding of the importance of trauma responsiveness and the impact of Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) Commits to demonstrating an ongoing commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Indigenization and Accessibility (EDIIA) by representing the diverse nature of our communities, promoting and practicing inclusion Supports consistent application and development of KCHC policies and procedures Supports KCHC’s student and volunteer placement programs Promotes awareness of and participation in KCHC activities Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and quality improvement On occasion, perform other temporary duties as required Basic Education and Experience Requirements Certification in Family Medicine by the College of Family Physicians (CCFP). Registration with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario is in good standing. CMPA (or equivalent) malpractice insurance. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Excellent oral and written communication skills (French language is an asset). Experience working with diverse or underserved populations considered an asset Experience with Quality Improvement (asset). Demonstrated ability to attend work on a regular basis and ability to meet the physical demands of the position. Excellent organizational skills and above average attention to detail. Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to engage marginalized clients, and a commitment to being a team player. Demonstrated ability to work respectfully with Indigenous communities. Proficiency in the use of computers and relevant software applications (Microsoft Office), including Electronic Medical Record software (PS Suite preferred). Other Requirements Current and satisfactory Criminal and Vulnerable Persons Check. As a registered professional, to abide by and be accountable to the ethics and standards set out by the relevant regulatory body of the profession. All KCHC staff have a duty to understand and follow KCHC policies, uphold high ethical and professional standards, and maintain confidentiality and privacy, using tact and good judgment in all dealings with other staff and clients. At Kingston Community Health Centres (KCHC), we understand that the work of Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Indigeneity, and Accessibility (EDIIA) is ongoing. We are dedicated to being accountable, transparent, and responsive to the holistic needs of the communities we serve. We will continue to listen, learn, and take meaningful action to ensure that our policies, practices, and services create an environment where everyone, regardless of their identity or circumstances, can thrive. We actively encourage individuals from all backgrounds, including but not limited to women, racialized groups, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and those who identify as members of the 2SLGBTQI+ communities, to apply to KCHC. Our commitment to EDIIA is a living practice, one that evolves as we grow and learn together. We pledge to contribute to building a system that is equitable, diverse, inclusive, accessible, and welcoming for all. KCHC is an equal opportunity employer, respecting and embracing the needs and diversity of our employees. If you require accommodation to fully participate in the hiring process, please notify Human Resources.

jobs.full_description_text: Rideau Family Medical Centre is seeking a Family Physician to join our growing practice in Kingston's east end. Located in a well-established shopping plaza adjacent to a thriving residential community, our clinic provides an excellent opportunity to build a rewarding family practice in a supportive and collaborative environment. This is an exceptional opportunity to join a well-established practice committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centered care while enjoying a collegial and welcoming workplace. jobs.title: Looking For Family Physician with Women's Health Focus
jobs.full_description_text: NEW AND MODERN MEDICAL CENTRE IN THE REGAL HEIGHTS AREA OF TORONTO SEEKING PART TIME FAMILY PHYSICIAN WITH WOMEN'S HEALTH FOCUS NEW GRADS WELCOME Job Title : Family Medicine Physician Location: Toronto, ON Company: Regal Heights Medical Centre About Us: Regal Heights Medical Centre is a brand new medical centre that is physician-owned near Dufferin and St. Clair Ave West, Toronto that opened February 2025. We are dedicated to providing exceptional healthcare services to individuals and families in Regal Heights and all surrounding communities. We offer a wide range of medical services, including family medicine and specialty medicine, pharmacy services, and walk-in all under one roof. Our mission is to deliver personalized, compassionate care in a comfortable, modern and welcoming environment. Position Overview: As a Family Medicine Physician with a focus on Women’s Health, you will play an important role in delivering comprehensive, patient-centred care across the various stages of a woman’s life. The position will have a particular emphasis on preventive women’s health, perimenopause and menopause care, reproductive and sexual health, and age-appropriate screening. You will be supported by an experienced administrative and clinical team to ensure cohesive and seamless clinic operations. You will also have the opportunity to collaborate with other physicians, pharmacists, specialists, and allied healthcare professionals to provide coordinated and comprehensive care. This position is well suited to a Family Physician with a particular interest in women’s health who is looking to develop or expand this area of practice within a busy and growing medical centre. Responsibilities: Provide comprehensive primary care with a particular focus on women’s health across the lifespan. Assess and manage perimenopausal and menopausal concerns, including vasomotor symptoms, sleep disturbance, mood changes, genitourinary symptoms, bone health, cardiovascular risk, and discussion of appropriate treatment options. Provide routine women’s health screening and preventive care, including cervical cancer screening, breast cancer screening, osteoporosis risk assessment, cardiovascular risk assessment, and other age-appropriate investigations. Provide reproductive and sexual health care, including contraception counselling, preconception counselling, menstrual concerns, fertility-related concerns, and sexually transmitted infection screening and prevention. Assess and manage common gynecologic concerns, including abnormal uterine bleeding, pelvic pain, vaginal and vulvar symptoms, recurrent urinary concerns, and menstrual irregularities. Provide preventive care, health maintenance, lifestyle counselling, and patient education tailored to women at different stages of life. Diagnose and manage acute and chronic medical conditions within the scope of family medicine. Develop individualized treatment plans in collaboration with patients, incorporating their health goals, preferences, and risk factors. Coordinate referrals and investigations with gynecology, endocrinology, breast imaging, fertility services, osteoporosis clinics, and other specialists as appropriate. Utilize the ACCURO EMR system to document patient encounters, review investigations, and maintain comprehensive medical records. Participate in quality improvement initiatives and adhere to evidence-based clinical guidelines, screening recommendations, and best practices. Qualifications: -Medical degree from an accredited medical school. -Board certification in Family Medicine. -Completion of residency training in Family Medicine. -Valid medical license in Ontario. -Strong clinical skills and knowledge of evidence-based medical practices. -Excellent communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills. -Commitment to providing high-quality, patient-centered care. -Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. -Willingness to participate in continuing medical education and professional development activities. Benefits: -Very competitive overhead offered: 23% (no HST) - Incentive of $5000 sign-on bonus for 1-year term with additional retention bonuses annually. Please inquire for more details. -Opportunity to work in a new, modern medical centre complete with full staff breakroom with coffee and snacks - Opportunity to form a FHG with option to transition to FHO+ -Supportive work environment Regal Heights Medical Centre is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Join us in making a difference in the lives of our patients and community! We look forward to welcoming you to our team at Regal Heights Medical Centre.

jobs.title: Physician - BIPOC specific
jobs.full_description_text: JOB TITLE Physician, BIPOC Specific LOCATION: Downtown (36B Prince Arthur Ave) & North York (940 Sheppard Ave West), SALARY $335,911.73 ($134,364.69 pro-rated to 0.4 FTE and inclusive of on-call stipend) FTE STATUS: 0.4 FTE REPORTING TO: Director of Community Health Services DURATION OF POSITION: Permanent Planned Parenthood Toronto (PPT) is a fully accredited community health centre that provides primary health care services to youth 13 to 29 years as well as health promotion programming, education, training and research to improve the health and well-being of equity-deserving youth in Toronto. We are currently seeking a racialized Physician to work 15 hours a week. In accordance to PPT’s anti-racist and equity principles, we particularly encourage applications from Black, Indigenous, and/or South Asian communities in order to better reflect the communities of youth we serve and the specific needs of racialized youth. POSITION OVERVIEW The Physician works within an interdisciplinary health care team to independently and collaboratively provide comprehensive primary and episodic health care to clients with an emphasis on sexual & reproductive health, health promotion, disease prevention and health education. The Physician is a member of the Health Services Team and is responsible for supporting the agency's mission, values and objectives. The Physician also functions in accordance with relevant legislation and standards of medical practice. RESPONSIBILITIES • Performs assessment, diagnosis, treatment, health education/counselling and other medical functions as required according to the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario standards of practice. • Provides virtual, over-the-phone and in-person client-centred care. • Manages and supports a client caseload. • Acts as primary liaison and consult with the Nurse Practitioners in assessment, diagnosis and treatment of clients. • Utilizes appropriate referral networks and agencies for clients. • Participates in chart reviews and case conferences. • Able to perform venipuncture and carry out related blood work. • Ensures that laboratory procedural forms are filled out correctly and that specimens are procured and handled properly. • Participates in the Centre’s on call service as directed. • Participates in developing, reviewing, and updating policies and procedures; has specific responsibility for developing medical protocols and procedures. • Provides Standard HIV Point of Care HIV counselling and testing to clients in accordance with the Ministry of Health Policies, Procedures and Quality Assurance for Point-of-Care HIV testing in Ontario. • Provides educational information on IUDs and able to perform IUD insertions and removals. • Provides educational information on the birth control implant and does implant insertions and removals (training can be provided) • Supports trans clients with gender affirming care, including hormone therapy and puberty suppression • Prescribe relevant medications and provide follow up care to clients requesting medical abortions at PPT • Maintains complete and accurate records of client visits including data required by Ontario Health and participates in regular quality of care chart audits and review. • Provides support in the development of Health Services protocols, and collects data and other appropriate administrative tasks as required. • Contributes to the planning and evaluation of Health Services programming and activities. QUALIFICATIONS • Medical degree from a recognized university • Licence to practice medicine and membership in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario • Three to five years primary care experience; preferably in a community health setting • The successful candidate will be Black, Indigenous and / or a person of colour. • Demonstrated ability to work with youth in areas of sexual and reproductive health, mental health, and gender-affirming care. • Proficiency and experience working with electronic health records an asset. • Demonstrated commitment to equity goals and principles, sexual and reproductive rights and to being youth positive, 2SLGBTQ positive, sex-positive, sex work positive and to being inclusive of diverse sexual and gender identities. • Commitment to pro-choice philosophy • Commitment to working from a community development perspective • Commitment to working cooperatively in a community-based setting as part of an inter-disciplinary team • Excellent written and verbal communication skills • Proficiency and experience working in a computerized environment

jobs.title: 100% Virtual - Endocrinology focused in Obesity Medicine
jobs.full_description_text: About Us: Metabolite is a leading virtual metabolic clinic in Ontario, focused on improving access to high-quality, evidence-based care. We provide obesity care & mens health focused in TRT through specialist-led treatment, dietitian support, and psychotherapy—all delivered online. jobs.title: Internist with Cardiology Focus
jobs.full_description_text: Job type: Full-time, Part-time or Flexible MDSearch is recruiting Internists with a cardiology focus to join a dynamic and progressive team in Toronto, Ontario. This is an excellent opportunity for recent graduates or experienced professionals seeking dynamic environments. As a General Internist, your role will involve delivering comprehensive care to patients with cardiac and vascular conditions, while also performing diagnostic procedures. You will collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary team that includes Cardiologists, General Internists, and specialized cardiac care nurses to ensure the highest standard of patient care. This position offers the chance to work in a modern, well-equipped facility with a talented and experienced team. It presents a valuable opportunity to enhance your clinical expertise and contribute to advancements in cardiac and vascular care. Whether you’re looking for a full-time, part-time, or flexible schedule, this role provides a fulfilling career path in cardiology, enabling you to make a meaningful impact on patients' health and well-being. ABOUT THE CLINIC The clinic offers a full range of diagnostic services, including nuclear testing, echocardiograms, cardiac sonography, stress tests, stress echo testing, Holter monitoring, and blood pressure monitoring. This professionally managed clinic is dedicated to delivering the highest quality patient care. A skilled team ensures all administrative and clinical operations are handled to an exceptional standard, allowing physicians to focus entirely on patient care. As part of an established and integral cardiology service in the region, the clinic offers a comprehensive range of diagnostic testing. You will join a team that understands each patient is unique and strives to develop personalized treatment plans for everyone. Requirements Independent Practice Certificate of Registration from the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) Membership in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) Royal College certification in General Internal Medicine (or pending certification) US-trained specialists are exempt from The Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons eligibility requirements (US Board Certified Physicians are eligible for an independent license in Ontario) Internationally trained candidates who pass the subspecialty exam being launched by the CPSO (College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario) will be considered Medical liability insurance from the Canadian Medical Protective Association (CMPA) or equivalent required, appropriate to the category of practice Benefits 100% of your billing during the first month to support your ramp-up period Competitive overhead Set your own schedule, including evenings and weekends Control your patient volume to maximize income. Partnership opportunities available in future Dedicated administrative, medical records personnel, nuclear medicine and ECG technicians Flexible schedule, allowing you to manage patient volume at your comfort level, with established demand and patient flow. To apply: Send your CV to Kaizen@mdsearch.ca.
