jobs.title: ***GP Psychotherapist**~$400/hour NET. Virtual only. Part-time
jobs.full_description_text: Key information on opportunity : • Virtual appointments only • Schedule is flexible (your choice) • Approximately 5-10 hours/week with opportunity to increase if you desire • No admin work, you just have to document your consultations • Billings: estimated billings up to $400/hour net to you (OHIP) Position Overview : We are looking for an GP Psychotherapist (Must have GP Focused Practice Designation in Psychotherapy by the MOHLTC-OMA committee) with excellent people skills to do depression/anxiety/PTSD consults for our patients. The purpose of these consultations will be to see if the patient is a good candidate for Group Counselling Sessions in mindfulness, CBT, CPT, CBT-i, etc. ( Group Counselling | Institute for Behavioural and Functional Medicine ) We are also looking for the physician to do CBT and/or CPT Group Counselling Sessions with patients. Time commitment : 5-10 hours per month. Opportunity to add more hours will likely be available if interested. Income : • Estimated billings $400/hour net to you (OHIP, no HST charged) Location : Virtual, appointments done over Zoom Healthcare. Hours : flexible Admin : Complete Admin support. No admin work - you just have to complete your notes (Accuro EMR) - several templates to choose from and can help you create your own. Extensive questionnaires are already completed prior to appointments to cut down on charting and we can help you create the ones you would like. Requirements : Licensed to practice medicine in Ontario. Must have GP Focused Practice Designation in Psychotherapy by the MOHLTC-OMA committee and be visible in the OMA directory. About the clinic : Institute for Behavioural & Functional Medicine offers behavioural & lifestyle interventions to help patients retrainng their physiology to correct chronic health problems. We offer patients evidence-based, OHIP-funded rehabilitation programs like CBT-i, CBT for headache, CBT for energy management and more. The first consultation is with the physician to evaluate for a patient's suitability for beginning psychological rehabilitation of their chronic condition. The 2nd appointment is with the GP Psychotherapist to prepare for the OHIP funded counselling. Learn more about this rapidly expanding field at ibfmed.ca .

jobs.title: ACADEMIC CARDIOLOGIST (CLINICIAN INVESTIGATOR/CLINICIAN TEACHER, ACHD)
jobs.full_description_text: Temerty Faculty of Medicine at the University of Toronto (U of T) and The Toronto Hospital Department of Medicine within the University Health Network (UHN) and Sinai Health (SH), Division of Cardiology is seeking to recruit a qualified full-time Clinical Academic Cardiologist with expertise in Adult Congenital Heart Disease (ACHD) and CardioObstetrics to be based at the Toronto General Hospital, 585 University Avenue, Toronto, ON M5G 2N2. The successful candidate would fulfil the academic position description of Clinician Teacher (CT) or Clinician Investigator (CI) and must be eligible for academic appointment at the minimum rank of Assistant Professor at the U of T. The anticipated start date is January 1, 2027 or as mutually agreed upon. The successful candidate will have completed a 2-year fellowship in the management of ACHD and CardioObstetrics. The candidate will have appropriate experience or formal training in research or education in ACHD and CardioObstetrics, such that he/she/they will be able to collaborate, develop and/or maintain a research or educational portfolio in ACHD and CardioObstetrics. Expertise in echocardiography would be a strength. The candidate will also be expected to work collaboratively to deliver high quality care to patients with complex ACHD and CardioObstetrics at the UHN/SH (585 University Avenue, Toronto, ON, M5G 2N2/600 University Avenue, Toronto, ON M5G 1X5). The clinical position includes inpatient coverage of the ACHD service, and outpatient management of ACHD and CardioObstetrics patients is expected. A graduate degree relevant to research, education or a related field, or a proven record of academic excellence in clinical research or education, is a strong pre-requisite. The successful applicant will have demonstrated the capacity for independent academic activity in the field of Cardiology, and is expected to advance scholarship in ACHD and CardioObstetrics. Advancing academic training, such as a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline and/or doctoral research training, is considered an asset. The successful candidate will report to the Division Head of Cardiology at UHN/SH. Candidates must hold an MD degree or equivalent and should have, or be eligible for, certification in Cardiology by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO). The primary language of work will be English. The position will be placed in the Sinai Health/University Health Network Department of Medicine (DOM) Practice Plan and compensation will depend on the amount of clinical work performed, (estimated based on fee for service billing) but will be in the usual range of $450,000 to $500,000, for an experienced academic Cardiologist in the Province of Ontario, commensurate with qualifications and experience. Additional sources of income from Alternate Funding Plans (AFPs) and merit awards from the Department of Medicine may be available. Health benefit options and plans are supplied per institutional policy. In addition, through the Department of Medicine Practice Plan (DMPP), the successful candidate may be reimbursed up to $5,000 in start-up costs for eligible office expenses incurred within the first year of appointment, as well as reasonable moving expenses up to $10,000 upon submission of eligible receipts. The primary goal of this recruitment is to participate and enrich the educational and scholarly achievements in ACHD and CardioObstetrics; maintain excellence in patient care, education, and research towards changing the lives of patients. Interested applicants should send a cover letter, a curriculum vitae and the names and contact information for 3 referees via email to: Dr. Douglas Lee Division Head, Cardiology, UHN/SH c/o Tiffany La: tiffany.la@uhn.ca Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadian citizens and permanent residents will be given priority. Diversity Statement The University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission. Accessibility Statement The University strives to be an equitable and inclusive community, and proactively seeks to increase diversity among its community members. Our values regarding equity and diversity are linked with our unwavering commitment to excellence in the pursuit of our academic mission. The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities. If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact uoft.careers@utoronto.ca .

jobs.title: Psychiatrist needed for CFB Toronto
jobs.full_description_text: Calian is proud to continue a long-standing contractual relationship with the Department of National Defence (DND) to provide healthcare services to the Canadian Armed Forces. Through the Health Care Provider Contract, Calian employs health care professionals across Canada who are integral to supporting the health and wellbeing of our military members. Position Overview Calian is seeking a part-time Psychiatrist to provide clinical services to Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) members at Canadian Forces Base Toronto. As a psychiatrist in this exclusive clinic, you’ll be part of a team of mental health professionals providing high quality care. Up to 0.4 FTE is available during clinic operation from Monday to Friday. Responsibilities • Conducting psychiatric assessments, providing diagnosis based on DSM, and providing treatment of a variety of mental health conditions including trauma-related disorders, depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, substance-related disorder, and addictive disorders. • Prepares detailed written psychiatric assessment reports on referred patients, including recommendations for a treatment plan, and participates in the implementation of the treatment plan by providing psychotherapy, prescribing appropriate somatic therapy, and generating patient medical records to support the multidisciplinary team. • Advising on operational readiness, return to work, prognosis, impairment, and restrictions. • Conducting psychopharmacological treatment, conducting evidence-based therapy such as CBT, responding to emergencies, and crisis. • Conducting tele-medicine assessments and interventions. • Providing clinical preceptorship and educational sessions for staff. • Participates as a member of the multidisciplinary mental health team in case reviews. • Provides expert advice on mental illness or disorders to primary care providers to assist them in the identification, diagnosis, and treatment of patients with mental health disorders. • Creates and maintains patient records. jobs.title: Physician, Home Based Primary Care
jobs.full_description_text: Family Physician, Home Based Primary Care Team Permanent, Part-time Position - 14 hours weekly (filling of vacancy) About Unison: Unison Health and Community Services is a non-profit, community-based organization that serves neighbourhoods in Northwest Toronto. Operating out of six locations, Unison offers core services that include primary health care, counselling, health promotion, Early Years programs, legal services, harm reduction programs, housing assistance, adult protective services, Pathways to Education™ and a Diabetes Education Program. Unison’s mission is working together to deliver accessible and high-quality health and community services that are integrated, respond to needs, build on strengths and inspire change. We provide high quality health care and community services and programs, with a focus on priority populations in Northwest Toronto. We are working from an inclusive, sex positive, harm reduction, anti-racist, pro-choice, anti-oppression, and participatory framework in addressing the issue of access to health care for our mandated priority populations encompassing all the determinants of health. At this time Unison is looking for a keen and committed Family Physician to provide primary care services to home-bound frail seniors in west Toronto. Reporting to the Hub and Satellite Manager at the Bathurst-Finch Site, this position is responsible for providing primary care services to home-bound frail seniors in west Toronto (travel area is smaller as patients are generally divided amongst the team members by geography). The Family Physician will work with an inter-professional team of family physicians, nurse practitioner, pharmacist, care coordinator and administrative assistant to provide primary care services for seniors that are complex, frail and marginalized with medical, functional, psychosocial and mental health issues. Working with the client services team and community services partners, the incumbent will ensure that quality client-focused services are delivered. The position is fee-for-service, but there are no overhead costs except for personal vehicle expenses (there is no compensation for transportation beyond what is covered by billed OHIP fees). Unison provides a stipend to cover physician participation in administrative meetings. EMR (TELUS PS Suite) access, a laptop computer, and a work cell phone, as well as allied health and administrative staff salaries are covered. The successful candidate will have: · Demonstrated experience in community-based primary care settings · An interest to work with older adults and serve them in their homes · Geriatrics focused-practice designation an asset but not required · Palliative care experience an asset · Demonstrated knowledge of and sensitivity to the impact of social, economic, environmental and cultural issues on health · Ability to work as part of an interdisciplinary team of clinical and program staff · License to practice medicine and membership in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario · Ability to cover other primary care providers for client care when they are not available · Ability to speak a second language an asset. The physician is compensated by billing OHIP fees. Overhead costs are covered by Unison. How to Apply: Interested candidates are asked to email a résumé with covering letter by Wednesday, October 15, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.to: Hiring Committee – HBPC Physician Unison Health and Community Services Toronto ON M6A 2N4 hirings@unisonhcs.org Please cite UN_2026_004 in the subject line of the email. We welcome applications from people who are reflective of the diverse communities we serve, including those who might need accommodation. Where needed, accommodations for applicants with disabilities will be provided, on request, to support their participation in all aspects of the recruitment process. Unison does not use Artificial Intelligence (AI) for screening, assessing, or the selection of applicants. While we thank all applicants for their interest, only those selected for interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Full time/Part time Family Physician — Scarborough, Ontario
jobs.full_description_text: Family Physician — Campus Medical Centre Company: Campus Medical Centre Location: Scarborough, Ontario Compensation: 80/20 split, FFS or FHO, $150 Guarantee per hour. Job Description Campus Clinic is seeking family physicians to join a new walk-in clinic being established in Scarborough. This is a unique opportunity to help build and shape a new community-based medical service while providing much-needed access to care for patients in Scarborough and the surrounding area. Our goal is to create a modern, physician-friendly clinic that combines flexible scheduling, strong administrative support, efficient workflows, and competitive remuneration. The clinic is owned and supported by experienced healthcare operators and physician owners who understand the operational and clinical needs of practicing physicians. This opportunity is suitable for both experienced physicians and new graduates. Physicians may work on a part-time or full-time basis and may choose regular weekly shifts, occasional shifts, or a customized schedule. Key Responsibilities Responsibilities include assessing and treating walk-in patients, ordering investigations, prescribing medications, completing referrals, documenting visits, and reviewing results related to patients seen. Clinic Features and Support Physicians will benefit from: •⁠ ⁠A brand-new, modern, spacious, and fully equipped clinic •⁠ ⁠A new AI-supported electronic medical record system designed to reduce documentation burden and improve efficiency •⁠ ⁠Remote EMR access •⁠ ⁠Complete billing and administrative support •⁠ ⁠Experienced medical assistants and managerial support •⁠ ⁠Established patient intake and clinic flow processes •⁠ ⁠Results management and urgent-message follow-up systems •⁠ ⁠Support from physician peers and experienced physician owners •⁠ ⁠Marketing, operational, and practice-development support •⁠ ⁠The opportunity to help establish and grow a new medical service in Scarborough •⁠ ⁠Mentorship and support for new graduates or physicians transitioning into walk-in practice Schedule Flexible shifts are available Monday through Friday. Potential shift times include: •⁠ ⁠Day shifts: 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. •⁠ ⁠Evening shifts: 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Physicians may choose: •⁠ ⁠Part-time or full-time work •⁠ ⁠Regular weekly shifts •⁠ ⁠Flexible or occasional shifts •⁠ ⁠A set day each week or selected days each month Compensation Physicians may choose between a guaranteed hourly model or a fee-for-service model. •⁠ ⁠Minimum guaranteed compensation of $150 per hour •⁠ ⁠Physicians may transition to fee-for-service compensation when their billings exceed the guaranteed hourly rate •⁠ ⁠Overhead is tiered and only begins to apply once the physician’s fee-for-service earnings exceed the guaranteed hourly compensation •⁠ ⁠Full billing and reconciliation support is provided This structure provides income stability while the new clinic builds patient volume, with the opportunity for increased earnings as the practice grows. Ideal Candidate The successful applicant will: •⁠ ⁠Hold, or be eligible to hold, an independent licence with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario •⁠ ⁠Be eligible to bill OHIP •⁠ ⁠Hold current CMPA coverage •⁠ ⁠Have an interest in community-based primary care and walk-in medicine •⁠ ⁠Demonstrate strong communication, documentation, and clinical decision-making skills •⁠ ⁠Be committed to providing respectful, patient-centred, and culturally sensitive care •⁠ ⁠Be comfortable working independently while collaborating with a broader healthcare team New graduates are encouraged to apply. The guaranteed hourly model, mentorship, administrative support, and initially manageable patient volumes may provide an excellent environment for physicians beginning independent practice. Why Join Campus Clinic? This is an opportunity to do more than simply work scheduled clinic shifts. Physicians joining Campus Clinic will have the opportunity to help establish a new service, improve access to medical care in Scarborough, give back to the local community, and contribute to the development of a reputable and trusted healthcare organization. The role offers flexibility, financial security, clinical autonomy, peer support, and the opportunity to grow with the clinic. How to Apply Please submit your résumé through the HFOJobs portal or email it directly to info@seneschalhealth.com If you are a dedicated family physician looking for a fulfilling opportunity to make a positive impact on the health and well-being of patients of all ages in a supportive and well-equipped environment, we encourage you to apply. Campus Medical Centre is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

This wonderful opportunity is perfect for physicians seeking flexible hours and days , allowing for a healthy work-life balance while enjoying an excellent medical practice in a modern, well-equipped facility. Advanced EMR system (training provided) PS Suite EMR with complete electronic integration of medical records, lab results, X-rays, ultrasounds, and other reports. On-site diagnostics and pharmacy The same professional building houses Lifelabs, a pharmacy, and diagnostic imaging services, including X-ray, ultrasound, bone mineral density, and breast imaging. Convenience for you and your patients Located beside the busy Agincourt Mall with ample free parking. Stress-free practice management We handle all patient bookings and administration—you simply arrive for your clinic days and focus on your patients. jobs.title: Maternity Leave Locum for FHO+ community practice - Scarborough (Guildwood)
jobs.full_description_text: 6–9 Month Family Medicine Locum – Scarborough (Guildwood), Ontario | Starting Mid-December 2026 I’m looking for a family physician to cover my practice during maternity leave for approximately 6–9 months , starting mid-December 2026 . Duration and weekly schedule are negotiable. This is a well-established FHO+ community practice in Guildwood, near the Scarborough Bluffs , with a lovely English-speaking patient population. Many families have been with the practice for decades — I genuinely see babies through to their great-grandparents. The practice Livingston Medical Centre, 123 Guildwood Parkway — large plaza with plenty of free parking and a pharmacy next door with very helpful pharmacists Approximately 1,150 rostered patients 6–8 clinic half-days per week , plus inbox/results management, with flexibility in how the schedule is arranged Work alongside 2 very supportive family physicians , including our FHO lead 2–3 experienced secretaries/MOAs working up front at any given time OSCAR Pro EMR with Cortico Access to my Heidi AI scribe We are actively experimenting with AI-enabled workflows, including Strello and Cortico’s AI tools Opportunity to join our FHO after the locum if interested Compensation $300 per half-day paid directly by me Plus applicable FHO+ hourly payments from the Ministry Plus shadow-billing income and non-insured fees No overhead The $300 half-day stipend plus FHO+ hourly payments should bring compensation to over $500 per half-day before shadow billing and non-insured fees After-hours coverage Approximately one Wednesday evening per month, 5–8 pm Approximately 2 weekend after-hours shifts over a 6-month period Required Qualifications CCFP-certified family physician licensed to practise independently in Ontario with the CPSO CMPA coverage Eligible to bill OHIP Comfortable providing comprehensive family medicine across the lifespan, including pediatric, adult and geriatric care Comfortable managing routine results, referrals, prescription renewals and other inbox work associated with the practice Interested in working in a warm, community-based practice with friendly and supportive physician colleagues, staff and patients Experience with OSCAR Pro/Cortico is an asset, but not required. This would be a great fit for someone looking for a friendly, well-supported community practice with an established and very pleasant patient population. There is also the possibility of a longer-term opportunity to join our FHO afterward if interested.

jobs.title: Family Physician
jobs.full_description_text: Family Physician, Black Health and Social Services Hub Permanent Full time Position: 35 hours per week Permanent Part time Position: 17.5 hours per week Salary Range: $157.81- $182.40 per hour Location: Black Health and Social Services Hub in Brampton This is an existing opening. Artificial Intelligence tools may be used to screen candidates Organization Background LAMP Community Health Centre is a multi-service, community based charitable organization that provides a wide range of programs and services to improve a person's health. LAMP uses a co-ordinated approach to connect people to medical services and other programs that build personal resources. By providing services that improve physical, emotional, social and economic well-being, people can better control their health and environment. Our organization is grounded in principles of health equity, and we are committed to delivering services and programs through an anti-racism, anti-oppression lens. We strive to create a healthier community by putting people first and addressing systemic barriers to care. The Black Health and Social Services (BHSS Hub) is an Afrocentric, culturally-affirming hub offering primary health care, social services and mental health and addictions support to Black, African and Caribbean (BAC) communities in Peel Region. Roots Community Services, LAMP Community Health Centre and the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA) Peel Dufferin are partnering to offer this initiative which was being designed with the holistic health of the individual as the primary focus. This ensures that services are easily accessible and closer to home for Black, African and Caribbean (BAC) communities in Peel. Job Summary At the heart of our work is an interdisciplinary approach that delivers holistic, community-based care – with a strong focus on individuals who experience barriers to accessing health services. Our team is deeply committed to inclusivity and works within the social determinants of health framework, emphasizing prevention, health promotion, and client education. Working within the objectives of the program and the standards of the College, the Family Physician works in an interdisciplinary team environment to provide comprehensive primary health care to clients and their families taking into consideration the social determinants of health within a model of care which emphasizes health promotion and prevention through client education. The role is expected to advance community health by using an equity lens and provide services through an anti-racism, anti-oppression framework. Primary Responsibilities Client Care • Provide ongoing client-centred comprehensive primary medical care to individuals of all ages including assessments, diagnosis, counselling, screening, referral, education, treatment and follow-up during contracted hours of service on both a scheduled and urgent basis. • Provide primary care to the general community with an emphasis on The BHSS Hub’s priority populations, which prioritizes Black, African and Caribbean communities in Peel. • Participate in the rotation for on call among physicians, providing advice to patients (in-person, via phone or other virtual platforms), and dealing with urgent lab results. • Collaborate with other health care professionals and health promotion services as necessary, and consult as required with Nurse Practitioners and Registered Nurses, to enable them to work within their full scope of practice. • Ensure complete and up to date documentation of medical records including various performance indicators in accordance with LAMP’s funder agreements (e.g. MSAA). • Answer client enquiries, provide education in a manner which can be understood by the client and when applicable, their families and ensure translation services available as needed. • Strong clinical skills in diabetes, hypertension, HIV and sickle cell disease management is required. • Participate in program clinics as required. Education & Professional Development • Participate in the supervision and education of medical students/residents. • Continue to improve professional knowledge, develop skills and remain up to date concerning current trends, especially related to the BHSS Hub’’s priority populations. Administrative & Organizational Responsibilities • Initiate, participate in, or lead program development, delivery and evaluation in collaboration with other clinical and health promotion staff. • Attend and contribute to organizational events and meetings as required. • Initiate or participate in the development of clinical policies, procedures and protocols, including medical directives. • Participate in quality assurance initiatives including chart audits and peer reviews. Required Qualifications • A member in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario. • Certification from the College of Family Physicians of Canada. • A minimum of three years’ experience in a primary care setting, and/or community based experience preferred. • Ability to provide coverage for one evening is required. • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team environment. • Excellent interpersonal skills necessary to work effectively with our diverse clientele and across all levels of the organization’s workforce. • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to clearly convey information and ideas in a respectful manner. • Positive attitude and dependable with strong initiative and the ability to work both independently and in a team oriented atmosphere. • Demonstrated commitment to and knowledge of the principles of primary health care, community-based health care, harm reduction practices, the social determinants of health and health promotion principles and values. • Knowledge of immigrant and refugee health, health policies, and the Ontario health system. • Open minded, eager and willing to constantly learn and improve oneself. • A valid drivers’ license is an asset. • Knowledge of LAMP’s local communities, priority populations and/or a second language that is reflective of the community being served are all preferable assets. What We Offer For qualifying full-time and part-time employees and pro-rated to full time equivalent: Comprehensive Health & Wellness Coverage · Extended health and dental: coverage for prescription drugs, vision, health practitioners and more · Group life insurance · Employee Assistance Program (EAP): free, confidential support · Healthcare discounts via Altum Health for services like massage therapy and physiotherapy · Free access to Calm (meditation, sleep stories, self-care tools) and access to employee engagement platform Motivosity · 4 weeks of vacation to start plus paid sick days · 11 paid statutory and organizational holidays · Pension: membership in the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP) · No 24-hour rotational shifts (*physicians do support pooled after hours on-call with stipend) · No overhead costs – EMR, supplies, tech, management and staff support provided Growth, Purpose & Community Impact · Paid orientation, ongoing training, and professional development opportunities · On-site and e-learning, plus access to course fee support · Opportunities to serve diverse communities through inclusive, client-centered care · Collaborative work environment focused on innovation and continuous improvement · Active involvement in internal/external committees and community partnerships · A workplace committed to equity, diversity, and removing barriers to accessibility LAMP Community Health Centre is dedicated to achieving a workforce that reflects the diversity of the community it serves and encourages applications from equity seeking groups. Requests for accommodation due to disability can be made at any stage in the recruitment process. https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=f5713d6f-a125-4870-97d4-5bd14171d00f&ccId=19000101_000001&type=JS&lang=en_CA&selectedMenuKey=CurrentOpenings&jobId=563864 We thank all applicants for their interest. However, only those selected for interviews will be contacted. No phone calls please.

jobs.title: Hospitalist/Internist/General Practitioner - Oncology in-patient care
jobs.full_description_text: Career Opportunity in: Oncology for: General Practitioners in Oncology, Hospitalists and Internists The Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology is seeking Hospitalist Associates. The Department of Medicine, Division of Oncology is recruiting for hospitalists, internists or general practitioners in oncology (GPO) for an opportunity to join the current team of physicians that support in-patient oncology care. Our oncology unit is located at Brampton Civic Hospital and has 23 dedicated beds. In addition to in-patient management of complications of malignancy or treatment, we provide in-patient chemotherapy and manage patients post autologous stem cell transplantation in which standardized protocols have been created. Our oncology unit is supported by a rotating schedule of MDs supporting the unit, with a transition to have two MDs covering at a given time, in addition to nurse practitioners that have expertise in managing complex patients with solid tumours and hematologic malignancies. Additional supports include palliative care, allied health, malignant effusions program and access to radiation oncology. Back up subspecialist support from medical oncology will be available when needed . Remuneration is supported a stipend, in addition to fee-for-service as set by the OHIP Schedule of Benefits and Fees Qualifications The candidates must have a certificate of registration to practice from the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario and hold either a Fellowship in Internal Medicine from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or College of Family Physicians. Additional oncology exposure will be an asset but is not a requirement. The position requires excellent communication skills in English. Additional languages are considered an asset as we serve a highly diverse population. About the Program The Osler Oncology program sees over 3,000 new oncology consults annually and provides care for patients at the Brampton Civic Hospital and Etobicoke General Hospital, with a satellite clinic at Headwaters Health Care Centre. The program sees a wide variety of solid tumours and hematologic malignancies supported by 16 hematologists/oncologists. About Osler William Osler Health System (Osler) includes Brampton Civic Hospital, Etobicoke General Hospital, and Peel Memorial Centre for Integrated Health & Wellness. Serving 1.3 million residents of Brampton, Etobicoke and surrounding communities within the Central West region and nationally recognized for its commitment to patient safety. Osler is Accredited with Exemplary Standing, the highest rating a Canadian hospital can receive. Osler is a primary clinical partner for Toronto Metropolitan University School of Medicine and is an academic community partner with the University of Toronto’s Temerty Faculty of Medicine, McMaster’s Michael G. DeGroote School of Medicine, and there is ample opportunity to train the next generation of clinicians. Make an impact, lead and go beyond at Osler. Click here to watch our recruitment video and view our career opportunities. Osler values inclusivity and diversity in the workplace. We welcome and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds. We are committed to providing accessible employment practices that are in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you require an accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please notify the Medical Staff Office at mso.recruitment@williamoslerhs.ca . While we thank all applicants, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Any information obtained during the course of recruitment will be used for employment recruitment purposes only, and not for any other purpose. T: 905-494-2120 F: 905-494-6206 Web: www.williamoslerhs.ca Brampton Civic Hospital Etobicoke General Hospital Peel Memorial Centre for Integrated 2100 Bovaird Drive East, 101 Humber College Boulevard, Health and Wellness Brampton ON L6R 3J7 Etobicoke, ON M9V 1R8 20 Lynch Street Brampton, ON L6W 2Z8

jobs.title: Family Physician Opportunity
jobs.full_description_text: Job description Position Summary: Are you a compassionate and skilled family medicine physician seeking a practice opportunity in Ontario, Canada. Look no further! Our family medicine clinic’s is looking to add multiple family medicine physicians to meet patient demand. What you will be doing: Practice Environment: Our well-managed practice offers a supportive and collegial atmosphere where you can thrive. We provide trained support staff, MOA, receptionists, and an on-site clinic manager. The clinic also has venipuncture and pulmonary testing available. Modernization: We’ve embraced modern practices to enhance patient care and streamline operations. Team Collaboration: Join a collaborative team of well-respected healthcare professionals dedicated to providing exceptional care. In addition to family medicine, the clinic offers Pediatrics and Women’s Health services. The walk-in clinic also provides backup support for your family practice and serves as a valuable source of new patients. Financial Considerations: Enjoy reasonable overhead costs and a flexible schedule. Growth Potential: The clinic has patients waiting and receives daily new requests daily for a family doctor. Well Health will actively market your practice to attract additional patients. You have: Licensing: You must be a licensed physician (or eligible for licensing) in the Province of Ontario. The salary for this position falls within a defined range and will be determined based on several factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and the needs of the organization. At WELL, we are committed to fair and equitable compensation and aim to provide a competitive salary that reflects the value and expertise of the successful candidate. WELL is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace. We welcome and celebrate the diversity of applicants and team members across ability, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, and lived experience. We strive to create an environment where differences are valued and contribute to our collective success – this is the WELL Way. WELL has been independently certified as a Great Place to Work® by the Great Place to Work Institute® Canada. This recognition reflects our commitment to building a workplace culture rooted in trust, inclusivity, and employee well-being. It also aligns with our Healthy Place to Work pillar and the priorities outlined in our annual Sustainability Impact Report .

jobs.title: Surgical Assistant at Minor Surgery Center Vaughan - Saturdays
jobs.full_description_text: The Minor Surgey Center Vaughan is a practise that performs excisions of skin cancers, lumps and bumps (lipomas/cysts/skin tags/etc) and minor hand surgeries such as carpal tunnel releases and trigger fingers. We have an oustanding staff of over 20 plastic surgeons and 10 nurses. We have 6 functioning minor procedure rooms where the surgeries are performed under local anesthesia. We are looking for one or two part time family doctors to help as surgical assistants on Saturdays. This is a fee for service structure where the assistant will directly bill OHIP and the surgical assistant will keep 100% of billings. Saturday premium applies to surgical assist codes. Typical days are 9am to 3pm or 10am to 4pm with a 30 minute lunch break. Expected duties are prepping and drapping, holding retractors, cutting sutures, applying dressings and helping the nurse with room turnover. It is a positive if the assistant can suture, however we are always happy to teach.

jobs.title: Adolescent Medicine: Physician Job Opportunity
jobs.full_description_text: We are currently looking for an Adolescent Medicine physician to fill a full-time/part-time position who will work collaboratively with the medical team and rehabilitation and developmental clinicians in the clinics and at SickKids. We are also open to hiring supervised physicians. Boomerang Health, powered by SickKids, is a multidisciplinary paediatric clinic, independent but wholly owned by The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids). We offer physician, rehabilitation, and developmental services up to age 18 and transitional-aged youth services up to age 25. Medical and rehab services are offered both in-person and virtually. Our paediatricians and paediatric specialists work Monday to Friday by appointment, as we do not provide urgent care or walk-in services. Our rehabilitation and developmental services are offered Monday to Sunday. When you join Boomerang Health, you are joining an organization dedicated to reducing the complexities associated with the health and well-being of children and teenagers. Our connection to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) requires a continuous commitment to high-quality patient care. Boomerang Health incorporates SickKids’ policies and best practices with oversight from a quality assurance committee. Boomerang Health employees can access training and education sessions at SickKids to stay up to date on the latest knowledge and research. We are committed to working together, learning, and creating an environment where everyone feels safe, represented, included, respected, and valued at Boomerang Health. We cannot do this without a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion. As people and healthcare professionals, we stand together against racism and oppression, which have a huge impact on the health of the many communities we serve. Moreover, Boomerang Health is an equal opportunity employer. Benefits of working at Boomerang Health: · Engagement with multidisciplinary teams in rehab and medical disciplines · Opportunities for professional development and continued education · Collaborative and supportive work environment · Comprehensive administrative assistance for schedule management

jobs.title: Maternal Fetal Medicine Specialist Opportunity
jobs.full_description_text: Maternal Fetal Medicine Specialist Opportunity – Join Mackenzie Health’s growing Women and Child Health Program Experience a place where people come first As a healthcare leader serving a population of more than half a million people, Mackenzie Health offers a dynamic, supportive environment grounded in respect, collaboration and continuous learning. Our staff and professional staff are valued members of a friendly, diverse team, empowered to do meaningful work and supported by best-in-class technology to deliver exceptional patient care. Experience a place where people come first. Experience Mackenzie Health — your ultimate career destination. Cortellucci Vaughan Hospital serves a large and diverse community and supports more than 4,000 deliveries each year. Our well-established Maternal Fetal Medicine (MFM) clinic currently provides fetal assessment and surveillance for high-risk pregnancies within our hospital catchment area. This MFM clinic is a 2-room, Monday-Friday ultrasound unit supported by 2 full-time, dedicated, experienced sonographers and one full-time Maternal Fetal Medicine physician. We are seeking to expand this fetal assessment unit to 3 full-time rooms. We also have the opportunity to provide full obstetrical care for some of our higher-risk patients. The program also includes a highly skilled multidisciplinary team, including an on-site Level 2C NICU, antenatal neonatal clinic, pediatric cardiology clinic, obstetric medicine clinic, and prenatal genetic services. This multidisciplinary team enables us to provide exemplary high-risk obstetrical care. We are seeking passionate professionals who share our commitment to high-quality, timely, patient-centred care. Ultimately, this is where you want to be. Position Overview Mackenzie Health is currently recruiting an RCPSC-certified Maternal Fetal Medicine (MFM) Specialist for a 1.0 FTE opportunity to support the continued growth of our MFM program. The successful physician will participate in the departmental call roster, co-manage the busy MFM clinic and antepartum unit, and have access to state-of-the-art equipment across both hospital sites. The clinic operates Monday to Friday and provides timely access to amniocentesis and fetal echocardiography on-site to support diagnosis, consultation and management. The MFM Specialist will provide consultation services at Mackenzie Health in support of the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. Qualifications: The Physician must possess the following competencies: Provide consultation for high-risk pregnancies, manage high-risk antenatal inpatient care, complete obstetrical ultrasound reporting (subject to delineation of privileges), perform amniocentesis and prenatal diagnosis, and demonstrate competence in operative obstetrics, including caesarean delivery. Manage complex pregnancies, including maternal medical conditions, fetal anomalies, growth restriction, multifetal gestations, preeclampsia and other pregnancy-related complications. Comply with the call schedule established by the Chief of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. Be available for consultation with professional colleagues during inpatient days Participate in quality improvement projects within the department. Participate in staff and departmental meetings. Maintain clinical acumen and skills within scope of practice. Demonstrate excellence in clinical care. Abide by the Professional Staff By-Law and Professional Staff Rules of the Hospital, the Public Hospitals Act and all other applicable legislation. Demonstrate understanding of, compliance with, and commitment to patient safety responsibilities, including applicable program plans, policies and procedures that support a safe environment for patients, families, staff and professional staff. Skills – Abilities Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to perform the essential duties of the job. Strong clinical and operative obstetrical skills. Demonstrates behaviours consistent with Mackenzie Health’s Commitment to Caring. Model behaviours aligned with Mackenzie Health’s values of Excellence, Leadership and Empathy. Commitment to providing an exceptional experience for patients, families, staff and professional staff within a challenging and exciting healthcare environment. Demonstrates understanding and contributes to patient and staff safety. Education – Certification – Licenses Medical degree approved by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) required. Certification in Obstetrics and Gynecology as recognized by The Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC) or equivalent as recognized by the Provincial Licensing Body required. Royal College-approved fellowship in Maternal Fetal Medicine, or equivalent, required. Membership with the Canadian Medical Protective Association in good standing is required. Remuneration Fee-for-service remuneration Eligibility for Hospital On-Call Coverage (HOCC) funding, subject to the Hospital’s approved HOCC service plan and Ministry eligibility criteria Mackenzie Health is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer committed to providing accommodations for applicants upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code. We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those under consideration for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.full_description_text: Position Summary: Are you a compassionate and skilled family medicine physician seeking a practice opportunity in Ontario, Canada. Look no further! Our family medicine clinic’s is looking to add multiple family medicine physicians to meet patient demand. jobs.title: Family Physician
jobs.full_description_text: Job Overview We are seeking a dedicated and compassionate Family Physician to join our healthcare team. In this vital role, you will provide comprehensive medical care to patients across all ages, focusing on prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of a wide range of health conditions. Your expertise will help improve patient outcomes through personalized care, effective communication, and evidence-based practices. This position offers an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families within our community. You will work in a dynamic environment that values innovation, teamwork, and continuous learning. Responsibilities Conduct thorough patient assessments, including medical history reviews and physical examinations using medical terminology accurately. Diagnose and treat acute and chronic illnesses, utilizing your hospital experience and acute care expertise. Manage pain effectively through medication administration and non-pharmacological strategies, ensuring patient comfort and safety. Coordinate patient care plans that include referrals for specialized services such as pediatrics or home care when necessary. Document clinical encounters precisely in electronic health record systems like Epic or Jane App, ensuring data collection is accurate for ongoing patient management. Educate patients on health maintenance, disease prevention, and medication use to promote long-term wellness. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to optimize patient outcomes and participate in research initiatives to advance clinical practices. Experience Proven hospital experience with a strong background in acute care settings. Demonstrated expertise in pain management techniques and medication administration protocols. Experience providing pediatric care with a focus on family-centered approaches. Familiarity with medical terminology, electronic health records (Epic or Jane App), and medical office operations. Skilled in data collection for clinical research or quality improvement projects. Prior experience in home care services is highly desirable to support patients outside the clinical setting. Ability to handle diverse patient populations with compassion, professionalism, and attention to detail. Also, fluency in Farsi (Persian) is preferred. Join us to be part of a forward-thinking healthcare organization committed to delivering exceptional patient care while fostering your professional growth!

jobs.title: Family Physician
jobs.full_description_text: Job Summary: We are seeking a dedicated Family Physician to provide comprehensive primary care and walk-in services to patients of all ages in our clinic in Ontario. The ideal candidate will diagnose and treat a variety of medical conditions, promote preventive healthcare, and contribute to the well-being of the community. This role is suitable for physicians looking to join a clinic and build a patient panel. Key Responsibilities: Provide primary medical care including diagnosis, treatment, and management of acute and chronic conditions. Conduct patient consultations, physical examinations, and medical assessments. Develop and implement treatment plans tailored to patient needs. Offer preventative care such as vaccinations, health screenings, and lifestyle counseling. Order and interpret diagnostic tests (e.g., bloodwork, imaging, ECGs). Collaborate with specialists and allied healthcare providers for patient referrals and coordinated care. Maintain accurate medical records in accordance with Ontario’s health regulations (e.g., Electronic Medical Records – EMR). Stay up to date with continuing medical education (CME) and regulatory requirements. Qualifications & Requirements: Medical Degree (MD/MBBS) from an accredited institution. Licensure with the College of Physicians & Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) or eligibility to obtain licensure. Certification with the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CCFP) or equivalent. Current Medical Liability Insurance (CMPA coverage). Experience in primary care, urgent care, or rural medicine. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and patient-care skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary healthcare team. To Apply please send an email to Samantha at swilk@medicentres.com

jobs.title: Physiatrist - Complex Continuing Care, Palliative Care and Rehabilitation
jobs.full_description_text: Physiatrist Opportunity – Join our Growing Organization Experience a place where people come first. As a healthcare leader serving a population of more than half a million people, Mackenzie Health offers a dynamic, supportive environment of respect and continuous learning. A place where all staff are valued, can engage in meaningful work as part of a friendly, diverse team and use best-in-class technology to provide exceptional patient care. Experience a place where people come first. Experience Mackenzie Health – your ultimate career destination. At Mackenzie Health, we have many opportunities for passionate professionals like you, who share our commitment to quality, timely patient-centred care. Ultimately, this is where you want to be. Position Overview Mackenzie Health is seeking a 0.5 FTE Specialist in Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation (Physiatrist) to join our growing Rehabilitation Program. This role is primarily based on the inpatient musculoskeletal rehabilitation unit, which includes 12 High-Intensity Rehabilitation beds and 10 Low Tolerance Long Duration (LTLD) beds, with additional opportunities to provide consultative physiatry services to patients within the Complex Continuing Care, Acute Medicine, and other inpatient programs. The successful candidate will play an integral role in delivering comprehensive, patient-centred rehabilitation care and will work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team to assess, treat, and optimize functional outcomes for patients with complex rehabilitation needs. The Physiatrist will contribute to the ongoing development and enhancement of rehabilitation services and support innovative models of care across the organization. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate closely with the Chief of Family Practice, Physician Lead, Complex Continuing Care and Palliative Care, and Physician Lead, Rehabilitation, as well as a dedicated team of healthcare professionals committed to excellence in patient care, quality improvement, education, and program development. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and growing healthcare organization focused on advancing rehabilitation services and improving patient outcomes across the continuum of care. Responsibilities As a Physiatrist, the Physician will be responsible for the following: Provides Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation consultative assessment of physical, mental and occupational rehabilitation needs of patients in the high-intensity rehabilitation program, and on an as-needed basis on LTLD, CCC and Medicine programs at the Mackenzie Richmond Hill Hospital. Addresses musculoskeletal issues such as pain, deformity, immobility and other physiatric barriers limiting progression within a rehabilitation program, candidacy for a rehabilitation program or other disposition Works closely with other Mackenzie Health Physiatrist(s) to negotiate cross-hospital consultation or coverage if/when necessary. Opportunity to provide support for MSK consultations at other sites depending on consultation volumes. Collaborates with community partners to support hospital pathways for a small number of patients in other physiatric populations (amputee, stroke, SCI) Participates in meetings and committees, as required. Performs duties and responsibilities as agreed upon by the Division Head. Performs duties and responsibilities outlined in the Hospital By-laws, department and division rules, and applicable policies. Skills – Abilities – Experience Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work both independently and as a team member within a group environment. Ability to perform the essential duties of the job. Demonstrates behaviours consistent with Mackenzie Health’s Commitment to Caring. Models behaviour that is aligned with the values of Mackenzie Health – Excellence, Leadership and Empathy. Commitment to providing an exceptional experience for staff and clients within a challenging and exciting healthcare environment. Demonstrates understanding of contribution to patient and staff safety. Experience in inpatient settings in York Region, managing teams, teaching. Interest in teaching, passion for building programs in collaboration with hospital and community partners in York Region, and specialty academic sites are all highly valued. Education – Certification – Licenses Medical degree approved by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO) required. Postdoctoral training in physical medicine and rehabilitation residency required. Canadian Medical Protection Association (CMPA) in good standing. Mackenzie Health is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer committed to providing accommodations for applicants upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code. We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those under consideration for an interview will be contacted. Interested candidates should submit their curriculum vitae to: Sophie Stratos, Manager of Medical Affairs Mackenzie Health 10 Trench Street, Richmond Hill, Ontario L4C 4Z3 sophie.stratos@mackenziehealth.ca

jobs.title: Otolaryngology - Head & Neck Surgery
jobs.full_description_text: North Bay Regional Health Centre is looking to recruit a General Otolaryngologist to join our team. If you want to establish a community practice rich in all aspects of your field while enjoying your home/family life, cutting out the commute and high cost of living, this job is for you! Job Summary The North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) is a progressive community hospital serving as a large regional referral centre for northeastern Ontario. Our Department of Surgery includes Otolaryngology, General Surgery, Urology, Orthopedics, Obstetrics & Gynecology, and Ophthalmology, supported by a highly skilled team of FRCPC anesthesiologists. The Otolaryngology Service currently consists of one full-time otolaryngologist, with a second specialist joining soon. We are now seeking an additional colleague to complete a three-physician group, ensuring robust coverage and continued access to high quality ENT care across the region. Our state-of-the-art Operating Room features advanced technology, including the Medtronic Stealth Image Guidance System and the Medtronic NIM Nerve Monitoring System (with recurrent laryngeal nerve monitoring). We also maintain a comprehensive suite of bronchoscopes and rhino-laryngoscopes on-site. The Otolaryngology Service enjoys strong institutional support and generous resource allocation within NBRHC. The successful candidate will receive dedicated operating room blocks and ambulatory procedure time each month, with resources flexibly adjusted to match operative and procedural volume. Call responsibilities are shared equally among the group. NBRHC is an affiliated academic teaching centre with NOSM University, and our ENT team is actively involved in teaching medical students and Family Medicine residents. This position offers an excellent balance of community-based practice, academic engagement, and access to advanced surgical technology, all within a collegial, team-oriented environment. Qualifications Applicants are required to be certified in Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and independently licensed (or eligible for licensure) in the Province of Ontario. Proof of MMR vaccination Organization & Community Info North Bay Regional Health Centre is a 480 bed health care organization with three primary roles: providing acute care services to North Bay and its surrounding communities, functioning as the district referral center providing specialist services for smaller communities in the area, and it is the specialized mental health service provider serving all of northeast Ontario. For further information please view For more information about the NBRHC, visit www.nbrhc.on.ca or https://northbaydocs.ca/about/ North Bay, Ontario combines the tranquility of cottage life with the amenities of a mid-sized city. Situated on the banks of two large lakes and opportunely located an hour north of Muskoka, North Bay is home to the largest airport north of Toronto and is a 3.5 hour drive to the GTA, 4 hour drive to Ottawa and a 1.5 hour drive to Sudbury. North Bay has a population of 52,000 and features an abundance of elementary and secondary schools, retail and entertainment venues, waterfront dining and outdoor recreation. A provincially recognized Community in Bloom, with a 5 bloom-rating in 2025, North Bay offers the best in Northern culture and all-season activities. Within minutes from home, you can enjoy access to over 40 hiking trails, bike the Kate Pace Way, cross country ski at the Nordic Ski Club or snowboard down the Laurentian Ski Hill and still be back in time for dinner. See more of beautiful North Bay and learn about our lifestyle, www.northbay.ca Remuneration This position will be remunerated through a combination of fee-for-service billings, a lucrative Northern Specialist Alternative Payment Plan, & Hospital On-Call stipends. In addition, NBRHC has a competitive Incentive Package which includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, $25,000 practice start up grant, assistance with relocation expenses, and $94,000 via the Northern Rural Recruitment & Retention Initiative. To Apply Candidates should submit an expression of interest and CV to Chastity Saudino, Manager of Medical Affairs, at chastity.saudino@nbrhc.on.ca Qualified candidates will be welcomed for locums and interviews as part of the hiring decision process.

We are now seeking an additional colleague to complete a three-physician group, ensuring robust coverage and continued access to high quality ENT care across the region. Our state-of-the-art Operating Room features advanced technology, including the Medtronic Stealth Image Guidance System and the Medtronic NIM Nerve Monitoring System (with recurrent laryngeal nerve monitoring). We also maintain a comprehensive suite of bronchoscopes and rhino-laryngoscopes on-site. The Otolaryngology Service enjoys strong institutional support and generous resource allocation within NBRHC. The successful candidate will receive dedicated operating room blocks and ambulatory procedure time each month, with resources flexibly adjusted to match operative and procedural volume. Call responsibilities are shared equally among the group. NBRHC is an affiliated academic teaching centre with NOSM University, and our ENT team is actively involved in teaching medical students and Family Medicine residents. This position offers an excellent balance of community-based practice, academic engagement, and access to advanced surgical technology, all within a collegial, team-oriented environment. Qualifications Applicants are required to be certified in Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and independently licensed (or eligible for licensure) in the Province of Ontario. jobs.title: Substance Use Disorders Physician
jobs.full_description_text: Job Description: North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) is seeking a physician, with experience providing addictions medicine, to join its Substance Use Disorders (SUDS) Team. The focus of the team is to provide clear, consistent, and appropriate addiction medicine treatment to NBRHC patients, regardless of the time of the patient's arrival, primary reason for presentation, or location within the hospital/hospital sites. The SUDS Team provides weekday addiction medicine consultation services to the hospital's Emergency Department, IP medical & surgical units, as well as MRP care to the hospital-based Withdrawal Management Services (WMS), and MRP care to the Community Withdrawal Management Services (CWMS), in collaboration with the CWMS Nurse Practitioner. Future growth of the program will include an after hours on-call service. Consultation addiction medicine services are provided in collaboration with the most responsible physician/provider of the respective patient. The SUDS Team follows patients for addictions treatment despite where they are admitted within the hospital as clinically indicated or until such time as discharge. Members of the SUDS Team are responsible to complete patient care plans and relevant assessments in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team, order medications used to manage withdrawal from substances, initiate evidence based anti-craving medications, and support clients in out-patient addictions programs i.e. day/eve treatment The City of North Bay and Community: North Bay, Ontario combines the tranquility of cottage life with the amenities of a mid-sized city. Situated on the banks of two large lakes and opportunely located an hour north of Muskoka, North Bay is home to the largest airport north of Toronto and is a 3.5 hour drive to the GTA, 4 hour drive to Ottawa and a 1.5 hour drive to Sudbury. North Bay has a population of 52,000 and features an abundance of elementary and secondary schools, retail and entertainment venues, waterfront dining and outdoor recreation. See more about North Bay at www.tourismnorthbay.com/ or https://northbay.ca Our Organization: North Bay Regional Health Centre, constructed in 2011, is a 480 bed health care organization with acute care services including a 24/7 emergency department, 16 bed Critical Care Unit, inpatient adult and pediatric medicine, internal medicine and IM subspecialties (GI, respirology, endocrinology, nephrology, non-invasive cardiology), obstetrics and gynecology, pathology, psychiatry and surgical subspecialties to North Bay and the surrounding catchment areas of Mattawa, West Nipissing and Temiskaming. Onsite radiology / diagnostic imaging services include x-ray, ultrasound, computed tomography, MRI, bone densometry, nuclear medicine and interventional procedures. See more about NBRHC at https://northbaydocs.ca/about/ Qualifications Qualified applicants will have CPSO licensure to practice medicine independently in Ontario. Proven experience providing addiction medicine services is required. Additional training with a focused competence in addiction medicine would be an asset. Remuneration This position will be remunerated with a combination of weekday stipends, and fee-for service OHIP billings. NBRHC offers a Recruitment Incentive Package that includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, a $25,000 practice start-up grant, assistance with relocation expenses, and up to $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment and Retention Initiative (NRRRI)

jobs.title: Neurologist
jobs.full_description_text: North Bay Regional Health Centre is seeking an Neurologist to join our Department of Medicine. Job Description: The successful applicant will establish outpatient community neurology services for chronic care of neurological disease. Diagnostic and therapeutic resources from NBRHC are available, including CT, MRI and EEG, as well as lab/pathology services and supervised IV medication infusions. The role will include participation in the hospital-based stroke prevention clinic with an option to join the existing roster of EEG interpreters. Hospital privileges come with an opportunity to provide inpatient consultation services for acute neurological conditions, currently supported by the Service of Internal Medicine. Our Organization: The North Bay Regional Health Centre, constructed in 2011, is a 480 bed health care organization with acute care services including a 24/7 emergency department, 16 bed Critical Care Unit, inpatient adult and pediatric medicine, dialysis, endoscopy and bronchoscopy services, obstetrics, pathology and surgical subspecialties to the surrounding catchment areas of Mattawa, West Nipissing and Temiskaming. On-site diagnostic imaging services include x-ray, ultrasound, computed tomography, MRI, bone densometry and nuclear medicine. The City of North Bay and Community: North Bay, Ontario combines the tranquility of cottage life with the amenities of a mid-sized city. Opportunely located an hour North of Muskoka, North Boy is home to the largest airport North of Toronto and is a 3.5 hour drive to the GTA, 4 hour drive to Ottawa and a 1.5 hour drive to Sudbury. North Bay has a population of 52,000 and features an abundance of elementary and secondary schools, retail and entertainment venues, waterfront dining and outdoor recreation. A provincially recognized Community on Bloom, with a 5 bloom-rating in 2025, North Bay offers the best in Northern culture and all-season activities. Within minutes from home, you can enjoy access to over 40 hiking trails, bike the Kate Pace Way, cross-country ski at the Nordic Ski Club or snowboard down the Laurentian Ski Hill and be back in time for dinner. See more about North Bay at https://www.tourismnorthbay.com/ or https://northbaydocs.ca/about/ Qualifications: Qualified applicants will have licensure to practice independently in Ontario and a standing Neurology fellowship from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. Proof of full vaccination of MMR vaccination is also required. To Apply: Those seeking job satisfaction and a balanced lifestyle are invited to submit their CV and an expression of interest to physicianrecruitment@nbrhc.on.ca . Qualified candidates will be welcomed for locums and interviews as part of the hiring decision process.

jobs.title: Emergency Medicine Locums
jobs.full_description_text: North Bay Regional Health Centre is seeking Emergency Medicine Locums and is offering shift flexibility and excellent compensation! About Us: We are a 24/7 department staffed by a collegial group of CCFP-EM, FRCP(EM) and experienced CCFP physicians in a multidisciplinary team that includes an NP, RT's, nurses, geriatric ED nurses, a sexual assault program and crisis intervention workers . Our department sees an average of 120 patients per day, in a fast paced environment. We are a regional stroke referral center, a level III trauma center and have a large catchment area of smaller surrounding communities. We have onsite CT and MRI imaging modalities. Our team is well supported by local specialists including ortho, ENT, urology, pediatrics, general surgery, anesthesia, obstetrics & gynecology, psychiatry, GIM, nephrology, endocrinology, GI, respirology, and visiting rheumatology. The organization is affiliated with the NOSM University which provides various opportunities for teaching and mentorship. Community Information: Situated roughly equal distances from Toronto and Ottawa, we really are "just north enough to be perfect." Our population of 52,000 boasts that our city is the perfect mix of opportunity and lifestyle. Located between beautiful Lake Nipissing and Trout Lake, North Bay provides residents and visitors alike with countless recreational opportunities. Join us for a locum and experience the beauty of Northern Ontario while you are here! Hospital Information: Circa 2011, NBRHC is a 480 bed facility that houses our well organized 41 bed ED with 2 trauma bays, 4 bed acute care room, easy access imaging and level 1 trauma infusers. We are also the regional center for psychiatric care of Northeastern Ontario and have well established inpatient and outpatient psychiatric programs. For information about the NBRHC, please view www.nbrhc.on.ca and https://vimeo.com/106279645 Qualifications: CPSO Independent license to practice Remuneration: Our locums are well remunerated with earnings including: $161-$195 hourly rate (depending on shift type) Incentive top up Shadow OHIP billings Hospital parking is provided A paid four hour orientation is required before the start of a locum's first shift with NBRHC Locums are NSLP Respite + funded: Travel & accommodation expenses are reimbursed in line with NSLP guidelines Daily honourarium of $386 for clinical days Travel sessionals in line with NSLP guidelines Travel honorarium of $386 for locum travel days to/from the community Contact: Interested candidates are asked to contact Chastity Saudino, Medical Affairs Manager, at physicianrecruitment@nbrhc.on.ca Check out our website for more details about this great department and team at www.northbayemerg.ca or find us on Instagram @northbayemer

jobs.title: Emergency Medicine Physicians
jobs.full_description_text: The North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) Department of Emergency Medicine is seeking physicians to join its high performance team! About Us: We are a collegial group of CCFP, CCFP-EM and FRCP trained physicians with a wide variety of professional and personal interests. Our department sees on average 120 patients per day in a fast paced environment. We area regional stroke referral center, a level III trauma center and have a large catchment area of smaller surrounding communities. Our ED is supported by Health Science North, our nearest Teritary Care Center, just over an hour away. Our workload is broken into 7 shifts per day, typically with double or triple physician coverage. Our team is well supported by specialists including ortho, surgery, ENT, urology, pediatrics, anesthesia, obstetrics and internal medicine and its subspecialties. We have onsite CT and MRI imaging modalities. As a group we regularly participate in CME with an excellent SIM program and high fidelity SIM lab, monthly accredited Grand Rounds and case reviews. Our work is supported by an excellent group of nurses, RT’s, geriatric EM nurses, sexual assault program and crisis workers. The organization is affiliated with NOSM University which provides various opportunities for teaching and mentorship. ED physicians are remunerated through a Alternate Funding Plan (AFA) with a rewarding financial structure. Mentorship opportunities for new hires exist both formally through the MOHLTC and informally within our group. Check out our website for more details about this great department and team at www.northbayemerg.ca or find us on Instagram @northbay.emerg Community Information: We truly feel that we live in an amazing community. Situated roughly equal distances from Toronto and Ottawa, we really are “just north enough to be perfect”. In our downtime you can find us skiing, trail running, paddling, fishing, mountain biking, or just putting our feet up by the lake. Our population of 52,000 boasts that our city is the perfect mix of opportunity and lifestyle. Situated between beautiful Lake Nipissing and Trout Lake, North Bay provides residents and visitors alike with countless recreational opportunities, while larger city amenities and a low crime rate contribute to safe, but bustling communities. Hospital Information: NBRHC is a state of the art regional center with a catchment area of 180,000 residents with strong inpatient and outpatient programs to support them. Circa 2011, this newly built 480 bed facility houses our well organized 41 bed ED with 2 trauma bays, 4 bed acute care room, easy to access imaging, Level 1 trauma infusers and established mass casualty and massive hemorrhage protocols. We are also the regional center for psychiatric care in Northeastern Ontario and have well established inpatient and outpatient psychiatric programs. For further information about the NBRHC please view www.nbrhc.on.ca and https://vimeo.com/106279645 Qualifications: CPSO Independent license to practice (CCFP-EM, FRCPC EM or CCFP with emergency medicine experience) Remuneration: Physicians are competitively remunerated. Travel and accommodation expenses are provided for locums. NBRHC offers a Recruitment Incentive Package which includes: $25,000 recruitment incentive $25,000 practice start-up grant Assistance with moving expenses $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment and Retention Initiative (NRRRI) $87,000 (over two years) with the Ontario Health ER Recruitment Program Contact: For additional information on practice opportunities with NBRHC, please contact Chastity Saudino, Medical Affairs Manager at physicianrecruitment@nbrhc.on.ca .
