We area regional stroke referral center, a level III trauma center and have a large catchment area of smaller surrounding communities. Our ED is supported by Health Science North, our nearest Teritary Care Center, just over an hour away. Our workload is broken into 7 shifts per day, typically with double or triple physician coverage. Our team is well supported by specialists including ortho, surgery, ENT, urology, pediatrics, anesthesia, obstetrics and internal medicine and its subspecialties. We have onsite CT and MRI imaging modalities. As a group we regularly participate in CME with an excellent SIM program and high fidelity SIM lab, monthly accredited Grand Rounds and case reviews. Our work is supported by an excellent group of nurses, RT’s, geriatric EM nurses, sexual assault program and crisis workers. The organization is affiliated with NOSM University which provides various opportunities for teaching and mentorship. ED physicians are remunerated through a Alternate Funding Plan (AFA) with a rewarding financial structure. Mentorship opportunities for new hires exist both formally through the MOHLTC and informally within our group. Check out our website for more details about this great department and team at www.northbayemerg.ca or find us on Instagram @northbay.emerg Community Information: We truly feel that we live in an amazing community. Situated roughly equal distances from Toronto and Ottawa, we really are “just north enough to be perfect”. In our downtime you can find us skiing, trail running, paddling, fishing, mountain biking, or just putting our feet up by the lake. Our population of 52,000 boasts that our city is the perfect mix of opportunity and lifestyle. Situated between beautiful Lake Nipissing and Trout Lake, North Bay provides residents and visitors alike with countless recreational opportunities, while larger city amenities and a low crime rate contribute to safe, but bustling communities. Hospital Information: NBRHC is a state of the art regional center with a catchment area of 180,000 residents with strong inpatient and outpatient programs to support them. Circa 2011, this newly built 480 bed facility houses our well organized 41 bed ED with 2 trauma bays, 4 bed acute care room, easy to access imaging, Level 1 trauma infusers and established mass casualty and massive hemorrhage protocols. We are also the regional center for psychiatric care in Northeastern Ontario and have well established inpatient and outpatient psychiatric programs. For further information about the NBRHC please view www.nbrhc.on.ca and https://vimeo.com/106279645 Qualifications: CPSO Independent license to practice (CCFP-EM, FRCPC EM or CCFP with emergency medicine experience) Remuneration: Physicians are competitively remunerated. Travel and accommodation expenses are provided for locums. NBRHC offers a Recruitment Incentive Package which includes: $25,000 recruitment incentive $25,000 practice start-up grant Assistance with moving expenses $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment and Retention Initiative (NRRRI) $87,000 (over two years) with the Ontario Health ER Recruitment Program Contact: For additional information on practice opportunities with NBRHC, please contact Chastity Saudino, Medical Affairs Manager at physicianrecruitment@nbrhc.on.ca .

jobs.title: Full Time Anaesthesiologist (FRCPC or GPA)
jobs.full_description_text: The Service of Anaesthesia at North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) is seeking full-time Anaesthesiologists to join its collaborative and growing team. This is an excellent opportunity to practice in a modern regional referral centre while enjoying the lifestyle benefits of Northern Ontario. Physicians will work alongside an experienced and supportive group of colleagues, providing comprehensive perioperative care and participating in shared daytime and on-call coverage within a collegial environment that values high-quality patient care, teamwork, and professional collaboration. Service Details: NBRHC Anaesthesiologists provide services to General Surgery, Orthopedic Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Otolaryngology, Urology, Ophthalmology, Dental Surgery, Pain Management, ECT, the Preadmission Clinic and support the Critical Care Unit team when needed. NBRHC has an 8 theatre OR, a 13 bed PACU, endoscopy suite, ophthalmology suite, labour & delivery suite. The service also provides consultative support for vented patients in the critical care unit. Hospital Information: NBRHC is a modern, state-of-the-art healthcare facility that opened in 2011 and serves as a key regional referral center for Northeastern Ontario. With 480 beds, NBRHC provides a full spectrum of acute care and specialized services to a catchment population extending across North Bay and surrounding communities including Mattawa, West Nipissing and Temiskaming Shores. The hospital offers comprehensive acute care services, including a 24/7 emergency department, 16 bed Critical Care Unit, inpatient adult and pediatric medicine, dialysis, endoscopy and bronchoscopy, obstetrics, pathology and surgical subspecialties. NBRHC also provides advances diagnostic imaging services, including x-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI, bone densitometry and nuclear medicine, supporting timely and high-quality diagnostic care for the region. NBRHC is unique in Ontario for its fully integrated model of care, combining acute care services and specialzed mental health services on one campus. The organization fulfills three important roles: Providing acute care services to North Bay and surrounding communities Serving as the district referral center providing specialist services for smaller communities across the region Delivering specialized mental health services for the entire Northeast region of Ontario. This integrated system allows NBRHC to provide coordinated, patient-centered care while supporting strong collaboration among medical specialists and healthcare teams. Additional information about the hospital and physician opportunities can be found at northbaydoctors.ca Community Information: Often referred to as Ontario’s Gateway to the North, the community of North Bay offers an exceptional balance of professional opportunity and quality of life. With a population of approximately 54,000, North Bay is a safe, welcoming city situated about 3.5 hours from both Toronto and Ottawa. Surrounded by beautiful natural landscapes, including the shores of Lake Nipissing, the city offers four distinct seasons of outdoor recreation such as boating, skiing, hiking, and cycling. North Bay features a diverse and growing economy, excellent schools, and a vibrant community atmosphere, making it an ideal place to build a rewarding medical career while enjoying a healthy and balanced lifestyle. Qualifications: Qualified applicants will have licensure to practice independently in Ontario, and either a standing anaesthesiology fellowship from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada or Family Medicine CCFP designation with a certificate of added competence in anaesthesia. Proficiency and experience with community pediatric anaesthesia is required. Remuneration: This position will be remunerated with a combination of OHIP billings, Northern Specialist APP & Hospital On-Call stipends. Our organization has a competitive Incentive Package which includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, $25,000 practice start-up grant, assistance with moving expenses and up to $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment & Retention Initiative (NRRRI)

jobs.full_description_text: Join a dynamic team of ophthalmologists at North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) as a Comprehensive Ophthalmologist in the beautiful community of North Bay, Ontario. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a collegial, patient-focused environment while enjoying exceptional work-life balance. Key Responsibilities: Perform cataract surgery with dedicated surgical time, including 1-2 operating days per week at NBRHC Participate in minor procedure ORs at the hospital Practice in a state-of-the-art medical clinic opened in 2025, featuring 6 ophthalmic lanes and a comprehensive clinical support team Embrace a team-based approach to patient care in a collaborative environment Provide 1 in 4 call coverage for the community and the surrounding area What We Offer: Dedicated operating room access at NBRHC for cataract surgery and minor procedures Opportunity to practice in a brand new clinic equipped with advance technology and designed to support future growth Support from a skilled and welcoming team of technicians, medical office administrators, and healthcare professionals Strong mentorship to new graduates seeking to establish their careers, within a supportive team of ophthalmologists dedicated to facilitating a smooth and confident transition into practice Excellent work-life balance with the flexibility to build a practice aligned with your professional interests Access to North Bay's natural beauty, including 2 lakes, 46 scenic trails, a ski-hill, and abundant year-round outdoor recreation opportunities Qualifications & Requirements: Ophthalmology certification from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada with a strong interest in comprehensive care and a variety of subspecialities Licensure with CPSO to practice ophthalmology independently in Ontario Ability to work collaboratively in a dynamic, patient centered team A passion for providing high-quality care with a focus on improving patient outcomes Remuneration: This position will be remunerated with a combination of OHIP billings, Northern Specialist APP & Hospital On-Call stipends. Our organization has a competitive Incentive Package which includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, $25,000 practice start-up grant, assistance with moving expenses and up to $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment & Retention Initiative (NRRRI). jobs.title: Pathologist (General or Anatomical)
jobs.full_description_text: The North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) Department of Laboratory Medicine is seeking a full-time Pathologist to join its collegial and well-established team of four pathologists. The successful candidate will contribute to a broad range of diagnostic services including general surgical pathology, gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytology, hematology, transfusion medicine, clinical chemistry, and microbiology. NBRHC pathologists are also actively engaged in a comprehensive Quality Assurance and quality improvement program, supporting high standards of diagnostic excellence and patient care. This is an excellent opportunity to practice in a modern health care centre serving Northeastern Ontario while enjoying the exceptional lifestyle and recreational opportunities of Northern Ontario. Hospital & Service Information: North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) is a modern, state-of-the-art healthcare facility that opened in 2011 and serves as a key regional referral centre for Northeastern Ontario. With 480 beds, NBRHC provides a broad range of acute care and specialized services to a catchment population that includes North Bay and surrounding communities across the Nipissing District. The Department of Laboratory Medicine provides comprehensive diagnostic laboratory services in support of inpatient care and hospital-based outpatient programs across the organization. The laboratory includes a Core Laboratory (hematology, clinical biochemistry, and transfusion medicine) as well as microbiology, histopathology, and cytology services, supported by centralized specimen procurement, phlebotomy, and central receiving. The laboratory delivers timely diagnostic testing for acute care, critical care, surgical, medical, and specialty programs, with 24/7 coverage for critical testing and rapid turnaround for routine investigations. Most testing is performed on-site, with access to specialized reference laboratories for complex or highly specialized assays. Working in close collaboration with clinical teams across the hospital, the laboratory supports patient care for a regional population throughout Nipissing District and surrounding Northern Ontario communities, providing high-quality diagnostic services essential to emergency medicine, oncology, renal, surgical, inpatient, and ambulatory programs. Community Information: Often referred to as Ontario’s Gateway to the North, the community of North Bay offers an exceptional balance of professional opportunity and quality of life. With a population of approximately 54,000, North Bay is a safe, welcoming city situated about 3.5 hours from Toronto and 4.5 hours from Ottawa. Surrounded by beautiful natural landscapes, including the shores of Lake Nipissing and Trout Lake, the city offers four distinct seasons and abundant opportunities for outdoor recreation such as boating, fishing, skiing, hiking and cycling. North Bay also features a diverse and growing economy, excellent schools, and a vibrant arts and cultural scene. Combining the amenities of a mid-sized city with the charm and accessibility of Northern Ontario, North Bay provides an ideal environment to build a rewarding medical career while enjoying a healthy, balanced lifestyle. Additional information about the Hospital and City of North Bay can be found at northbaydoctors.ca Qualifications Licensure with the CPSO to practice pathology independently in Ontario A fellowship from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada in General Pathology or in Anatomical Pathology with extra training and/or experience in 1 or more of the clinical areas Remuneration This position will be remunerated in line with the NBRHC Pathology service agreement, including monthly stipends and OHIP billings, as well as Hospital On-Call stipends. Our organization has a competitive Incentive Package, which includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, $25,000 practice start-up grant, assistance with moving expenses and up to $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment & Retention Initiative (NRRRI) To Apply: Interested candidates should contact Chastity Saudino, NBRHC Medical Affairs Manager, with an expression of interest and their CV at physicianrecruitment@nbrhc.on.ca

jobs.title: Level III Echocardiographer (Remote Echocardiography Reporting)
jobs.full_description_text: North Bay Cardiology is seeking an experienced Level III Echocardiographer / Cardiologist with expertise in echocardiography to join our growing regional cardiovascular program providing remote echocardiography interpretation. This is an ideal opportunity for physicians seeking a highly flexible role that can be performed remotely while contributing to the delivery of high-quality cardiovascular care in Northern Ontario. About North Bay Cardiology North Bay Cardiology is a comprehensive regional cardiovascular practice serving North Bay and communities across Northeastern Ontario. Since opening in 2022, the practice has rapidly expanded and now provides: Accreditation Canada accredited echocardiography laboratory Contrast-enhanced echocardiography Large ambulatory rhythm monitoring program Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) Exercise stress testing Regional heart failure program Rapid access chest pain clinic Multidisciplinary cardiac rehabilitation program developed in collaboration with the University Health Network (UHN) Active participation in cardiovascular quality improvement initiatives Our echocardiography laboratory performs a large and growing volume of outpatient studies, creating an opportunity for experienced echocardiographers to join our reporting team. Position The successful candidate will provide remote interpretation of transthoracic echocardiograms performed in our Accreditation Canada accredited laboratory. This position offers exceptional flexibility and may be ideal for physicians wishing to supplement an existing practice, reduce clinical workload while remaining professionally active, or transition toward a more flexible work schedule. The successful candidate could also contribute to the offices continuing education with once monthly virtual rounds. Reporting volumes can be tailored to individual preference. Examples include: 10–20 studies per week 20–40 studies per week There are no clinic responsibilities, hospital call requirements, or administrative responsibilities associated with this position. What We Offer Fully remote reporting from anywhere in Ontario Flexible scheduling and reporting volumes Competitive per-study compensation Modern digital reporting platform with secure remote access (cerebrum) Excellent administrative and technical support Accreditation Canada accredited echocardiography laboratory Opportunity to participate in quality improvement and laboratory development Collegial and collaborative working environment Qualifications Applicants should possess: Certification in Cardiology with expertise in echocardiography Level III training in adult echocardiography (or equivalent experience) Eligibility for independent practice in Ontario Excellent communication skills Commitment to high-quality, evidence-based echocardiography About North Bay Cardiology Founded by Dr. Jari Tuomi , North Bay Cardiology has developed into one of Northern Ontario's most comprehensive community cardiovascular programs, providing advanced diagnostics, heart failure management, ambulatory rhythm monitoring, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and multidisciplinary cardiac rehabilitation. Our goal is to improve access to high-quality cardiovascular care through innovation, quality improvement, and collaborative models of care. As our echocardiography service continues to grow, we are seeking experienced colleagues who share a commitment to quality and timely patient care. Interested candidates are encouraged to contact: Dr. Jari Tuomi, MD, PhD, FRCPC Founder & CEO North Bay Cardiology Email: jarituomi@northbaycardiology.ca Website: www.northbaycardiology.ca

jobs.title: Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist
jobs.full_description_text: Position Description Serving the Districts of Nipissing, Temiskaming and Muskoka and the broader North East region, the NBRHC Service of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry is seeking a Psychiatrist to join its team to provide inpatient and outpatient/outreach intervention to youth with severe mental illness. Working to full scope of practice, the incumbent will apply clinical leadership and expertise in the assessment, treatment, and/or consultation for inpatient and community-based care. Our inpatient service includes a Child & Adolescent Mental Health Unit (6-beds) servings individuals under the age of 18 who require acute short term stabilization and/or longer term treatment. The interdisciplinary team works collaboratively with community partners to provide comprehensive assessment, intervention and transitional supports Our outpatient/outreach services support youth and their families in the community, providing early intervention, and assists in the prevention of hospitalization where possible. Consultation is also provided to specialized outpatient services such as the eating disorders program and the gender diversity clinic. The service also provides specialized consultations, inter-sectoral capacity building and knowledge exchange across the North East. The successful candidate will be expected to participate in the Department of Psychiatry hospital on-call rota along with consult liaison services to the medical units of the organization. In addition, there are opportunities to join the faculty of NOSM University and engage in clinical teaching at the undergraduate and postgraduate level. Hospital Information: North Bay Regional Health Centre (NBRHC) is a unique health care organization with three primary roles: providing acute care services to North Bay and its surrounding communities, functioning as the district referral center providing specialist services for smaller communities in the area, and it is the specialized mental health service provider serving all of northeast Ontario. NBRHC is a 480 bed hospital with acute care services including a 24/7 emergency department, 8 theatre OR, 13 bed PACU, endoscopy suite, ophthalmology suite, labour & delivery suite and a 16 bed CCU. Community Information: North Bay is located 3.5 hours north of Toronto, just down the four-lane highway from the Muskokas, and 3.5 hours west of Ottawa. With a population of 54,000 within a regional catchment area serving 557,000, it is a safe and welcoming community that offers a healthy and balanced environment for working, living and raising a family. North Bay is situated on the banks of two large lakes and boasts beautiful scenery and four distinct seasons. Whatever your interests are, you will have access to numerous activities and amenities within minutes of home – reclaim your work-life balance and join us! For further information about North Bay Regional Health Centre and/or the City of North Bay please visit NorthBayDoctors.ca Qualifications: Applicants require certification in Child & Adolescent Psychiatry by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada and must be independently licensed to practice Psychiatry in Ontario by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario (CPSO). NBRHC also welcomes interest from residents in their final year of specialty training. Remuneration: This position will be remunerated with a competitive monthly clinical stipend with opportunities for additional OHIP billing income, Northern Specialist APP, Hospital On-Call Compensation (HOCC) stipends and teaching stipends. The hospital has a competitive physician recruitment incentive package which includes a $25,000 recruitment stipend, $25,000 practice start-up grant, assistance with relocation expenses and up to $94,000 through the Northern Rural Recruitment & Retention Initiative (NRRRI).

jobs.title: Regional Cardiology Outreach Opportunities: EP, CHF, Rehab, CPET, Echo
jobs.full_description_text: Regional Cardiology Outreach Opportunities Cardiac Electrophysiology • Heart Failure • Cardiac Rehabilitation • Preventive Cardiology • Cardiac Imaging North Bay Cardiology – Hybrid Outreach Practice North Bay Cardiology is seeking cardiologists with subspecialty expertise who are interested in helping improve access to cardiovascular care across Northern Ontario (North Bay and Nipissing Region) through an innovative collaborative hybrid outreach practice. This opportunity is ideal for physicians who wish to maintain their primary practice in a larger academic or tertiary centre while developing a rewarding regional outreach practice combining periodic in-person clinics with virtual care and remote diagnostic interpretation. Rather than relocating, physicians can contribute to the development of specialized regional cardiovascular programs while maintaining flexibility and work-life balance. The new Ontario North Lander train allows direct links between downtown Toronto and North Bay. ABOUT NORTH BAY CARDIOLOGY North Bay Cardiology has rapidly grown into one of Northern Ontario's most comprehensive community cardiovascular centres. Our practice includes: Accreditation Canada Accredited Echocardiography Laboratory Contrast-enhanced echocardiography and advanced imaging technologies Large regional ambulatory rhythm monitoring program Exercise stress testing Advanced Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), performed with a new Vyntus CPX metabolic cart Regional Heart Failure Program Comprehensive multidisciplinary Cardiac Rehabilitation Program developed in collaboration with the University Health Network (UHN) Active cardiovascular quality improvement and clinical research initiatives The practice serves a large regional referral population across Northeastern Ontario with significant unmet demand for cardiovascular subspecialty services. OUTREACH SUBSPECIALTY OPPORTUNITIES Cardiac Electrophysiology Help develop a regional atrial fibrillation and electrophysiology program. Clinical opportunities include: Comprehensive atrial fibrillation assessment Ablation referral pathways Antiarrhythmic medication management Interpretation of ambulatory rhythm monitoring Hybrid in-person and virtual follow-up clinics Physicians may combine one or two outreach clinic days per month with remote Holter/echo interpretation and virtual follow-up appointments. Heart Failure North Bay has a rapidly expanding population of patients with: HFrEF HFnrEF Complex heart failure requiring longitudinal management Physicians may participate in: Monthly multidisciplinary heart failure clinics Guideline-directed medical therapy optimization Virtual longitudinal follow-up Interpretation of echocardiography ECG interpretation Holter interpretation CPET interpretation Collaborative care model with local provider (Dr Jari Tuomi) Cardiac Rehabilitation & Preventive Cardiology Our comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation program offers opportunities for physicians interested in: Exercise medicine Secondary prevention Cardiometabolic medicine CPET interpretation Rehabilitation consultation Virtual rehabilitation follow-up Rehabilitation discharge assessment Exercise prescription Our 16 week Comprehensive cardiac rehab program was developed in collaboration with UHN rehab and is supported by the North Bay Cardiac Rehabilitation Foundation. Website: www.nbcr-foundation.ca ( Home - North Bay Cardiac Rehabilitation Foundation ). Physicians can combine periodic in-person rehabilitation clinics with remote/inperson CPET interpretation and virtual patient follow-up. Cardiac Imaging Opportunities are also available for physicians interested in: Remote Echocardiography interpretation Quality assurance Educational initiatives FLEXIBLE HYBRID PRACTICE Physicians may customize their level of participation. Examples include: One or two in-person clinic days per month Virtual follow-up clinics Remote echocardiography reporting Remote Holter reporting Remote CPET interpretation Participation in multidisciplinary case conferences Collaborative management with local cardiology services The model is designed to minimize travel while maximizing patient access to specialized cardiovascular care. WHY PARTICIPATE? This outreach model allows physicians to: Maintain a primary academic or tertiary-care practice. Develop a regional outreach subspecialty practice without relocating. Improve access to cardiovascular care for underserved communities. Participate in innovative hybrid models of care. Collaborate with an experienced multidisciplinary cardiovascular team. Contribute to education, quality improvement, and clinical research. For physicians with academic appointments, opportunities may also exist to participate in trainee education, quality improvement, implementation science, and collaborative research focused on regional and remote cardiovascular care. North Bay Cardiology is also interested in hosting cardiovascular trainee's with the ability to arrange an elective through NOSM. HELP BUILD THE FUTURE OF REGIONAL CARDIOLOGY Our vision is to create a sustainable regional cardiovascular network where specialized expertise can be delivered closer to home through thoughtful integration of outreach clinics, virtual care, remote diagnostics, and collaborative multidisciplinary practice. If you are passionate about expanding access to high-quality cardiovascular care while maintaining your existing practice, we would welcome the opportunity to discuss how your expertise could become part of this growing regional program. Interested? If this opportunity intrigues you, I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how we might collaborate to improve access to cardiovascular care across North Eastern Ontario. Whether your interests include electrophysiology, heart failure, cardiac rehabilitation, preventive cardiology, cardiac imaging, ambulatory rhythm monitoring, or other areas of cardiovascular medicine, we are happy to explore flexible practice models that complement your existing academic or community practice. We recognize that every physician's career goals are unique. Together, we can develop an outreach model that aligns with your professional interests while helping bring specialized cardiovascular care closer to home for patients living in underserved communities. For a confidential discussion, please contact: Dr. Jari Tuomi, MD, PhD, FRCPC email: jarituomi@northbaycardiology.ca Founder & CEO, North Bay Cardiology Medical Director North Bay Cardiac Rehabilitation program Medical Director North Bay Cardiology Echo lab Chair- North Bay Cardiac Rehabilitation Foundation Website: www.northbaycardiology.ca

jobs.title: Medical Director and/or Attending Physicians - Long Term Care
jobs.full_description_text: Medical Director &/or Attending Physicians, Long Term Care, North Bay, ON At Sienna Senior Living, quality and safety of resident care are our top priorities, and we are proud of the excellent results in our long-term care and residential care communities. We are one of Canada’s largest owners and operators of over 100 owned and managed seniors’ living residences. Our portfolio includes locations across Ontario, British Columbia and Saskatchewan. We are working with Dr. Hugh Boyd, Sienna’s Chief Medical Officer, to strengthen the medical services model in our Care Communities and are currently recruiting for a medical director and attending physicians at: Northern Heights Community 720 McLaren St. North Bay ON, P1B 3L8 Overview of Position: Reporting to Executive Director and the Chief Medical Officer, the Medical Director will work closely with the clinical leadership team at the Care Community to direct the medical services program. Features: Warm and vibrant 160 bed facility in North Bay, Ontario Weekly in-house labs In house BSO Lead Responsibilities: Provides advice and leadership on the medical services program Regularly communicates with the medical staff regarding relevant policies, procedures and responsibilities as attending physicians Ensures appropriate on-call coverage has been arranged for all residents, after hours, in accordance with LTC on-call program as established between the MOLTC and the Ontario Medical Association Participates in quality improvement activities in collaboration with the Care Community and interdisciplinary team Willing to provide clinical care as one of the attending physicians at the Care Community Develop quality of care standards in conjunction with the Care Community and interdisciplinary team Attends the Care Community weekly in the provision of clinical care to assigned residents Addresses resident acute and chronic care needs and provides appropriate and timely documentation Identifies circumstances in which palliative and/or end of life care may benefit the resident and family members Collaborate effectively and efficiently with members of the interdisciplinary team including the medical director to ensure the highest level of care is provided to residents Conducts regular medication drug review and documents/updates resident’s health record Participates in after hours on-call along with other attending physicians at the facility Commits to continuing education related to long term care, care of the elderly and palliative care Qualifications: Medical practitioner licensed to practice medicine in the Province of Ontario and at all times be a member in good standing of the Colleges of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario Experience working in Long Term Care or as a Medical Director preferred, with a willingness to enrol in the Ontario LTC Medical Director Curriculum within 12 months of starting as a Medical Director Ability to build trust, adapt, provide coaching, facilitate change and continually improve resident care Strong skills in communication and interprofessional collaboration Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team Ability to build trust and interact in a professional manner with staff, residents, families and other community partners

jobs.title: INFECTIOUS DISEASE SPECIALIST
jobs.full_description_text: Infectious Diseases Practice Opportunities Join Northeastern Ontario’s health care leader Health Sciences North/Horizon Santé-Nord ( HSN ) is recruiting health care professionals who have a keen interest in affecting change within its dynamic health care system. As the tertiary care referral centre for the entire Northeastern Ontario region, HSN serves a catchment population of over 600,000 residents. HSN is seeking energetic and dedicated Adult Infectious Diseases physicians to establish broad scope ID practices. Successful candidates will provide both hospital based and community consultative and concurrent care services for patients with a broad array of infectious diseases including a fully supported HIV clinic. ID physicians are contributing members of the Department of Medicine and provide clinical teaching to core Internal Medicine residency through the NOSM University Residency Training Program. Why choose HSN? ¨ Vast scope and broad spectrum of cases ¨ Dynamic team of over 600 credentialed medical staff ¨ Greater Sudbury is a natural paradise with activities to enjoy all year-round ¨ Attractive financial incentives for full-time practicing physicians Candidates must be eligible for licensure in Ontario and have obtained or be eligible to obtain speciality qualifications from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. The successful applicant will be expected to obtain academic appointment with the Northern Ontario School of Medicine University ( NOSM-U ) and sup port the academic mandate of the Department of Medicine. Research opportunities are also available through the Health Sciences North Research Institute ( HSNRI). If you are currently practicing or within one year of graduating, and are interested in opportunities in Sudbury, the Ministry of Health’s Community Assessment Visit Program will cover travel and accommodation expenses for both you and your spouse to come explore our practice opportunity and the City of Greater Sudbury. Come discover Sudbury’s exceptional quality of life, abundant lakes, parklands and extensive recreational opportunities! Sudbury is a bilingual and multicultural community, and offers a variety of excellent elementary, secondary, and post-secondary education institutions. Physicians who practice full –time in Sudbury are eligible for attractive financial incentives. Interested individuals should send a letter of interest and CV to the Medical Affairs office by e-mail to medcareers@hsnsudbury.ca . HSN thanks all applicants, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Pediatric Intensivist
jobs.full_description_text: Pediatric Intensivist Practice Opportunity Join Northeastern Ontario’s healthcare leader Health Sciences North/Horizon Santé-Nord (HSN) is recruiting health care professionals who have a keen interest in affecting change within its dynamic health care system. As the tertiary care referral centre for the entire Northeastern Ontario region, HSN serves a catchment population of over 600,000 residents. Are you passionate about providing exceptional care to critically ill children? Do you thrive in a collaborative environment focused on excellence and innovation? We have the perfect opportunity for you. The Department of Pediatrics is actively seeking a Royal College certified Pediatric Intensivist to join our team at the Northeastern Ontario Health Centre for Kids (NEO Kids) . NEO Kids became a vital part of HSN in 2014 and is home to over 20 specialized outpatient clinics and services. NEO Kids is Northeastern Ontario’s hub for specialized children’s care, comprising of Pediatricians and other allied health care professionals dedicated to providing the highest quality patient care to pediatric patients in Northeastern Ontario. The NEO Kids Foundation (NKF) was launched in November 2015, with a mission to advocate for healthier children in the North, raising funds for children’s services, equipment and research at HSN. The Department’s current complement of 10 Pediatricians staff regional programs in diabetes, cystic fibrosis, Autism testing, spasticity, neonatal follow-up, and oncology. As a Pediatric Intensivist, you will play a key role in the management and treatment of critically ill children in our Pediatric Critical Care Unit (PCCU). You will work closely with a multidisciplinary team to deliver comprehensive care to our young patients. jobs.full_description_text: Respirology & Sleep Medicine Practice Opportunities Practice Opportunities Join Northeastern Ontario’s health care leader Health Sciences North/Horizon Santé-Nord ( HSN ) is recruiting health care professionals who have a keen interest in affecting change within its dynamic health care system. As the tertiary care referral centre for the entire Northeastern Ontario region, HSN serves a catchment population of over 600,000 residents. The Department of Medicine is currently recruiting 4 Respirologists and/or Sleep Medicine Specialists to join 2 existing Respirologists. This unique practice opportunity allows for flexibility to focus on or combine general respirology and sleep medicine to provide pulmonary care and consultative services to the City of Greater Sudbury and Northeastern Ontario. jobs.title: Permanent Full-Time Radiologist Practice Opportunities
jobs.full_description_text: Radiology Practice Opportunities Join Northeastern Ontario’s healthcare leader Health Sciences North ( HSN ) is recruiting health care professionals who have a keen interest in affecting change within its dynamic health care system. As the tertiary care referral centre for the entire Northeastern Ontario region, HSN serves a catchment population of over 600,000 residents. The Department of Medical Imaging at Health Sciences North is currently recruiting Radiologists with Women’s Imaging Fellowship training, Body Imaging Fellowship training, Diagnostic Neuroradiology training and/or training in Musculoskeletal Imaging. The Department offers flexibility in scheduling, a medically diverse environment, and an opportunity for great personal and professional growth. The Medical Imaging Department at HSN utilizes state-of-the-art technology to perform a wide range of diagnostic and interventional procedures. The department operates two GE Revolution CT scanners (installed in 2018 and 2024) and two MRI scanners—a 1.5T GE Signa system (upgraded in February 2022) and a 3T Siemens Vida system (installed in September 2021). Each year, the department performs approximately 38,000 ultrasound exams, 55,000 CT exams, and 18,000 MRI exams, providing timely imaging access for patients across Northeastern Ontario—closer to home. The majority of studies focus on body imaging, with neuroradiology comprising roughly 15,000 brain, head & neck, and spine CTs and 10,000 MRIs annually. Our musculoskeletal (MSK) practice includes about 4,000 MRIs each year, along with interventional procedures such as MR arthrograms. HSN also serves as a tertiary breast screening centre, offering a comprehensive high-risk breast screening program, diagnostic assessments, and more than 15,000 digital screening and diagnostic mammograms annually. As an Ontario Breast Screening Program (OBSP) High-Risk site, HSN performs approximately 200 breast MRIs per year, along with 100 stereotactic and over 300 ultrasound-guided core biopsies annually. In addition, HSN is the regional referral centre for gynecologic and obstetric imaging for the North East LHIN, with a growing volume of pelvic MRI studies. The women’s imaging MRI program continues to expand, supported by the installation of the new 3T Siemens Vida MRI scanner. Why choose HSN? · Vast scope and broad spectrum of cases · Dynamic team of over 600 credentialed medical staff · Greater Sudbury is a natural paradise with activities to enjoy all year-round · Attractive financial incentives for full-time practicing physicians Candidates must be eligible for licensure in Ontario and have obtained or be eligible to obtain speciality qualifications from the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. Candidates eligible for restricted licensure and/or international applicants will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The successful applicant will be expected to obtain academic appointment with NOSM-University ( NOSM-U ) and support the academic mandate of the Department of Medical Imaging. Research opportunities are also available through the Health Sciences North Research Institute ( HSNRI ). If you are currently practicing or within one year of graduating, and are interested in opportunities in Sudbury, the Ministry of Health’s Community Assessment Visit Program will cover travel and accommodation expenses for both you and your spouse to come explore our practice opportunity and the City of Greater Sudbury. Come discover Sudbury’s exceptional quality of life, abundant lakes, parklands and extensive recreational opportunities! Sudbury is a bilingual and multicultural community, and offers a variety of excellent elementary, secondary, and post-secondary education institutions. Physicians who practice fulltime in Sudbury are eligible for attractive financial incentives. Interested individuals are invited to send a Letter of Interest and CV to The Chief of Medical Imaging, Dr. Heidi Schmidt: hschmidt@hsnsudbury.ca . HSN thanks all applicants, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Full-Time Plastic Surgeon
jobs.full_description_text: Health Sciences North is Recruiting Plastic Surgeons - Full-Time and Locum See full advertisement here: https://hsnsudbury.ca/en/About-Us/For-Physicians Health Sciences North (HSN) is inviting applications for a full-time Plastic Surgeon to join our collegial and expanding team of five Plastic Surgeons serving Northeastern Ontario. Plastic Surgery at Health Sciences North Health Sciences North (HSN) is the largest hospital in Northern Ontario and the tertiary care referral centre for more than 600,000 residents across a vast geographic region. Our Division of Plastic Surgery is an integral part of HSN’s Surgical Program, working in close collaboration with over 75 surgeons across multiple specialties. Plastic surgeons at HSN provide a full spectrum of care, including reconstructive, hand, craniofacial, trauma, and cancer-related procedures, supported by a strong multidisciplinary network of anesthesiologists, intensivists, perioperative nurses, and allied health professionals. Surgeons also benefit from the hospital’s comprehensive cancer program, which supports complex oncologic reconstructions for breast, head & neck, and skin cancers. Program Highlights: 17 fully equipped operating rooms with state-of-the-art technology 16,000+ operative procedures annually across a wide range of subspecialties Comprehensive perioperative services, including a Level III Intensive Care Unit and dedicated surgical inpatient/outpatient units Regional cancer centre with integrated multidisciplinary teams supporting advanced oncologic reconstructions Trauma centre designation, offering exposure to complex trauma and microsurgery cases Academic affiliation with NOSM University, with opportunities for clinical teaching, mentorship, and collaborative research through the Health Sciences North Research Institute (HSNRI) Requirements: Specialty certification in Plastic Surgery and eligibility for licensure with the CPSO. Maintain a faculty appointment with NOSM-University and contribute to the academic mandate of the Service of Plastic Surgery Why Sudbury? Located in the heart of Northeastern Ontario, Sudbury offers a unique mix of urban amenities and natural beauty, with over 330 lakes, a thriving arts and culture scene, affordable living, and easy access to outdoor activities yearround. Whether you’re raising a family, seeking a close-knit medical community, or looking to strike a better worklife balance, Sudbury has it all. Physicians practicing full-time in Sudbury are eligible for attractive recruitment incentives.
